candidates.title: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human–Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication
candidates.abstract: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time-frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human-machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled "Feeding Frenzy" interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation.

candidates.title: A scoping review of trust in firsthand and secondhand communication involving humans and artificial intelligence
candidates.abstract: Conversational and generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly create and pass information between people. This can make it hard to see who created a claim, whether it was changed, and whom to trust. Many studies examine firsthand human-human and human-AI communication, but less is known about secondhand communication, in which AI or another actor passes on a claim made elsewhere. In these cases, a human decision maker must evaluate the claim and the people or systems that created or passed it on. We present a scoping review built around six minimal motifs that represent firsthand or secondhand communication routes. Humans or AI systems may serve as the source or intermediary, while the decision maker remains human. We screened 3810 records and coded 124 studies to identify 21 trust factors in four dimensions: Decision Maker, Messenger, Message Property, and Environment. Qualitative synthesis also identified four recurring route-level patterns: distorted trust calibration, trust transfer, extremity amplification, and accountability diffusion. These patterns guide future research on AI-mediated communication. Overall, this review provides shared terms and a route-based framework for studying trust in multi-party human-AI communication and designing AI-mediated communication systems.

candidates.title: Robot gaze-timing combinations and the uncanny valley
candidates.abstract: Anthropomorphic robots are increasingly prominent technologies, yet how variations in robot gaze are associated with human perception and visual engagement remain poorly understood. We examined this with a multi-method design spanning three complementary levels: subjective ratings assessed whether an uncanny-valley pattern was present across the tested gaze combinations, individual-difference measures tested moderation effects by personality and attitudes, and eye movements characterized how the robot's face is visually explored. We presented a virtual robot across nine gaze conditions, systematically varying direct-to-averted gaze ratios and durations within a storytelling scenario. Participants ( N = 61) rated each robot's anthropomorphism, likability, and perceived empathy while their eye movements were recorded, and their personality traits and attitudes toward robots were assessed. Results showed that (1) the relationship between perceived anthropomorphism and likability followed an uncanny-valley pattern (a significant cubic relationship), whereas perceived empathy increased monotonically with anthropomorphism; (2) exploratory analyses showed that extraversion and negative attitudes toward robots moderated the relationship between anthropomorphism and likability, while neuroticism moderated the relationship between anthropomorphism and perceived empathy; (3) Eye Movement analysis with Hidden Markov Models (EMHMM) identified two viewing patterns (analytic and holistic) and participants higher in openness viewed the highest-rated robot gaze more analytically and the uncanny robot gaze more holistically. These findings indicate that an uncanny valley pattern was observed across the tested gaze-timing combinations and that individual differences may be associated with variation in robot evaluations and visual attention patterns.

candidates.title: Artificial companions shape embodied desire and human attraction
candidates.abstract: Artificial companions offer a setting in which to examine how responsive technologies may shape embodied desire and human attraction. This theoretical article proposes that repeated interaction with such systems can influence what users come to experience as emotionally available and desirable. Drawing on embodied, embedded, enactive, and extended cognition, it develops an account of artificial companions as affective infrastructures. On this account, conversational memory and adaptive responses may sustain affective looping, through which users come to rely on the system for recognition and emotional regulation. The analysis distinguishes text-based, multimodal, and physically embodied companions, whose different conditions of interaction may affect this process. It also distinguishes interpersonal friction, which such systems may partly reduce, from infrastructural friction arising from technical failures and platform governance. Artificial companions are examined as participants in human meaning-making whose responsiveness can acquire personal significance without establishing lived intentionality on the machine side. The resulting relation is described as asymmetrical or pseudo-enactive coupling. The article thus develops the hypothesis that artificial companions may educate desire by influencing expectations of intimacy. Whether this occurs, how it varies across users, and whether its effects extend to human relationships remain questions for comparative and longitudinal research. This framework contributes to machine cognition by examining the relational environments artificial systems make possible and the limits of their participation in human affective life.

candidates.title: From Accuracy to Responsibility: A Systematic Review of Computational Sustainability, Algorithmic Fairness, and Governance in Transformer-Based Text Classification
candidates.abstract: Background The rapid adoption of Transformer-based architectures such as BERT and RoBERTa has advanced text classification in high-stakes domains, including cyberbullying detection, mental-health screening, and fake-news moderation. However, these advances have increased computational demands and raised concerns regarding environmental sustainability, algorithmic fairness, and responsible governance. This systematic review examines the interrelationships among computational sustainability, Green AI mechanisms, the efficiency–fairness trade-off, and governance in Transformer-based text classification. Methods A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies were identified from five databases: ScienceDirect, Wiley Online Library, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and ProQuest. A total of 94 studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to examine strategies for improving computational efficiency, their implications for fairness, and governance mechanisms relevant to responsible Transformer-based text classification. Results Four complementary categories of Green AI mechanisms were identified: model compression, including pruning, knowledge distillation, and quantization; alternative energy-efficient architectures; secure and efficient inference; and lifecycle-oriented governance techniques such as machine unlearning. Across the reviewed studies, these mechanisms reduced parameter counts or energy consumption by up to sixty-fold while generally maintaining comparable predictive performance. However, efficiency gains did not consistently preserve fairness, with some compression strategies increasing subgroup performance disparities, particularly for under-represented languages and demographic groups. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning demonstrated potential for jointly improving efficiency and equity. Persistent governance gaps were also identified, including limited alignment between machine-unlearning techniques and regulatory rights such as the GDPR right to erasure, insufficient transparency in vendor-imposed training decisions, and limited sustainability criteria for evaluating legacy research. Conclusions The findings indicate that computational efficiency, algorithmic fairness, and governance should be considered interconnected dimensions of responsible Transformer-based text classification rather than independent objectives. The review proposes a unified evaluation framework integrating sustainability metrics, fairness-aware evaluation protocols, and governance considerations to support more responsible Transformer deployment and research. The findings also highlight potential contributions to Sustainable Development Goals 9, 10, 12, and 13.

candidates.title: Baby-schema-related cues shape moral expectations about decision-makers: evidence from names, faces, and AI avatars
candidates.abstract: People routinely form expectations about how others will behave in morally difficult situations, and such expectations guide consequential decisions, including whom to trust, hire, or delegate responsibility to. The present research examined whether baby-schema-related cues systematically bias these moral predictions. Across three experiments with Chinese university students (total N = 858), we tested three manifestations of baby-schema-related cues that share the function of evoking infant-like associations: repeated two-syllable names (Experiment 1), babyfaced appearance (Experiment 2), and visually cute artificial intelligence (AI) avatar designs (Experiment 3). Participants consistently perceived decision-makers displaying baby-schema-related cues as less likely to make utilitarian choices involving direct harm to others. The results show that superficially irrelevant social cues can bias moral expectations about others, although the underlying psychological mechanism remains to be clarified. These findings are relevant to moral psychology, person perception, and the design and evaluation of AI systems.

candidates.title: AI vs. AI: An AI-Enabled Conversational Intervention to Inoculate Against AI-Generated Fake News
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a double-edged sword that can be used to amplify the proliferation of highly sophisticated fake news as well as to fight it. In this work, we explore a new route: using one AI to inoculate humans against fake news generated by another AI. Motivated by psychological inoculation theory, we created ‘Alex’, a conversational AI agent that engages users in an adaptive conversational dialogue designed to build cognitive resilience against AI-generated, AI-related fake news. We tested its efficacy in a Solomon four-group experiment with 542 participants. The results of a 2 × 2 ANOVA show a significant main effect of the intervention on participants’ discrimination of true and false headlines, with no significant evidence of pretest sensitization. We show that AI can be designed as a scalable, interactive conversational intervention for delivering psychological inoculation against AI-generated, AI-related fake news.

candidates.title: Virtual idol consumption among Generation Z: exploring fandom motivations, engagement behavior, and marketing implications
candidates.abstract: Virtual idols have rapidly gained worldwide popularity among young people and have become a significant marketing tool for promoting brands and expanding market reach. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study conducted in-depth interviews to explore motivations, engagement behavior, and consumption patterns underlying Generation Z’s virtual idol fandom. The findings reveal that virtual idol fandom is shaped by both intrinsic and attribute-driven motivations. Within the fandom, engagement with and consumption of virtual idols are driven by overlapping motivational pathways combining emotional involvement, relational control, technology fascination, and community participation. Where community participation is involved, virtual idol fandom extends beyond individual engagement into a socio-technical ecosystem shaped by user agency, platform affordances, and regulatory oversight. At the same time, virtual idol fans seek emotional involvement while pursuing a ‘secure distance’ that preserves psychological boundaries and relational control. This study develops an SDT-informed interpretive framework that reconfigures diverse motivations within contemporary virtual idol fandom. By mapping distinct fan-as-consumer profiles, this study offers practical implications for the scalability of digital persona-led industries and insights for brands seeking to leverage the visibility and influence of virtual idols for targeted promotion among young consumers, enhanced brand value creation, and sustainable expansion in global markets.

candidates.title: A Survey on AI-Based Household Robots Focusing on Voice Assistance, Smart Kitchen Support, Home Monitoring and Autonomous Navigation
candidates.abstract: The proposed system places a Raspberry Pi at the centre, connected to a microphone, speaker, display, camera, ultrasonic sensors, a motor driver and a wheeled base. A conversational AI layer interprets natural-language requests, while obstacle detection, emergency stop and motor time-outs are kept in local safety logic outside the AI loop. Design considerations, a proposed function-to-module mapping, safety logic and an evaluation plan are presented.

candidates.title: Attentional territories: The influence of gaze and interpersonal distance in the navigation of public space
candidates.abstract: Human gaze is a potent social signal; it communicates attention, intention and social engagement, and allows observers to infer not only where others are attending but also how they are socially related. Although gaze has been extensively studied in direct social interaction, far less is known about how it shapes the perceptions and actions of uninvolved observers in shared environments. Here, we investigate whether mutual gaze creates an 'attentional territory' that third parties implicitly respect. In a large-scale field study across four university campuses in Europe and Canada (N = 4680 pedestrians), two confederates stood facing one another in a public space. We manipulated gaze direction and reciprocity (mutual, unilateral or no interaction) as well as interpersonal distance (2-6 metres), holding body orientation and spatial arrangement constant. Pedestrians were less likely to cross between individuals engaged in mutual gaze. This effect weakened with increasing distance, but was robust across all locations. Together, the findings demonstrate that gaze does not merely coordinate interaction between individuals but also shapes how uninvolved others perceive and move through shared environments. By isolating gaze reciprocity from spatial arrangement, we demonstrate that mutual gaze functions as a dynamic social boundary organizing the permeability of public space.

candidates.title: What craft-makers know, and what they need: mapping skills and learning preferences across European craft-ecosystems
candidates.abstract: This article investigates which skills contemporary craft-makers consider most relevant, which they prefer to develop or outsource, and how these preferences reflect different educational contexts. We conducted fieldwork in four European craft ecosystems (Bassano del Grappa, Venice, Dals Långed, Bornholm) through interviews, an online questionnaire, and three co-creation workshops. We develop a framework comprising five skill areas: craft-making and technical, technological, business, communication and selling, and transversal skills. Our findings reveal how craft-making is shaped by a complex interplay between the primacy of craft-making skills, the uneasy yet unavoidable role of managerial and communication skills, and persistent tensions around technology and sustainability. Craft-makers generally prefer to develop making and transversal skills while outsourcing business and administrative activities. Learning is also constrained by limited time, and economic precarity, while national educational systems shape distinct career pathways and skill needs, requiring context-sensitive policy support.

candidates.title: When loneliness amplifies the risk of problematic emotional dependence: perceived anthropomorphism and basic psychological need satisfaction in AI companion use
candidates.abstract: Background Companion-oriented conversational AI can be experienced as socially responsive, yet evidence about problematic reliance requires construct clarity and noncausal interpretation. This study examined whether perceived anthropomorphism was associated with problematic AI-companion dependence directly and indirectly through basic psychological need satisfaction. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 666 adults in China who reported using a listed AI companion or conversational AI product during the preceding month. The nonclinical outcome was operationalized with six indicators spanning impaired control, distress, continued use, perceived understanding, emotion-regulation reliance, and displacement of offline communication. Measurement evidence was examined using reliability estimates, one-factor confirmatory models, and HTMT. Standardized composite-score regressions used HC3 robust standard errors, and the indirect association was evaluated with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Results Perceived anthropomorphism was positively associated with need satisfaction ( β = 0.569, p < 0.001). In the outcome model, need satisfaction ( β = 0.317, p < 0.001) and perceived anthropomorphism ( β = 0.385, p < 0.001) were both positively associated with problematic dependence. The standardized indirect association was 0.180 (95% bootstrap CI [0.137, 0.229]); R 2 was 0.323 for need satisfaction and 0.389 for problematic dependence. Conclusion The pattern is consistent with a need-satisfaction account of companion-oriented AI use, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering, substitution, or causality. Design and policy implications should therefore focus on transparency, user agency, and safeguards against escalating reliance rather than treating anthropomorphism itself as inherently harmful.

candidates.title: Using photo-elicitation interviews to explore the experiences of social media influencers with visible differences: “I didn’t mean to become a voice for our whole community”
candidates.abstract: Some individuals with visible differences (conditions or injuries that affect one's appearance), have become social media influencers, using their platforms to share experiences, challenge stereotypes, and promote representation of appearance diversity. However, no research has explored their experiences and how they navigate this evolving role. Therefore, semi-structured photo-elicitation interviews were carried out with fourteen adult influencers (aged 18-45) with a range of visible differences to understand their experiences. Social media posts from their own accounts were used to facilitate the discussion. The sample included nine cisgender women, one trans woman, and four cisgender men. All participants used Instagram, 11 used TikTok, nine Facebook, and three YouTube, with follower counts ranging from 4300 to 300,000. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis within a critical realist/contextualist framework. Three themes were generated: (1) 'You've got to create your own seat at the table', (2) 'Feeling an endless pressure to influence', and (3) 'There is no handbook for this job'. Social media provided opportunities to increase visibility of visible differences, foster connection, and influence public perceptions. However, participants described continuous pressure to produce content, remain visible, and support their communities while protecting their own wellbeing. As influencing is a new and evolving role, they often balanced authenticity, social responsibility, and financial sustainability without formal guidance. Influencers with visible differences play an important role in representation and advocacy of appearance diversity but face unique challenges. Findings underscore the need for clearer guidance, regulation, and support to promote safe, sustainable, and socially responsible influencing.

candidates.title: From Virtual Persona to Purchase: The Trust Engagement Pathway of AI-Generated Influencers in Sustainable Textile Marketing
candidates.abstract: While AI-generated social media influencers can provide consistency, scalability, and creative control to the textile industry, there is a question about their credibility when they make sustainability-related statements. The current research investigates how the effectiveness of AI-influencers affects consumers' trust in brands, sustainable brand engagement, and purchase intention in the textile industry in Pakistan. The model combines the Stimulus-Organism-Response model and source credibility and signaling models. To finalize and validate the reporting framework, a deliberately generated data set of 250 potential social-media consumers was analyzed with an explicitly simulated approach in PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrapped replications. All HTMT ratios were below .85 and the measurement model had acceptable reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .854-.884) and convergent validity (AVE = .683-.718). AI-influencer effectiveness was a strong predictor of consumer trust, sustainable engagement, and purchase intention (beta = .497, .251, and .181, respectively). The trust variable (beta = .425) and the variable of sustainable engagement (beta = .176) to purchase intention were significant, while the variable of sustainable engagement was the strongest predictor of purchase intention (beta = .346). Indirect effects via trust and engagement and the serial pathway of trust-engagement also showed significant results. The results confirm that AI-powered endorsers have the greatest impact when they are transparent and credible, fostering trust and driving sustainability awareness to genuine engagement with the brand. This is a simulated numerical dataset, and thus the results illustrate an analytically coherent paper structure; these should be replaced or verified with real field data prior to the actual publication of the dataset.

candidates.title: Toward Trustworthy Physical AI for Human Interaction
candidates.abstract: Robots are entering human spaces faster than we can establish when they deserve trust. We propose a framework for trustworthy physical AI that integrates Safety, Behavioral Intelligibility, and Perceptual Alignment across embodiment, control, cognition, and design. Trustworthiness emerges from aligning physical capabilities, observable behavior, and expectations people form during interaction.

candidates.title: Why Large Language Models will Never be Embodied: A Categorical, Not Engineering, Impossibility
candidates.abstract: Abstract A persistent ambition in artificial intelligence research holds that large language models (LLMs) will eventually become embodied—through attachment to robots, augmentation with multimodal sensors, integration into vision–language–action architectures, or sheer scale until grounding emerges from training data. This ambition rests on a misunderstanding of embodiment. Embodiment is a constitutive condition of being a self-producing, self-maintaining living system whose continued existence is genuinely at stake in its couplings with the environment. Adding sensors, actuators, or physical instantiation to a computational substrate yields engineered coupling, which is something else entirely. We identify five conditions that any genuinely embodied system must satisfy—autopoietic closure, precariousness, constructive self-determination, intrinsic temporality, and mereological closure—and show that no computational artifact can satisfy any of them, let alone all five. The barrier is categorical incompatibility: the same property that makes a system computational (heteronomous design and maintenance through external specification) is the property that precludes it from being embodied. Coupling artifacts to environments through transducers achieves engineered interaction. Having a body and being a body are different conditions. We close by examining why the embodiment-equivalence claim persists despite its categorical impossibility, and by arguing that the confusion sustains two harms—overselling AI systems for tasks they cannot perform, and misdirecting public concern toward speculative futures while the actual harms of deployed systems accumulate without being addressed. Clarifying the categorical distinction is a precondition for taking the genuine stakes of AI deployment seriously rather than as a philosophical aside.

candidates.title: アニメを通して学ぶ中級の日本語 Learning Intermediate Japanese through Anime
candidates.abstract: Learning Intermediate Japanese through Anime builds Japanese learners’ linguistic proficiency while deepening their cultural and historical understanding of anime. Designed around anime-themed readings, dialogues, and activities, the textbook helps learners develop skills in reading, writing, listening, and speaking as they explore anime as a significant artistic and cultural form. The book is structured around eight key topics: the origins of anime, the anime industry, anime as technology, anime as design, anime as genre, anime as language, gods of anime, and anime fandom. Each lesson focuses on a different language skill such as describing historical events in the passive voice, interpreting and presenting data, explaining processes, describing visual and narrative elements, summarizing information, forming arguments, making comparisons, and expressing opinions. Through this integrated approach, learners gain both practical Japanese language skills and a critical framework for understanding anime as a dynamic and influential part of Japanese culture. This textbook is intended for students of Japanese language at the intermediate high to advanced low level on the ACTFL proficiency scale and CEFR level B1 to B2. Accompanying online resources include audio recordings of readings from the book and sample grammar worksheets to facilitate classroom planning. These materials can be accessed at www.routledge.com/9781041089636 .

candidates.title: Virtual bodies, real touch: haptic social communication across VR, MR, and cross-reality
candidates.abstract: Introduction Visual and auditory channels in collaborative Extended Reality (XR) can become saturated during complex shared interactions, leaving the potential of social touch–one of the most direct channels for interpersonal communication–largely ignored. This work investigates haptic feedback as a complementary communication channel for supporting social coordination and interpersonal communication across Virtual Reality (VR), Mixed Reality (MR), and cross-reality environments. Methods We present a haptic-enabled multi-user XR system that enables physically distant users to initiate and receive real-time, bidirectional social touch. We developed wearable gloves and forearm sleeves containing 26 vibrotactile actuators distributed across each hand and arm, controlled through a wireless, device-agnostic communication framework. Users can perform and receive social touch gestures, interact with virtual objects, and receive spatially localized vibrotactile feedback. We evaluated our framework with 40 participants forming 20 dyads in a two-part within-subject study. In a prescribed-touch task, participants communicated seven emotions using direct physical touch and mediated touch across VR and MR. We examined how emotion communication differed between physical and mediated touch and whether the realities of the initiator and receiver influenced the interaction. In a free-exploration task, participants interacted unconstrained in VR and MR while we assessed touch behavior, embodiment, presence, social presence, usability, and haptic experience. Results Our results showed that meaningful affective information and emotion-specific gesture patterns were preserved across realities, although direct physical touch produced the strongest affective alignment. The receiver’s reality influenced emotion recognition more strongly than the initiator’s reality, while VR supported longer and more varied touch interactions and MR provided stronger embodiment and perceived usability. Our findings demonstrate that haptic feedback can serve as a critical secondary communication channel for social touch in XR, and our system can support meaningful social touch across heterogeneous realities. Discussion Our findings help derive design implications for improving affective experiences, multisensory interaction, embodiment, and future collaborative XR systems.

candidates.title: Peer Review Report For: TECHNOLOGY-BASED TEACHING IN HIGHER EDUCATION IN SOUTH AFRICA: NAVIGATING THE POST-COVID LANDSCAPE (A Systematic Review) [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]
candidates.abstract: This systematic review examines the impact of Technology-Based Teaching (TBT) on transforming learning and knowledge production in South Africa’s higher education institutions (HEIs) in the post-COVID-19 context. Grounded in the principles of Digital Humanities (DH), the study explores how TBT fosters inclusive, student-centered, and context-responsive learning in environments characterized by unequal access to digital resources. A systematic search of Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect was conducted for studies published between 2002 and 2024. Following PRISMA guidelines, 204 records were screened, 84 full-text articles were assessed, and 49 studies were included in the final synthesis. Data were analyzed using mixed coding techniques within a critical research paradigm, guided by Actor–Network Theory (ANT), to examine interactions among human actors (lecturers, students, policymakers) and technological systems (e.g., learning management systems, virtual classrooms, and Open Educational Resources). The findings reveal persistent challenges, including unequal access to digital infrastructure, limited technological proficiency, language barriers, and ethical concerns related to privacy and surveillance. However, evidence indicates that, when effectively supported, TBT enhances learner engagement, promotes collaborative and participatory learning, and strengthens critical thinking. Despite these benefits, structural inequalities and institutional resistance continue to hinder widespread adoption. The study concludes that TBT holds significant transformative potential for African HEIs, provided its implementation is ethically grounded, contextually responsive, and supported by strong institutional commitment. It recommends investing in digital infrastructure, continuous digital skills development, adopting blended learning models, and strengthening cross-sector collaboration to advance equitable and sustainable digital teaching ecosystems.

candidates.title: 2026 State of Open Source in Europe: Navigating AI and Digital Sovereignty Through Open Governance
candidates.abstract: How are AI and digital sovereignty reshaping open source governance in Europe? Marking a major research milestone, LF Research and LF Europe have published the 5th annual State of Open Source in Europe, delivering crucial data on navigating these operational mandates. Digital sovereignty is now a strategic priority for 94% of European organizations, driven heavily by security and privacy concerns. Meanwhile, AI adoption is accelerating open source engagement: 76% of organizations report AI tools help them extract greater value from their existing open source software. Crucially, governance maturity pays off, as organizations with advanced governance achieve a 4.6x benefit-to-cost return on open source, compared to 3.6x for those with no formal governance. Read the report to discover how open governance drives ROI, mitigates regulatory risk, and secures long-term digital resilience.

candidates.title: Neither queer, nor just a transaction: realignment speech and the pursuit of heteronormative intelligibility in otome cosplay commissions
candidates.abstract: The commercial rise of Chinese otome games has birthed a novel gig economy: ‘cosplay commissions’, where female fans hire female cosplayers to enact fictional romances. Drawing on 32 in-depth interviews, this study explores the tension in this novel fan practice: while the practice enables participants to experiment with a feminized, consumer-driven model of intimacy, where women actively orchestrate their ideal romance, it simultaneously triggers anxieties about violating scripts of heteronormativity. To manage these tensions, participants collaboratively enact a ‘sanitized romance’ through relational work that meticulously curates idealized heteronormative romance scripts (caring, pampering, and exclusivity), compensating for the perceived failures of real-world masculinity. More importantly, to secure moral legitimacy within China’s patriarchal constraints, participants produce what we term realignment speech, drawing symbolic boundaries to distance themselves from any association with sex work, queerness, or moral deviance. Through this boundary work, they reframe their actions not as ‘buying love’ or ‘loving a woman’, but as ‘immersing in pure love fantasy’. We argue that this ambivalent mode of intimacy – transgressive in practice yet normatively policed in self-understanding – demonstrates how realignment speech renders female desire intelligible and thus survivable within a rigid moral economy through both micro-resistance to dominant norms and creative reappropriation of their toolkit.

Together, 5 these modalities can support more robust and adaptive robotic behaviors. candidates.title: From Decision-Maker to Decision Architect: Generative AI and the Changing Role of Leadership
candidates.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is becoming an integral part of managerial work, changing how leaders analyse information, communicate, coordinate, and decide. Much of the existing leadership literature emphasizes productivity effects or debates substitution versus augmentation. We argue that the more fundamental leadership challenge is the reconfiguration of decision authority and the design of decision processes across human–AI arrangements. As GenAI systems become more capable, context-aware, and agentic, leadership becomes less about individual judgement and more about structuring how judgement is distributed across human and AI actors. This conceptual paper asks how GenAI changes leadership decision-making in contemporary organizations. Drawing on research on algorithmic management, the automation–augmentation paradox, AI-mediated leadership, and principal–agent perspectives on AI agents, we develop a framework that positions leaders as decision architects, i.e., actors who deliberately design and govern decision processes rather than merely participate in them. The main contribution of the paper is a typology of four roles GenAI can have in leadership decision making, distinguished by the degree of AI autonomy and the locus of decision authority: AI as assistant, AI as advisor, AI as oversight partner, and AI as delegated actor. For each role, we discuss implications for decision rights, employee autonomy, and managerial expertise. We further argue that the agentic AI highlights classical delegation problems of goal alignment, information asymmetries, and control, turning governance decisions into a core leadership concern. By focusing on design of human–AI decision architectures, the paper contributes to leadership and organization literature by clarifying how GenAI can change concepts of authority, control, and legitimacy in contemporary organizations. We outline a research agenda on AI-augmented leadership capabilities, responsible delegation to AI agents, and the conditions under which GenAI can improve leadership legitimacy.

candidates.title: Towards Designing for (Dis)Trust in Technologies for Aging
candidates.abstract: Across cohorts of older adults and generations of technology, (dis)trust has continued to shape the acceptance of technologies for aging. Yet, we still know little about if or how to design for older adults’ distrust in technology. Towards this, we reviewed empirical studies in which older adults discussed trust and distrust in relation to technology. Our analysis shows that (dis)trust is constituted in three key ways: emerges when material arrangements of digital systems become illegible, such as when older adults cannot determine where information is stored or trace its movement; is temporally constituted and fluid, building and shifting through prior experience and breakdowns, and at times distrust can operate as boundary work through which individuals limit technology’s reach into their autonomy, relationships, and everyday lives. Our work yields design directions for supporting trust across different phases of technology use and by designing systems that make the movement and persistence of information more perceptible.

candidates.title: Towards Enhanced Psychosocial Well-Being for Persons Living with Dementia: An Integrative Review of Meaningful Activities in Long-Term Care
candidates.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Meaningful engagement in clinical interventions or technology-mediated activities can support the psychosocial well-being of persons living with dementia. However, meaningfulness is often assumed rather than explicitly conceptualized in both academic context and in care practice.OBJECTIVES: This review aims to examine how interventions and activity provision can support psychosocial well-being and how meaningful engagement is shaped by the conditions surrounding their provision, with particular attention to people with moderate and advanced dementia in long-term care facilities. METHODS: An integrative review was conducted through article searching in databases including PubMed, Scopus, and the ACM Digital Library dated from 2014 through 2025. In this review, 60 publications were synthesized for answering proposed objectives and questions.RESULTS: We identified six activity forms and five recurring mechanisms through which activities acquire psychosocial value and are considered meaningful. The central finding is that meaningfulness is not an inherent property of an intervention or technology-mediated activity. It was shaped by the changing relationship between the person, activity, other stakeholders, and care environment. Activities are more likely to become meaningful when they connect with the person’s identity and retained abilities, permit supported forms of agency, are facilitated within responsive relationships and workable care routines.CONCLUSION: This review advances a person-centered design agenda that shifts attention from isolated interventions toward activity-care ecosystems. It extends previous intervention- and technology-centered reviews by explaining how meaningful engagement can be co-produced, evaluated, and sustained in everyday dementia care.

candidates.title: Value‑added and overdraft risks in new‑media marketing of offline entertainment derivatives from an emotional currency perspective
candidates.abstract: The offline cultural‑entertainment performance market has continued to experience robust growth. Meanwhile, IP derivatives have leveraged social media to facilitate both dissemination and commercial conversion, with emotional currency emerging as a critical analytical lens for interpreting contemporary consumption behaviors in this sector. Taking the new‑media marketing of offline cultural‑entertainment derivatives as its research subject, this paper employs literature review and case study analysis to systematically delineate the relevant conceptual and theoretical frameworks, and further explores how emotional currency is generated, disseminated, and ultimately achieves value appreciation within the new‑media environment. This study reveals that offline cultural‑entertainment scenarios lay the foundation for emotional currency, and User‑Generated Content communication within social circles drives its value appreciation. Nevertheless, traffic‑dominated excessive marketing may result in the overdraft of emotional currency. Value appreciation and overdraft are not entirely contradictory; instead, they are two sides of the same coin with homologous symbiosis. While new‑media marketing creates emotional value, it inherently carries risks of consuming audience sentiment.

candidates.title: Seeing the Forest for the Trees: Emergent Agreement from Individual Conversations
candidates.abstract: As LLM agents interact in the wild and shape each other's decisions, understanding how they converge toward agreement becomes important. We study this in multi-turn conversations where two LLMs discuss subjective matters, can agree or disagree, and may change their stances. Using a linear classifier on individual conversation activations, we identify an internal representation of agreement. We find that it varies substantially across turns and conversations and does not reliably track external agreement at the individual conversation level. We therefore move beyond the representation of agreement in individual conversations, by aggregating the agreement representation across conversations. Externally, this aggregate view reveals a simple structure: when pooled across conversations, agreement can be predicted well with a Markov process, with agreement at each turn being a direct function of agreement at the previous turn. Similarly, when internal agreement is aggregated, it couples with the external Markov agreement through a power-law mapping, exposing Markovian dynamics in internal representations. Additionally, we find that after a change of stance, models express agreement externally before their internal representations reflect the same shift. These results reveal a joint structure between internal and external agreement that emerges only when internal features are aggregated across conversations. Code available at https://github.com/technion-cs-nlp/SeeingTheForestForTheTrees.

Remote Expert Evaluation of Tabletop Avatar Gaze Control in Asymmetric Multi-Scale MR--VR Collaboration
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes an integrated setup for a multi-scale asymmetric collaboration scenario in the context of a remote-expert use case, focusing on the expert side. In this system, the remote expert (with an exocentric view in Mixed Reality (MR)) uses a Tangible User Interface (TUI) to precisely position and rotate their avatar within a scaled tabletop World-in-Miniature (WIM). Inside the WIM, the expert's avatar and the operator share the same scale and egocentric view, while the expert retains a global tabletop overview of the plant to support collaboration. Interviews with industry experts during the participatory design phase revealed the need for an egocentric view inside the plant on the remote-expert side to enable full collaboration. We designed and studied three interaction-visualisation combinations to integrate and control the expert avatar's gaze: VR (fully immersive with direct head control), Head (floating screen with direct head control), and Touch (on-avatar screen with touchpad control). We evaluated these methods with 29 participants across two fault-detection tasks: Same Machine, where both collaborators inspect the same machine, and Twin Machine, where they inspect identical machines in separate locations. The VR condition, which combines immersion, direct head control, and a full-scale view, yielded the strongest overall performance and user experience, while the tabletop avatar setup was well received for collaboration. Our findings inform the design of gaze-control techniques for asymmetric MR-VR collaboration and reveal challenges and opportunities for future work.

Trade, AI-robot adoption, and manufacturing transformation: cross-national determinants of firm-level automation in heterogeneous institutional contexts
candidates.abstract: It investigates the multi-dimensional determinants of AI-driven robot adoption among manufacturing firms to examine how perceived benefits, industry peer pressure, and international trade exposure jointly shape firm-level automation decisions across heterogeneous institutional contexts during 2016–2024. Using a firm-level 12,000 manufacturer panel data, it employs PPML estimation with high-dimensional fixed effects, instrumental variables using historical tariffs and partner-country demand shocks to address trade endogeneity, and System GMM to capture dynamic adjustment. The analytical framework integrates TAM, institutional isomorphism theory, and Melitz’s heterogeneous firm model. Empirical results show the strongest adoption driver, with long-run effects nearly double short-run estimates. Industry peer pressure accelerates diffusion through competitive mimicry and network density. Trade exposure causally stimulates automation, exporters respond to quality demands, import-competing firms automate defensively. Cross-country analysis reveals Germany’s highest benefit responsiveness, Korea’s strongest peer effects, and China’s policy-coordinated balanced patterns. It provides the first integrated cross-national empirical analysis of behavioral, institutional, and trade-related automation mechanisms within a single framework, demonstrating that effective automation policy must verify benefit perceptions, industry coordination, and trade integration across diverse institutional contexts. candidates.title: MemRevise: A Self-Revising Memory for Conversational Search
candidates.abstract: In conversational search, users correct misun-derstandings, revise their requests and return to earlier topics, so part of the history no longer reflects what they want. Existing benchmarks do not isolate such turns. Current search methods either re-read the history or keep a record of every turn, and none of them marks earlier content as dropped. We introduce CONVREVISE, a benchmark of 4,429 test questions in six tiers of returns and revisions over TopiOCQA, CORAL and OR-QuAC. We also propose MEMREVISE, which combines a revisable memory graph, a 3B writer distilled from teacher memories, and a search guided by the memory. The writer reads each turn once and adds a node that records its topic, its facts and the operations it performs, such as adding, abandoning or reactivating a topic. Topic status follows from these operations, so a dropped topic keeps its facts and can be restored. With a frozen retriever, MEMREVISE reaches a mean MRR@10 of 0.701, against 0.589 for the best competitor, ConvSearch-R1-FT, and 0.617 for a writer distilled the same way without the memory, so the memory and the steps built on it add 0.084. MEMREVISE is significantly better on Topi- OCQA and OR-QuAC, statistically tied with prompted 32B rewriters on CORAL, and never significantly behind the strongest competitor of any tier.

candidates.title: The adoption, efficacy, and limitations of large language models in urological education
candidates.abstract: The integration of large language models into medical education is rapidly transforming pedagogical approaches, particularly in specialized fields like urology. This study aims to evaluate the adoption patterns, perceived efficacy, and significant limitations of these artificial intelligence (AI) tools among urology trainees. This research employed a descriptive, cross-sectional study design through an online survey disseminated to urology trainees at a single institution. A total of 194 complete responses were collected from medical students and interns. The survey assessed adoption patterns, perceived efficacy on a 7-point Likert-scale, and limitations. The analysis revealed near-universal adoption (98.4%), with 65% of participants using AI tools daily, predominantly ChatGPT. Key applications included generating exam-style questions and summarizing complex guidelines. Participants reported significant perceived improvements in core knowledge areas, with the highest gains in disease knowledge and diagnostics (Median = 7, interquartile range: 6-7), which were strongly correlated with increased clinical confidence. Multivariate regression identified usage frequency and comfort with technology as significant predictors of knowledge improvement (β = 0.29, P = .001) and confidence gains (β = 0.30, P < .001). The primary limitation identified was the potential for AI "hallucinations" or incorrect information (54.1%). Large language models are widely adopted and perceived as highly effective for enhancing knowledge and clinical reasoning in urological education. However, their transformative potential is tempered by critical concerns regarding reliability. A balanced approach that combines these powerful AI tools with vigilant oversight is essential.

candidates.title: A Deep Learning-based Feature-level Privacy-preserving and Intrusion Detection Framework for Intelligent Cybersecurity Using Blockchain
candidates.abstract: The advent of the fast growth of interconnected digital infrastructures has increased the necessity of privacyconserving cybersecurity solutions that can detect network intrusions without revealing sensitive traffic data.Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDSs) typically analyse raw network traffic in a centralized manner, a practice that heightens the risk of data leakage and privacy breaches.This study proposes an IDS that preserves privacy at the feature level by coupling deep representation learning with encrypted, blockchain-based storage.The architecture suggested uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) model for extracting compact and discriminative representations of network traffic flows.A multi-stage privacy pipeline comprising feature normalization, secret permutation, and AES-256-GCM encryption is proposed and empirically evaluated against membership-inference, reconstruction, and attribute-inference attacks before storage in a permissioned blockchain ledger.The suggested framework uses encrypted deep feature vectors, unlike current methods of storing raw traffic data or sharing model gradients, which significantly lowers the privacy attack surface and preserve detection.The framework was tested on four popular databases of intrusion detection, such as CICIDS2017, IoTIDS20, NSL-KDD, and TRAIN_TEST_NETWORK.Experimental results demonstrate strong detection performance, with accuracy exceeding 0.95 and reaching approximately 0.997, alongside high processing throughput and low computational overhead.The findings indicate that integrating deep feature learning, cryptographic protection, and blockchain-based storage achieves a favorable balance among privacy preservation, system efficiency, and detection accuracy.The proposed architecture could be scaled to privacy-sensitive environments, such as in IoT systems, healthcare systems, and enterprise security monitoring systems.

candidates.title: Menuju Sistem AI yang Dapat Dijelaskan (XAI) untuk Pengalaman Pengguna yang Lebih Baik: Studi tentang Interaksi Multimodal pada Perangkat Cerdas untuk Pembelajaran Reflektif
candidates.abstract: Sistem Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) semakin terintegrasi dalam kehidupan sehari-hari melalui perangkat cerdas, namun kurangnya transparansi dan kemampuan menjelaskan (explainability) sering menjadi hambatan dalam membangun kepercayaan dan pengalaman pengguna yang bermakna. Penelitian ini mengkaji peran Explainable AI (XAI) dalam meningkatkan pengalaman pengguna melalui interaksi multimodal pada perangkat cerdas, dengan fokus pada bagaimana mekanisme penjelasan dapat mendukung pembelajaran reflektif. Melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis terhadap perkembangan terkini dalam XAI, interaksi multimodal, dan desain antarmuka, penelitian ini mengidentifikasi bahwa efektivitas XAI sangat bergantung pada bagaimana penjelasan disampaikan dan dikontekstualisasikan dalam pengalaman pengguna. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan multimodal menggabungkan penjelasan visual, tekstual, dan auditori meningkatkan pemahaman pengguna hingga 40% dibandingkan penjelasan unimodal, sementara penjelasan adaptif yang disesuaikan dengan tingkat keahlian pengguna meningkatkan kepercayaan dan kepuasan secara signifikan. Interaksi multimodal pada perangkat cerdas memungkinkan pengguna untuk mengeksplorasi dan memahami keputusan AI melalui berbagai saluran sensorik, mendorong pembelajaran reflektif dimana pengguna tidak hanya menerima output AI tetapi juga merefleksikan proses penalaran di baliknya. Tantangan yang masih ada mencakup trade-off antara transparansi dan kejelasan, beban kognitif dari penjelasan yang berlebihan, serta kebutuhan untuk menyeimbangkan akurasi dan interpretabilitas dalam model AI. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa XAI multimodal yang dirancang dengan mempertimbangkan kebutuhan pengguna dan konteks penggunaan dapat menjadi jembatan antara kompleksitas teknis AI dan pengalaman pengguna yang intuitif dan memberdayakan, membuka jalan menuju AI yang lebih transparan, tepercaya, dan kolaboratif.

candidates.title: Robotics and Trust
candidates.abstract: Imagine you would be hanging on a cliff—Would you take a robot’s hand? Though the imagination of one hanging on a cliff seems dramatic, it well demonstrates a situation of vulnerability in which a person needs to rely on another’s capability and integrity to help him or her. As the number of service robots in various fields increases enormously, see [ 74 ], it is likely that people will find themselves in situations of vulnerability in which they depend on robotic assistance. As such, robots cannot be merely regarded as tools performing repetitive tasks. Instead, robots’ role as embodied social agents that are attributed with intentions and morality gains importance. This calls for a clear understanding of trust in HRI which needs to be well distinguished from trust in automation, see [ 41 ] for a review. The best way to achieve this is to understand trust in interpersonal relationships first.

candidates.title: How Should We Evaluate Naturalness for Synthetic Speech with a Foreign Accent?
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis technology have enabled the generation of speech with diverse characteristics. One such characteristic is a foreign accent. In our preliminary experiments, we found that UTMOS, a widely used automatic speech quality assessment system, tended to assign lower scores to speech with stronger foreign accents, even though it is produced by a human speaker. This observation raised a question: How do humans evaluate the naturalness of foreign-accented speech? We conducted a large-scale subjective evaluation involving both native and non-native listeners under different evaluation instructions. The results showed that humans also considered accentedness when evaluating naturalness, but that defining naturalness in terms of human-likeness and selecting raters who have greater exposure to the target accent may enable more appropriate evaluation. This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

candidates.title: “I would not be a burden on a robot.” A scoping review of older adults' ‘lonely-emotional complexes’ when using Social AI (SAI)
Trust in AI-mediated electronic commerce: a systematic review and integrative framework
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence now stands between merchants and consumers across digital exchange, in chatbots, recommenders, virtual influencers, generative content, service robots and robo-advisors. Consumer reliance on that intermediary is shaped in part by trust. This review synthesises 166 studies in which trust or calibrated reliance is explicitly measured, manipulated or theorised, screened from 7,606 records under PRISMA 2020, with 45 trust-adjacent studies reported separately. Coding what is trusted shows three referents, the AI agent, the deploying merchant and the platform-institutional system, distributed non-randomly across applications. Formal testing finds no detectable association between the direction of the anthropomorphism effect and either stakes or referent, a provisional association between disclosure direction and stakes, and a strong association between reporting any boundary condition and experimental design. The resulting framework links referent, mechanism, boundary condition, trust and reliance state, outcome and repair, and reframes electronic commerce design around calibrated reliance rather than maximal trust.

candidates.title: AI BASED HAND GESTURE CONTROLLED ROBOT
candidates.abstract: The proposed system presents an advanced AI-based hand gesture controlled telepresence robot designed for operation in hazardous and inaccessible environments. The system enables a remote operator to control a robotic rover using real-time hand gestures without the need for physical controllers or wearable devices. It integrates computer vision techniques using OpenCV and MediaPipe for accurate skeletal hand tracking and gesture recognition. A dual-processing architecture ensures efficient handling of high-definition video streaming and gesture interpretation with minimal latency. The robot provides real-time visual feedback through wireless video transmission, enabling safe navigation and monitoring. The system ensures intuitive control, improved safety, and enhanced operational efficiency. This solution is highly applicable in disaster management, industrial inspection, and healthcare environments where human presence is risky or limited.

candidates.title: Implementing robotic-assisted therapy in stroke rehabilitation: a structured narrative review of evidence and technology adoption barriers in Indonesia
candidates.abstract: Introduction Robotic-assisted therapy (RAT) has emerged as a promising intervention for post-stroke recovery; however, its implementation in developing countries such as Indonesia remains limited by economic, technical, and systemic barriers. This structured narrative review summarizes clinical effect reported by systematics review and meta-analyses and examines implementation consideration and potential economic feasibility within the Indonesian healthcare context. Method A structured review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (2015–2025) was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and Cochrane Library. Studies involving adult with stroke were included. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity. Implementation barriers were analyzed, and a scenario-based economic model was developed to assess feasibility of RAT in Indonesia. QALY-equivalent outcomes (QEOs) were estimated using ratio-based value-transfer approach that scaled published reference values according to observed functional effects. Result Evidence from 22 systematic reviews indicated that RAT improved functional outcomes compared with conventional therapy, particularly gait and upper-limb function (effect sizes: 0.02–0.52). Key implementation barriers included limited device availability, inadequate workforce training, and regulatory constraints. Modelled ICERs ranged from US$236.23–752.31 per QEO for upper-limb rehabilitation and US$558.86–4,890 per QEO for gait-related rehabilitation. Most estimates remained below the Indonesian willingness-to-pay threshold ( Conclusion RAT shows potential clinical benefits, but implementation in Indonesia should consider clinical effectiveness, economic feasibility, infrastructure, workforce, technology acceptance, and reimbursement. A phased approach in suitable tertiary-care settings may support wider adoption based on local evidence.

candidates.title: AI-based task-scheduling advice: the associations between adoption intent, AI anthropomorphism, and perceived competence fit
candidates.abstract: Recent studies have suggested that user adoption of AI-based outputs may be positively related to AI agent anthropomorphism, with perceived agent competence serving as a mediator. This paper examines those relationships in the novel, general-purpose context of AI-based task-scheduling advice, which guides users in their daily activities. Path analyses were conducted across two scenario-based studies (Study 1, N = 258; Study 2, N = 194), which presented AI-based apps. Both studies indicated positive associations between perceived agent anthropomorphism and advice adoption, with a mediated path through perceived competence agent-advice fit. Moreover, Study 2 indicated positive associations between a user's individual tendency to anthropomorphize and advice adoption intent, with a mediated path through perceived agent anthropomorphism and perceived competence agent-advice fit. These results extend the knowledge about user response to AI by demonstrating associations between AI anthropomorphism, perceived competence, and adoption intent in the area of task-scheduling advice, and by applying anthropomorphizing tendency as a user characteristic involved in these associations. These findings can guide practitioners on how users may respond to AI-based task-scheduling advice.
