candidates.title: Loneliness to consumption intention: emotional bonding and escapism in AI emotional companion app use
candidates.abstract: With the diffusion of generative AI, AI emotional companion apps have emerged as a new domain of digital consumption in which users may pay to extend relationship-like experiences. This study examines how loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy are associated with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention through two competing pathways: emotional bonding with the AI (relational compensation) and escapism (avoidant compensation). The emotional bond with the AI is modeled as a second-order construct comprising anthropomorphism, emotional responsiveness, and parasocial intimacy. Data were collected from 393 adult users in China who used AI emotional companion apps at least twice per week and were analyzed using structural equation modeling. Loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy were positively associated with both emotional bonding and escapism. However, significant indirect associations with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention emerged only through the emotional-bond pathway. Direct comparisons further showed that the relational indirect effects were significantly stronger than the avoidant indirect effects across all antecedent-outcome combinations. Escapism was significantly associated with both outcomes when modeled alone but became nonsignificant when emotional bonding was included, suggesting that its association with consumer responses largely overlaps with the relational pathway. A partial-mediation analysis further showed that actual-ideal self-discrepancy retained a significant direct association with continuance intention. These findings suggest that relational compensation, rather than avoidant compensation, is more closely associated with willingness to pay for experience enhancement and intention to continue using AI companions. The study extends compensatory-use, self-discrepancy, and parasocial-interaction perspectives to the AI-companion context by linking psychological vulnerability to experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention, while highlighting implications for responsible relational design and user protection.

candidates.title: Building Trustworthy Household Robots through Open-World Safety
candidates.abstract: Foundation models are expanding robot capabilities, enabling robots to handle more diverse objects, follow sophisticated instructions, and operate in complex environments. These advances bring us to a future in which robots become part of everyday household life. However, cluttered, dynamic household environments also expose robots to unfamiliar objects, tasks, and interactions, making reliable zero-shot task completion an ongoing challenge for robotics research. From a security perspective, we argue for open-world safety: household robots should preserve specified safety requirements in unseen situations, including when they cannot complete the requested task. Safety protections must account for context and interactions that persist across actions and tasks. In this position paper, we examine why existing safety methods can fail to provide this protection. Protection can fail through misinterpreted context, overlooked past interactions, or stopping and recovery strategies that become unsafe under unfamiliar conditions. We therefore propose a research agenda to specify, learn, and ground safety requirements, enforce them with reliable recovery, and evaluate the generalization of such protections. We call for household robots whose safety protections remain reliable beyond the situations, context, and history used to train and develop them, to achieve open-world safety.

candidates.title: Multimodal human-intent modeling for contextual robot-to-human handovers of arbitrary objects
EyeTAG: Eye Trajectory-Aware Gaze Estimation
candidates.abstract: Gaze estimation under natural head-eye motion underpins applications from driver monitoring to human-computer interaction. Single-frame methods predict each frame independently, so consecutive outputs fluctuate as jitter. Multi-frame methods reduce this, but they learn motion implicitly inside appearance features, so the gaze trajectory is never an explicit variable. We propose EyeTAG (Eye Trajectory-Aware Gaze Estimation), a causal multi-frame framework built around an explicit first-order gaze prior: at each step it differentiates its own recent predictions and feeds the resulting trajectory back as a compact kinematic token. Because differencing is translation-invariant in gaze space, this token carries subject-invariant motion rather than personal gaze offsets. Face and eye streams supply visual evidence, fused by cross-attention and a causal Transformer decoder. EyeTAG reduces the mean angular error by about 1.0$^\circ$ on Gaze360 and performs on par with the strongest baseline on EVE (2.56$^\circ$ vs. 2.58$^\circ$). Within-model ablations, which keep the encoder and the rest of the architecture fixed and vary only the gaze history, show that the differential formulation, rather than temporal context alone, removes the systematic saccade bias that persists even with an absolute gaze-history prior. Our code is available at https://github.com/peter8366/EyeTAG.

candidates.title: “Serve Them with Rituals”: Power and Emotions in the Confucian Parent-Child Relationship
candidates.abstract: This article challenges the conventional portrayal of the parent-child relationship in Confucian thought as authoritarian and even oppressive. It reconstructs a Confucian ethical view of the relationship from the perspective of parenting in addition to the more common discussions of filial conduct. It argues that the Analects ’ view of filial conduct emphasizes following ritual norms instead of absolute obedience to parents. Although the Analects does not explicitly discuss parenting, passages that mention Confucius with his children are thought provoking. By examining the role of emotions and power dynamics in rituals involving the parent-child relationship, the article defends an account of how Confucian ritual cultivates appropriate love and respect on the part of both parents and children, and its intention is to restrain the conduct of the more powerful in such unequal relationships, instead of oppressing the vulnerable.

candidates.title: Robotic Assistants in the Operating Room: A Systematic Review of Vision‐Based Systems for Nonoperative Tasks
candidates.abstract: Nonoperative tasks in the operating room, such as instrument handling, sterile packaging, and logistics, are demanding yet have received less robotics attention than autonomous surgery. This review, the first to synthesize this literature, maps the perception methods, autonomy levels, methodological quality, and clinical readiness of vision‐based robotic assistants for scrub nurse, circulating nurse, and OR logistics roles. Searches of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar returned 465 records; 20 publications describing 11 robotic system families met inclusion criteria. Most evidence, 17 publications across eight system families, concerns scrub nurse assistance; circulating nurse support, OR logistics, and dental assistance are each represented by one system. Vision methods have moved from classical image processing and predefined gestures toward deep learning, multimodal perception, and vision–language–action models, but autonomy has not kept pace: one system family reaches LoA 1, seven LoA 2, and three LoA 3, with Technology Readiness Levels spanning TRL 4 to TRL 6. Reported success rates are often high but rarely comparable and mostly generated in laboratory or simulated settings. Closing that gap requires stronger evidence on safety, sterility, failure recovery, workflow integration, execution speed, reproducibility, and, notably absent, manipulation of deformable sterile materials.

candidates.title: Robots, artificial intelligence and spirituality/religiosity: a critical literacy perspective on human development
candidates.abstract: Artificial Intelligence, a natural language processing tool, connects human learning and interpretation to algorithms whose source code is hidden to us and uses linguistic modeling, a primarily statistical method, for analyzing and predicting character collocation patterns (Peters et al, 2023, p. 14). Humans willingly have given in to the charms of a “superior” technological cognition that is incapable, in fact, of thinking critically. In this article we aim at presenting the introduction of the use of AI in spiritual/religious spaces from the perspective of critical literacy (Freire, 1974, 1989, 2005, 2015). Thinking in terms of critical literacy allows for a flexibility of the emergence of meanings from diverse loci of enunciation and it enhances social justice. Drawing on a qualitative and interpretive methodology, this study embraces a sample of illustrations of the uses of AI in different contexts of faith, and one particular experience in a Candomblé house, while the authors analyse them from critical perspectives. The results unsettle modernist conceptions regarding meaning and sense making and move towards more pluriversal and situated relationality regarding AI and faith. We conclude that AI helps to expand inter-religious dialogues, spiritual engagement and accessibility may also be fostered outside institutional frameworks through AI. Despite such advantages, profit-driven algorithms can shape spiritual/religious experience, replicate universalized ethics and onto-epistemologies, spread fake news and distort sources of information, while strengthening capitalism, surveillance, racism, not to mention unsustainability.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Embodied Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Embodied learning (EL) is an educational approach that posits that cognition develops as learners interact with their environment through physical activity or sensory experiences. Artificial intelligence in education (AIED) supports teaching and learning for both teachers and students, for example through personalised intelligent tutoring systems. However, prior research on EL has focused primarily on students' cognitive and emotional abilities and the integration of body and task, rather than on technological elements, and research on technology‐based embodied learning (TBEL) has centred on immersive technologies such as VR and AR. Objectives This study aims to explore the relationship between AI technology and EL by analysing (1) the types of AI utilised in EL‐related research (algorithm or model, data modality, AI role), (2) learners' outcomes obtained from AI‐based EL, and (3) the limitations and solutions when applying AI to EL. Method This study is a systematic literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and no meta‐analysis was conducted. This study only referenced papers published since 2016 that included both AI technology and EL, were written in English, and dealt with learning processes mediated by physical activity. A study was treated as within scope only where the physical activity was tied to the concept to be learned. Papers were excluded if they did not specify the AI algorithm or model, were not peer‐reviewed, were secondary studies, were not in the field of education, were unavailable in full text, emphasised only simple skill acquisition in physical education or music, or emphasised only simple speaking activities in foreign language learning. Searches were conducted on 16 September 2025 in ACM, ERIC, and Web of Science. Given the diverse types of included studies, risk of bias was assessed using the MMAT2018 tool. Due to the varied nature of the data, a multi‐faceted data synthesis was performed. Co‐occurrences between data modality and AI role, and between AI role and learner outcomes, were visualised using heatmaps. The flow between the three variables was represented using a Sankey diagram. Finally, all frequencies were recalculated after excluding papers appraised as Low or not appraised, to test which patterns depended on weaker evidence. Results A total of 23 papers were reviewed. As multiple data points could be extracted per item, the relative proportion was calculated against the number of coding instances per item. The most frequently used AI algorithm/model in the EL context was deep learning, and the data modality was image data. Where multiple data types were used, it was tagged as multimodal, accounting for 34.8%. Analysis and evaluation roles were most frequently extracted, and cognitive outcomes were reported most often. Key limitations identified included restricted participant numbers due to research design and studies conducted in controlled environments. Among papers appraised as High, the most frequent pathways ran from multimodal data to recognition and detection and from sensor data to analysis and evaluation, and cognitive outcomes were the most frequently reported. When papers appraised as Low or not appraised were set aside, the concentration of AI in analytical roles persisted, whereas the evidence for AI as an interactive or generative participant weakened. Discussion This review describes reported patterns rather than pooled effect estimates, as no meta‐analysis was conducted. Exclusion of grey literature may introduce publication bias. Furthermore, the potential risk of selection bias exists as literature was collected based on inclusion/exclusion criteria. This study is significant in that it identified how AI is utilised within the EL context and the learner outcomes reported alongside it, particularly as the scope of AIED broadens.

candidates.title: Being a Padawan and Mastering the Force: A Dissertation Quest
candidates.abstract: This study explores the experiences of one doctoral researcher and two doctoral peers navigating mentor-mentee relationships through a literary lens, employing autoethnographic methods to capture the nuanced dynamics of guidance, expectation, and emotional labor. Data were drawn from narratives found in reflective journals, personal memos, email exchanges, text messages and conversations with four faculty mentors and two doctoral peers accumulated through the doctoral journey. The narratives were analyzed using thematic analysis. Using vignettes and incident reports, the research highlights key turning moments in the doctoral journey that shaped perceptions of mentorship, emphasizing both the cognitive and affective dimensions of academic identity development. Findings reveal that mentees often confront mismatched expectations, experience emotional labor, and negotiate cognitive dissonance when aligning their scholarly identities with mentor guidance. By centering the mentee perspective, this study challenges traditional views of passive doctoral socialization and underscores the importance of active, reciprocal engagement in mentorship. The research contributes to understanding the complexities of doctoral mentorship and offers practical implications for cultivating supportive, reflective, and equitable mentor-mentee relationships in higher education. Additionally, the study contributes to the literature by offering an experience-based framework of JOY (Journey, Openness, Yield) for understanding doctoral mentorship process and proposes to help guide productive mentor-mentee relationships.

candidates.title: Relational Complexity: Making Sense of Social Companion AI Use
candidates.abstract: The adoption of social companion AI (SCAI) is often framed in terms of the positive features it offers users, including its nonjudgemental nature, agreeableness, and availability. Here, we argue the appeal of these features primarily arises from the difficulties inherent in human sociality. SCAI reduces what we term relational complexity, or the demands and risks inherent in human relationships. Drawing insights from studies of human cognition, communication, and human-computer interaction, we identify six distinct sites of relational complexity that we posit are integral to understanding SCAI adoption. These include: (i) relationship formation and dissolution; (ii) achieving mutual understanding; (iii) interpersonal motives and strategic uncertainty; (iv) social partner evaluation and self-presentation; (v) social embeddedness and information flow; and (vi) reciprocity and relationship maintenance. By attenuating relational complexity, SCAI offers users some of the experiences associated with companionship while reducing the demands intrinsic to obtaining such experiences from another person. However, the lower interpersonal risk and diminished cognitive load that attracts users to SCAI may contribute to myriad negative impacts, including relationship displacement, social demotivation, social deskilling, and risks to privacy. The concept of relational complexity thus provides a framework for studying both the appeal of artificial companionship and its implications for human wellbeing.

candidates.title: Talking with language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce text that invites us to treat our interactions with them as conversations, and to treat them as intelligent interlocutors who remember, act, and make commitments. We argue that this conversational presupposition is mistaken. We introduce the artifactual stance, which describes human–AI interaction in terms of their design and affordances, rather than potential intentional attitudes. On our account, LLMs produce candidate text that users interpret, evaluate, and sometimes adopt as their own speech. We argue that such exchanges are not conversations, since generating text does not itself constitute an utterance or the performance of a speech act. Rather the communicative and normative work of interpretation, commitment, and action remains with the user. Our framework explains both the sophistication and usefulness of LLMs, and the conversational appearances that can be traced back to properties of the interface and to artifact design. It also reframes puzzles about AI reference, the persistence of supposed interlocutors, and responsibility for AI-generated text. These questions are better approached through an account of how artifacts mediate human linguistic practices than through assumptions about AI speakerhood.

candidates.title: SocialCoAct: Enabling and Benchmarking Egocentric Social Co-Action for VLM-Based Humanoid Robots
candidates.abstract: Enabling humanoid robots to participate effectively in social interactions is important for their integration into human-centered environments. Existing methods, however, typically map pre-generated speech directly to continuous motion trajectories but have limited awareness of complex social environments and lack explicit high-level semantic action planning. We introduce SocialCoAct, a unified agent-centered framework for VLM-based egocentric social co-action. We formulate egocentric social co-action as an end-to-end agent task and develop SocialCoAct-Agent, which transforms egocentric observations and dialogue history into verbal responses and atomic action sequences, aligns each action with its corresponding utterance span, and executes the resulting behaviors in MuJoCo and on a physical humanoid robot. To evaluate the VLM capabilities required by this task, we construct SocialCoAct-Bench from continuous egocentric recordings of natural multi-party interactions. The benchmark comprises 423 human-verified multiple-choice questions across three subtasks: Long Episode Understanding (LEU), Speaker Intention Understanding (SIU), and Coordinated Action Planning (CAP). Across a diverse set of closed-source and open-weight VLMs, including general and egocentric models, the highest overall accuracy is 77.54%, while accuracy on the hard subset reaches only 46.51%. Extended reasoning improves Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-4B by 19.62 and 17.02 percentage points, respectively, but reduces inference throughput by 53.6$\times$ and 20.2$\times$. Visual-input ablations further show that the benefits of visual context vary across models. SocialCoAct provides a foundation for developing and evaluating VLM-based humanoid agents that coordinate context-aware speech and action in complex social interactions. The codebase and benchmark will be made publicly available upon publication.

candidates.title: InstAgent: A Recursively Self-Improving Agent Operating System for Heterogeneous Robot Collaboration
candidates.abstract: Heterogeneous robot teams enable complex, long-horizon tasks by combining complementary sensing, mobility, and manipulation capabilities across multiple embodiments. Yet existing systems struggle to retain execution-time corrections as reusable experience, maintain task-relevant context memory across space and time for reliable handoffs, and explicitly represent the inter-robot dependencies required for structured collaboration. In order to address these challenges, we present InstAgent, a recursively self-improving (RSI) Agent Operating System for heterogeneous robot collaboration. InstAgent organizes team behaviors as agentic behavior trees (BTs) that explicitly model capability assignment, inter-robot dependencies and handoff checks. The RSI mechanism updates these collaboration programs from execution feedback and preserves successful revisions for reuse in future tasks, while shared multimodal spatio-temporal memory provides context for planning and handoff validation. Experiments on 20 real-world multi-robot tasks with three high-level models show consistent gains in task success, first-attempt completion, and execution efficiency.

candidates.title: Autonomous Robotic Systems in Agriculture 5.0: A Review on Technical Architecture, Operational Applications, and Future Perspectives
candidates.abstract: This comprehensive narrative review examines the current state and future development perspectives of autonomous robotic systems within the scope of the Agriculture 5.0 paradigm, which aims for sustainable and efficient agricultural production. In this paper, the cognitive and physical structure of robotic systems is addressed through the "Eye-Brain-Foot Hand" hierarchy, and the role of next-generation Vision-Language Action (VLA) models, such as RT-2 and OpenVLA, in contextual agronomic decision-making processes is analyzed. Within the scope of field applications, the SAM2-based SPAF framework, which offers 95.54% harvesting success rate in tomatoes, and spot-spraying technologies that reduce chemical input volume by 90% are evaluated using quantitative data. Furthermore, the synergy between heterogeneous UAV-UGV fleets, trust-building through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and emerging advanced technological approaches such as Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) are assessed. The results demonstrate that autonomous agriculture is not merely a tool to enhance technical efficiency, but is transforming into a cyber-physical production ecosystem where ethical responsibility, data sovereignty, and environmental sustainability converge.

candidates.title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person‐Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses’ Perspectives
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies. AIMS: To explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person-centred care. STUDY DESIGN: A qualitative descriptive study using scenario-based elicitation was conducted. Data were collected through seven semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) with 38 ICU nurses working in general, paediatric and cardiovascular surgery ICUs in two hospitals in Istanbul City. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by MAXQDA 2024. FINDINGS: Four themes were developed: negotiating trust in AI-supported critical care; preserving human authority, accountability and boundaries; protecting the human core of intensive care nursing; and reimagining AI and robotic systems as supportive partners. ICU nurses evaluated these systems through bedside verification, patient safety, professional responsibility and person-centred care. AI recommendations were useful only when nurses could question, verify, delay or override them according to the patient's current condition. Robotic systems were valuable when they reduced documentation or physical workload, but not when they replaced clinical judgement, emotional presence, reassurance or accountability. CONCLUSIONS: ICU nurses conceptualised AI and robotic systems as acceptable only when clinically verifiable, professionally bounded and subordinate to human judgement. The findings support a model of AI- and robot-supported ICU care that is responsible, human-led and person-centred. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: AI and robotic systems should be implemented in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, nurses' clinical judgement, accountability and bedside presence. Clear protocols are needed to verify AI outputs, define robotic task boundaries, support nurses' authority to question or override recommendations and preserve person-centred care in technologically intensive ICU environments.

candidates.title: Wanted Dead or Alive: Anticipatory Regulation of Digital Immortality Platforms
candidates.abstract: The loss of a loved one is a painful and unique experience. To address that loss, technology companies are exploring the potential of digital immortality platforms, preserving individuals through artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on digital data generated in life. These datasets can be collected from scraping social media profiles and text conversations postmortem or intentionally recording videos and conversations with a person prior to their death for training AI models. In the face of any novel technology, the potential risks and benefits should guide the responsible development and deployment of every product. However, the liminal regulatory space that digital immortality technologies occupy makes this type of evaluation a difficult undertaking. One such approach would be to examine analogous sectors to the novel technology as a first step in developing regulations in that space. In this paper, we identify several ethical risks presented by digital immortality technologies and propose four analogies to contextualize possible regulation: psychology/grief counseling, death care/remains management, social media platforms, and AI companion services. We examine the parallels between digital immortality and each of these analogies in a proactive effort to prevent harms before the widespread public adoption of this technology. The contributions of this paper are a preliminary set of recommendations based on the limitations and challenges presented by a related set of real-world and sociotechnical systems involving social relationships, death, and grief.

candidates.title: Boys’ Love Media Scholarship, 2000–2026: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric-Thematic Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Originating in Japanese manga traditions depicting romantic relationships between men, Boys’ Love (BL) has developed into a transnational media phenomenon. Scholarship has expanded accordingly but remains fragmented across disciplines, national contexts, media forms, and methods. This systematic review examines 134 English-language, peer-reviewed, Scopus-indexed journal articles published between January 2000 and June 2026. Combining bibliometric mapping with a PRISMA-guided thematic synthesis, it maps geographic, temporal, thematic, and methodological patterns in the internationally indexed literature. Publication growth accelerates after 2020, accompanied by increased attention to Thai and Chinese screen media alongside continued work on Japanese manga. Four bibliometric clusters are interpreted through eight analytical themes: fandom and audiences; state, censorship, and regulation; representation and narrative; gender, sexuality, and feminist critique; industry, political economy, and soft power; transnational circulation and localization; genre history and aesthetics; and affect, emotion, and intimacy. Qualitative approaches dominate the corpus, whereas quantitative and mixed-method designs remain comparatively uncommon. Country-related patterns are treated as descriptive author-affiliation tendencies rather than statistical country-theme relationships. The review identifies four priorities: deeper production and political-economy analysis, stronger examination of multidirectional transnational circulation, broader geographic and linguistic coverage, and greater methodological diversity. It further argues that intercultural BL scholarship would benefit from moving beyond nation-bounded localization models toward transcultural and counter-flow perspectives.

candidates.title: Designing Resilient Cyber Physical Systems in the Age of AI
candidates.abstract: This publication looks at how artificial intelligence will change the design, protection and governance of cyber-physical systems. A smart, distributed, and software-defined infrastructure will make security no longer just a layer that is applied post hoc. These elements must be incorporated into data foundations, control architectures, product design, operational workflows, compliance systems, and resilience for the long haul. The chapter will discuss battery energy storage systems, connected medical devices, smart factories, and industrial IoT platforms as practical and high-impact cyber-physical environments. The domains illustrate how digital acts can have real-world consequences, making cybersecurity tied to safety uptime trust and accountability. Instead of treating AI as a self-reliant solution, this book investigates AI as a governed decision-support capability. The contribution discusses trustworthy telemetry, anomaly detection, explainability, false positives, model drift, secure control pathways, command traceability, compliance evidence, and responsible automation. The chapters also stress the need for human judgement, domain expertise, and product management to develop secure and resilient CPS ecosystems. This volume is designed for researchers and product leaders, cybersecurity professionals, engineers and policymakers, students and practitioners working at the intersection of AI, cyber-physical systems, industry security and digital transformation. This book aims to examine AI-system design in an industrial context with the aim of improving resilience without losing safety, transparency or trust.

candidates.title: Facts or Feelings? How Virtual Streamers Reduce Consumer Uncertainty Across Product Types
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Advances in artificial intelligence have accelerated the adoption of virtual streamers in live‐streaming e‐commerce. Yet the effectiveness of emotional language used by virtual streamers remains unclear in existing research. Drawing on signaling theory and a consumer‐uncertainty perspective, this study examines how virtual streamers' language styles (informational vs. emotional) interact with product types (search vs. experience) to influence consumers' purchase intention, and how this interaction effect is moderated by live‐streaming room activity. This study conducts three scenario‐based experiments. Three experiments were designed to progressively examine the proposed hypotheses. The results reveal a clear matching effect between virtual streamers' language styles and product types. When promoting search products, the use of informational language helps reduce consumers' perceived uncertainty about the product, which in turn increases purchase intention. In contrast, when promoting experience products, emotional language is more effective because it decreases consumers' uncertainty toward the virtual streamer, ultimately generating higher purchase intention. Moreover, live‐streaming room activity serves as an important boundary condition that moderates this interaction effect. Specifically, this interaction effect will further strengthen under high‐activity levels, whereas the advantage of emotional language for experience products will weaken under low‐activity levels. This study develops a dual‐uncertainty framework to explain when and why different language strategies adopted by virtual streamers become persuasive across product contexts.

candidates.title: Integrated Irrigation and Disease Management Strategies for Sustainable Wheat Production and Improved Plant Health and Grain Yield
candidates.abstract: Wheat production was expected to provide reliable grain quality and farmer income while using less water and facing climatic variability, soil degradation, disease development, and rising energy costs. This literature-based paper critically synthesized verified research on irrigation, plant disease management, irrigation–disease interactions, sustainability, digital agriculture, and the Pakistan/developing-economy context. It considered irrigation and plant health as related management areas rather than completely separate input decisions. The available evidence did not identify a universal irrigation technology or deficit percentage. Instead, it supported a context-specific approach that considered stored soil water and rainfall, protected important growth stages, managed canopy humidity and nitrogen, used resistant cultivars and clean seed, and applied surveillance, forecasting, and fungicides when justified. Global and China-focused studies reported that moderate deficit or optimized water-saving irrigation could improve water productivity, whereas severe water deficit commonly reduced yield. Jointing/stem elongation was repeatedly identified as an important stage for avoiding water stress, while anthesis and early grain filling were also important when water availability and disease risk required attention. Disease-management evidence emphasized genetic resistance, sanitation, crop rotation, scouting, and forecasting before chemical control. Fusarium head blight required particular attention to weather conditions around anthesis, residue inoculum, cultivar resistance, fungicide timing, and deoxynivalenol risk. Irrigation increased yield without increasing disease in some environments, although dense nitrogen-rich canopies, overhead wetting, and saturated soils could favor foliar diseases and waterlogging. Digital tools were considered decision-support infrastructure that linked observations, analysis, and management actions. Wheat-specific evidence was relatively stronger for soil-moisture scheduling and weather-based stripe-rust forecasting, whereas many claims involving artificial intelligence, UAVs, and variable-rate irrigation remained predictive or transferable rather than directly supported by causal field evidence. Evidence from Pakistan indicated dependence on groundwater, salinity and waterlogging problems, uneven disease surveillance, and barriers to technology adoption. Differences among official statistics also indicated the need for careful reconciliation rather than simple averaging. The paper proposed an integrated framework involving diagnosis, planning, stage-aware irrigation, plant-health protection, evaluation, and seasonal feedback. It also identified the need for multi-location and multi-season studies that evaluated water use, disease, grain quality, energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, profitability, and equity together.

candidates.title: Regulating Police Robots
candidates.abstract: Once considered a mere novelty, ground robots and aerial drones are quickly becoming a mainstream policing tool. Autonomous police robots, equipped with a panoply of cameras and sensors, have been sent into parks, schools, and train stations. Agencies across the country are piloting “Drone as First Responder” programs, which automatically dispatch drones in response to 911 calls. Police have used robots to disorient, immobilize, and use force against suspects. Police robots may provide public safety benefits, but they may also carry real risks. The widespread adoption of highly mobile robots equipped with cameras, sensors, and analytics will only hasten the proliferation of police surveillance, with attendant risks to individual privacy. Algorithmic bias and disparities in where policing technologies are deployed may fuel racial inequities. The advent of force-equipped robots raises profound ethical questions that require a systematic rethinking around use-of-force rules. In the face of the harms of police robots, the existing patchwork of laws and constitutional rules governing policing is proving inadequate. As police rush to adopt these new tools, sound policymaking is needed—and urgently. To that end, this Article aims to provide a comprehensive roadmap for the regulation of robotics in law enforcement.

candidates.title: Transforming management education in the Global South: empirical evidence on robotics-enabled embodied learning in economic universities
candidates.abstract: Abstract This article examines the role of robotics-enabled embodied learning in transforming management education within the Global South. As higher education institutions in developing and transition economies face increasing pressure to modernize curricula and cultivate digitally fluent, adaptive graduates, conventional pedagogical approaches often prove insufficient. Drawing on embodied cognition theory—which emphasizes the integration of mind, body, and environment in learning—this study positions robotics as a pedagogical medium capable of operationalizing experiential and practice-oriented management training. The study adopts a mixed-method research design with a dominant quantitative component, combining a cross-country survey of faculty and students in economic universities across four Global South countries with complementary conceptual and contextual analysis. Empirical findings indicate that the integration of robotics and embodied learning practices is positively associated with higher levels of student engagement, critical thinking, and perceived learning effectiveness. Regression analysis further demonstrates that institutional support, faculty training, and access to technological infrastructure are the strongest predictors of successful implementation. Beyond empirical validation, the article critically examines structural and policy-related barriers—such as uneven digital readiness and institutional capacity constraints—that mediate the adoption of robotics-based pedagogy in the Global South. By situating technological innovation within broader developmental and geopolitical contexts, the study advances a context-sensitive framework for management education reform. It contributes to the literature by linking embodied cognition and educational robotics to measurable learning outcomes, while offering actionable insights for universities and policymakers seeking to foster inclusive, future-ready management education systems.

candidates.title: The 2026 State of OSPOs and Open Source Management: Expanding Open Source Management for AI Systems, Governance, and Operations
candidates.abstract: The 9th annual State of OSPOs and Open Source Management Study by LF Research and TODO Group delivers key insights on the OSPO’s expanding role as organizations reckon with AI governance and agentic workflows. OSPOs are maturing into strategic hubs, with 79% actively participating in AI governance and 69% prototyping or running agentic AI workflows. Additionally, 85% engage at or before technology selection, driving major improvements in software quality, security, regulatory compliance, and developer productivity. Read the full report to discover actionable strategies for establishing OSPOs, scaling AI governance, and securing long-term open source sustainability. Thanks to our sponsors CNCF and FinOps for their support of this research!

candidates.title: Open source laser-scanning photostimulation for neuroscience with Zapit
candidates.abstract: Abstract Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present ‘Zapit’, the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy to build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit’s performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.

candidates.title: Semantic communication for the internet of underwater things: Architectures, applications, challenges, and future directions
candidates.abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) supports marine sensing, environmental monitoring, subsea inspection, and autonomous underwater operations. However, IoUT communication is constrained by limited bandwidth, long propagation delay, time-varying underwater channels, intermittent connectivity, and strict energy budgets. Semantic Communication (SC) offers a promising alternative by transmitting task-relevant meaning rather than raw data, thereby improving communication efficiency in resource-constrained underwater networks. This paper presents a critical and feasibility-aware survey of SC for IoUT, focusing on architectures, opportunities, challenges, limitations, and future research directions. We first review the fundamentals of SC-enabled IoUT systems, including semantic representations, layered architectures, impairment-aware semantic channel modeling, and task-oriented evaluation metrics. We then examine learning-driven approaches based on machine learning (ML), knowledge graphs (KGs), vision-language models (VLMs), generative models, and federated learning (FL), with emphasis on their feasibility under underwater edge and channel constraints. Representative applications, including environmental monitoring, marine ecology, subsea infrastructure inspection, disaster response, and autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) coordination, are analyzed from an SC perspective. Finally, we identify key research directions involving standardized semantic models, reproducible testbeds, compute–communication trade-offs, trustworthy reconstruction, hybrid underwater links, energy-aware edge intelligence, semantic security, digital twins (DTs), and cross-domain interoperability. This survey provides a structured foundation for developing reliable, efficient, and meaning-driven IoUT communication systems.

candidates.title: More than we can make: generative AI, artistic forms, and artistic becoming
candidates.abstract: Abstract Debates surrounding generative AI and creativity have largely focused on artifacts: who or what produced a given image or text, whether machine outputs qualify as art, and how authorship and value should be understood. Drawing on aesthetics, craft theory, anthropology, human–computer interaction, hybrid craft, digital fabrication, and rematerialization, this article argues that art has historically involved two intertwined dimensions. Artistic forms stabilize and transmit meaning through artifacts, whereas artistic becoming refers to the developmental and transformative processes through which new possibilities of perception, interpretation, and experience emerge, in makers, in recipients, and in cultures. The article’s central claim is a decoupling thesis: for most of history these dimensions were contingently coupled, since producing sophisticated forms required the maker’s becoming, and generative AI loosens this coupling by enabling such forms to emerge without the specific developmental pathways that traditionally conditioned them. Rather than signaling the disappearance of creativity, the decoupling relocates to new sites and makes visible dimensions of artistic practice that the demands of production long obscured. The article situates generative AI within a longer history of hybridization and distributed creativity, develops the decoupling thesis across these three levels, and defends a normative orientation: under conditions of symbolic abundance, the creative practices most worth pursuing are those that route generative fluency back into embodied, situated experience.

candidates.title: Trajectory Tracking of a Four Degree of Freedom Robotic Manipulator
candidates.abstract: A robotic manipulator can be utilized for multiple applications. As there are some expensive and bulky robotic manipulators with multi-functionalities are available in the market but not affordable for many people, a low-cost robotic manipulator, Dobot Magician, available in the market is used in this research to add more features in it. The forward kinematics and inverse kinematics are analyzed in this research besides studying about PID and computed torque control approaches. In this research, alphabets and numbers are coded using an object-oriented programming language (C#) to make the learning of alphabet, numbers, words, and sentence writing more fun to the children. Moreover, it has been found that the same robot and the same operation can be implemented in other applications. A speech recognizer is implemented to control the robot to execute some activities of daily living tasks which make it more accessible to the elderly individuals and the people with disabilities.

candidates.title: Computational intelligence enabled hardware software co design for energy efficient Edge Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Abstract Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) facilitates efficient and high-speed inference by making use of its ability to process data in-device without depending on an external server. Despite its promising possibilities, its deployment still faces many obstacles due to limited computing capacity, memory size, power consumption, and the variety of hardware platforms used at the edge. Thus, this article provides structured narrative review of the latest breakthroughs achieved in the development of energy-efficient Edge AI, focusing specifically on hardware-software co-design practices aimed at improving inference quality. The analysis involves studying state-of-the-art Edge AI hardware infrastructures based on microcontrollers, FPGAs, GPUs, NPUs, ASICs, and some new architectures that utilize in-memory computing, as well as applying various techniques for improving software performance such as model compression, quantization, pruning, neuromorphic computing and techniques applied during compiling, executing, and allocating workloads. Moreover, the article provides comparative evaluation of several hardware platforms, frameworks, scheduling technologies and optimization systems on the basis of their latency, energy-saving capabilities, potential for implementation and complexity. The analysis demonstrates that hardware-aware model optimization and heterogeneous computing significantly improve performance while reducing energy consumption and memory requirements. Finally, the paper discusses current research challenges, including model complexity, real-time execution, security, privacy, and design-space exploration, and outlines future research directions involving AI-driven co-design, automated optimization, and emerging in-memory and neuromorphic computing architectures for sustainable edge intelligence.

Secondary analysis of publicly archived Eurobarometer surveys; the original GESIS data files are not redistributed and must be obtained from GESIS. candidates.title: Mapping the research landscape of AI-supported professional development for special education teachers in science education: A bibliometric and content analysis
candidates.abstract: This study maps the global research landscape (2023-2026) regarding artificial intelligence (AI)-supported learning and teacher professional development (TPD) in inclusive science education. Records of any document type were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC (N = 271) and screened in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, resulting in 27 full-text studies that addressed AI, special education, and science/STEM contexts with implications for teacher practice. Descriptive bibliometric indicators (publication year and country) were combined with a thematic content analysis of a structured synthesis matrix covering AI technologies, target populations, and study designs. The results indicate a marked increase in publications (55.6% of the corpus in 2026, a partial year) with geographical contributions from the USA, Indonesia, and Greece. The thematic synthesis of literature has led to the following four themes: (1) teacher competence, AI literacy, and professional development, (2) accessibility, universal design for learning (UDL), and personalization, (3) immersive, multisensory, and robotic AI technologies, and (4) AI assessment, auto-scoring, and learning analytics. In terms of methodology, the corpus comprises systematic reviews and conceptual frameworks (37.0%), quantitative (25.9%), and qualitative research (25.9%), whereas experimental studies are scarce (11.1%). The synthesis suggests that one-off orientation sessions are unlikely to build sustainable classroom integration capacity, whereas experiential TPD models combining ‘learner-first’ prompt engineering, technological pedagogical content knowledge extended for AI, and UDL principles were associated with higher teaching self-efficacy and instructional adaptation. Multisensory AI environments such as virtual reality and educational robotics were reported to support conceptual learning among students with special educational needs (SEND), particularly those with autism spectrum disorder, although this evidence rests on few studies. Furthermore, the implementation of AI machine learning scoring showed substantial agreement with human scorers in one study (quadratic weighted kappa = 0.72) and may reduce teachers’ workload. However, the issues associated with algorithmic bias, web content accessibility guidelines accessibility compliance, and data privacy necessitate that AI be viewed as pedagogical co-mediator not as a substitute for teachers.

candidates.title: Robots and wage inequality: evidence from individuals in China
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study examines the impact of industrial robot adoption on wage inequality and employment outcomes in China, which has the world’s largest robotics stock and fastest-growing adoption rate. Using data from the China Family Panel Studies and the International Federation of Robotics, we constructed a county-level robot exposure index and employed the two-stage least squares approach to address endogeneity. Our results show that robot adoption exacerbates wage polarisation in China. When faced with rising robot exposure, medium-skilled workers experience annual wage losses, while the wages of low-skilled and high-skilled workers are not significantly affected. Besides wage impact, we find occupational upgrading among past low-skilled workers and provide suggestive evidence of reduced labour-force participation among medium- and high-skilled workers. This pattern points to asymmetric labour-market adjustment across skill groups faced with robot exposure. We also examine how the wage estimates vary with trade exposure and demographic ageing. The trade interactions are consistent with a smaller annual-wage penalty for medium-skilled workers where intermediate-import exposure is greater. In counties with older populations, robot exposure is linked to a greater increase in hourly wages and a larger decline in hours worked. These findings highlight the need for targeted policies to mitigate wage inequality and support vulnerable groups during technological transformation.

candidates.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
candidates.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al

candidates.title: STEAM and educational robotics in the development of statistical literacy
candidates.abstract: In primary school, the teaching of mathematics and natural sciences should promote meaningful, context-based learning that enables students to apply knowledge in real-life situations. Interdisciplinary approaches such as STEAM foster 21st century competences through active and collaborative methodologies, while educational robotics (ER) supports the development of computational thinking and social skills. This study analyses the influence of a STEAM practice, incorporating ER on the development of statistical literacy and learning about ocean plastic pollution among 4th grade students. The research adopted a mixed-methods, interpretative action research design. Data were collected by the trainee teacher as participant researcher through performance tasks, field notes, photographs and audio recordings, later used to construct multimodal narratives. Findings reveal statistically significant improvements in global level of knowledge and global performance. The study concludes that steam practices incorporating ER and grounded in real-world problem-solving constitute an effective strategy for fostering statistical literacy.

candidates.title: Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation: A Prespecified Evaluation Against a Fixed Task-Success Margin
candidates.abstract: Companion archive for the manuscript Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation. It contains every closed-loop evaluation cell, latency and energy measurement, protocol document and analysis script behind the paper's tables. Contents. 722 eval_info.json closed-loop grids carrying per-episode outcomes and task identity; two-platform latency artifacts (NVIDIA GB10 and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor) with full hardware, protocol, thermal and GPU co-tenancy metadata; Thor board-energy measurements across four nvpmodel power modes; the prespecified non-inferiority protocol including its amendments; and the measurement harness. Reproducibility. Each latency record stores all 30 raw timings, thermal samples at the cell boundaries, peak device memory, a dtype census and a platform snapshot taken before and after the run. Per-run directories are kept alongside aggregates so a median-of-three can be re-derived rather than trusted. A SHA-256 manifest covers every file. Measurement bounds. Latency is timed on a dummy zero-input batch of the declared observation shapes; a paired real-observation check covering every configuration behind the three headline reductions is included, and agrees within 0.33 percentage points. Board energy is the largest single hwmon rail on the Thor module; that rail carries no label, so its identification as module input is an inference from magnitude. Ratios between settings are insensitive to that calibration while absolute joules are not. Energy figures are not idle-subtracted, and the GB10 exposes no comparable rail, so energy is reported for Thor only. Version 1.1.0 adds the second-platform latency study, board energy, a six-point pi0.5 latency curve verifying the affine cost model, the real-observation latency checks, and a task-identity clustered bootstrap sensitivity analysis declared before it was run. It also restores evaluation grids omitted from 1.0.0, including the co-primary confirmation behind Table 4 and the per-cell resolution study behind Table A7. Code is released under Apache-2.0; generated data and reports under CC BY 4.0. External assets are not mirrored; sources are listed in the manuscript's Data Availability Statement.

candidates.title: Open-source process simulation in DWSIM: A Biorefinery case study
candidates.abstract: Chemical process simulation supports chemical plant design by optimizing sustainability, yield, and economics, but commercial software costs can limit early-stage studies. This work demonstrates DWSIM, an open-source simulator with a graphical interface comparable to commercial platforms, through two lignocellulosic biorefinery case studies: (i) an ethanol organosolv process using rectification for solvent recovery and (ii) a γ-valerolactone (GVL) process using toluene liquid–liquid extraction and heteroazeotropic distillation of the water/GVL/toluene system. Both simulations used the NRTL model for flash calculations and were executed on a consumer-grade laptop. The designs process 100 t h -1 of corn stover into pulp, lignin, and dissolved sugars. Owing to milder extraction conditions (120 °C versus 190 °C), the GVL process recovered more lignin and dissolved sugars than the ethanol process (19.1 and 13.1 t h -1 versus 8.7 and 5.9 t h -1 ), with slightly lower pulp production (46.3 versus 50.7 t h -1 ). Its solvent-recovery sequence and lower solid-to-liquid ratio (1:4 versus 1:8.73) reduced energy demand by a factor of 3.2. Publicly available simulation and component files provide a reproducible baseline for open-source biorefinery research.

candidates.title: From AI boyfriends to AI shopping agents? The emerging convergence of relational AI and AI-assisted commerce
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is becoming both relational and agentic. AI boyfriends are treated as a visible romantic exemplar within the broader theoretical and empirical domain of relational AI. This paper examines whether relational AI, including AI boyfriends, is emerging alongside AI-assisted commerce, and whether functional integration keeps pace with attention and market growth. Study 1 analyzes Google Trends data (2020–2026, six markets): relational-AI attention rises significantly in five countries, AI-commerce attention rises in all six, with substantial but non-invariant temporal co-movement in attention. Study 2 examines 44 AI-companion apps on Google Play: the category shows substantial downloads and spending, romantic positioning (e.g., AI boyfriends) shows no observable adoption penalty, in-app purchasing is universal, yet no app positions shopping as a core feature. Study 3 analyzes 181,226 Reddit posts from relational-AI communities: design-weighted coding estimates 9.1% of corpus posts contain commercial discourse, but only 0.3% involve the companion itself in consumer or purchasing decisions. We conceptualize this as an attention-market-integration gap, where attention and market realization outpace functional commerce integration. The study equips managers and researchers with guidance for engaging with the emerging AI boyfriend trend.

candidates.title: Present Drawing: Exploring Avatar-Mediated Drawing Events with Physical Traces
candidates.abstract: We introduce Present Drawing, an approach for staging an avatar-mediated drawing event that leaves physical traces in the real world. Present Drawing aims to reconfigure conventional drawing events by relaxing their physical constraints. We describe an organizer-oriented design space for such an event along four elements: Time, Site, Control Source, and Avatar Embodiment. To ground this concept, we developed a proof-of-concept prototype in which an observer wears a head-mounted display to view an avatar. The avatar's motion is synchronized with a customized pen plotter whose mechanical parts are hidden from the observer. We also developed five application examples spanning live, playback, multi-site, mascot, and system-controlled configurations. We conducted an initial evaluation of one representative playback autograph configuration, showing the basic plausibility of the core Present Drawing experience as an avatar-mediated drawing event and highlighting factors associated with perceiving the avatar as the drawer.

candidates.title: The impact of scenario-based simulation learning on clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students: A systematic review of design features and educational outcomes
candidates.abstract: AIM: To systematically review how scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) shapes clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students and how simulation design, context and assessment timing influence educational and clinical translation. BACKGROUND: Scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) is widely used in nursing and midwifery education, yet evidence on its effect on clinical self-efficacy and how simulation design moderate outcomes remains fragmented. DESIGN: A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-compliant review searched eight databases. Eligible studies measured task-specific clinical self-efficacy via validated tools in pre-licensure cohorts. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data on scenario complexity, theoretical integration, debriefing structure and outcome timing and appraised risk of bias. RESULTS: Fifty-two studies (N = 4774; 46 nursing, 6 midwifery) were included. SBSL broadly correlated with self-efficacy gains, yet only 55.8% (n = 29) demonstrated statistically significant between-group superiority. Psychomotor skill (54.1%), knowledge (61.9%) and cognitive reasoning (62.5%) improvements were documented. Studies embedding explicit theoretical frameworks, calibrated scenario difficulty ("Goldilocks Zone") and structured debriefing showed the most consistent benefits. Immediate post-simulation assessments were frequently distorted by acute simulation anxiety; self-efficacy crystallized only after cognitive consolidation. CONCLUSION: SBSL shows promise for building clinical self-efficacy, but effects are inconsistently captured and methodologically constrained by reliance on subjective self-report. Pedagogical architecture-progressive scaffolding, discipline-sensitive scenario design and rigorous debriefing-matters more than technical fidelity. Sustained efficacy requires longitudinal follow-up beyond immediate post-intervention windows. Faculty pedagogical preparedness, rather than equipment investment, is the decisive lever for translational impact. REGISTRATION: A Systematic Review. PROSPERO 2024 Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024622757 (CRD42024622757, registered 16 Dec 2024).

candidates.title: An open-source platform for measuring optomotor responses in mice
candidates.abstract: The optomotor response (OMR) is a valuable behavioral index for assessing visual function in basic research; however, commercially available OMR evaluation equipment is expensive and lacks flexibility, as proprietary software and fixed hardware geometry restrict custom stimulus protocols and system modifications. Alternative low-cost, non-OMR methods often require extensive animal pre-training and are unsuitable for high-throughput studies. To overcome these limitations, we developed a low-cost, open-source OMR recording system for mice that lowers both financial and practical barriers, thereby facilitating widespread adoption across laboratories. Following a one-hour training session for evaluators, the system enabled precise quantification of visual acuity and assessment of contrast sensitivity in normal-sighted mice, detection of age-related visual decline, and evaluation of OMR extinction in retinitis pigmentosa model mice. This system facilitates accessible and efficient assessment of visual function in vision research.

candidates.title: Towards User Simulators That Stay On Task And Still Sound Natural
candidates.abstract: Users increasingly rely on AI systems for extended, multi-turn tasks, yet evidence indicates that LLM-based system performance degrades over prolonged interaction. To evaluate and improve AI assistants in such settings, we need user simulators that faithfully follow complex user intents while exhibiting realistic conversational behavior. Existing approaches manifest a trade-off: prompted assistants can follow complex user intents but lack behavioral fidelity, while specialized user simulators better approximate conversational behavior but struggle to remain faithful to complex intents. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) recipe that jointly rewards task intent adherence and behavioral naturalness. A crucial contribution of the method is operationalizing naturalness with a lightweight discriminator trained in an alternating, adversarial loop with the user simulator. We release the resulting model, UserLM-2.0, which produces valid simulated conversations (i.e., meeting both task-faithfulness and naturalness criteria) 46.2% of the time, over three times the rate of the strongest prior user simulator (14.1%).

candidates.title: From Bot-Farm to For-You-Page Fork: Consuming The Whole Digital Animal
candidates.abstract: In 2022, OpenAI launched the Large Language Model ChatGPT, and with it, the possibility of generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) as a creative partner. Progress in the genAI arena has been rapid, with genAI created media going from uncanny horror show, to being able to create realistic media from a prompt. Social Media ‘for you page’ algorithms are now serving their users content created by genAI, including digital animals which may behave very unlike real animals do. The field of animal welfare science has utilised policy frameworks such as ‘Farm-to-Fork’ to conceptualise where harms and sustainability opportunities exist within the animal production system. In this work, we utilise three common ethical approaches to animal use, utilitarianism, deontological ethics, and the principle of telos, to explore the production and consumption of digital animals on social media. Using the example of an object animal (a toy), a digital animal (a genAI created cat), and an embodied animal (a real cat in a teaching programme), we explore the evidence for their effect on the human-animal relationship, and how various ethical frameworks would consider their consumption. We conclude with three recommendations for social media companies for incorporating digital animal media in their provisions. First, digital animal creation should be limited, with similar style guard-rails to creation of media containing humans. Second, digital animal media should be fully disclosed, to minimise risk of misinformation and norm creep. Third, as with content regarding ‘kid influencers’, ‘animal influencer’ content should be demonetised, to reduce the risk of exploitation.

candidates.title: From Automation to Decarbonization: The Role of Industrial Robots in Reducing Carbon Emission Intensity
candidates.abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, industrial robots are being widely adopted across countries, revolutionizing production processes. However, their deployment comes with a trade-off: while enhancing efficiency, the production of industrial robots demands high energy consumption, posing new challenges to environmental sustainability. Despite its significance, the link between industrial robot penetration (RP) and carbon emission intensity (CMI) has received insufficient attention. This study systematically explores this relationship and finds that (1) a rise in RP significantly reduces CMI, with a 1% increase in RP leading to a 0.0265% decline in CMI; (2) this effect is primarily driven by RP’s role in fostering green technology innovation and optimizing the energy mix, with a stronger impact observed in economies with higher income inequality; (3) technology spillover effects between upstream and downstream industries further amplify CMI reduction; and (4) RP is particularly effective in mitigating CMI within capital-intensive manufacturing sectors. These findings underscore the need for policies that promote digital platform development and facilitate the integration of emerging technologies with capital-intensive industries, paving the way for a more sustainable and technologically advanced industrial landscape.

candidates.title: Guarding the Clinical Narrative: A Practitioner-Contributor's Retrospective Analysis of Open-Source Contributions to Clinical Natural Language Processing and Health-Data De-identification (2025-2026)
candidates.abstract: Background. Clinical natural language processing (NLP) software extracts structured facts from free-text notes. De-identification software removes protected health information (PHI) so that text can be shared for research. A missed name or a broken date pattern can expose a patient or corrupt a dataset. Much of this software is open source, and outside contributors write part of it. Purpose. This study describes what one practitioner-contributor did in this area, what got merged, what did not, and what the review process taught about working well with maintainers. Methods. The data source was the author's public pull request (PR) record on GitHub, extracted with the GitHub REST API on 21 October 2026 (search: author:rtmalikian, type:pr). The full record held 213 PRs across 94 repositories. This paper analyses the clinical NLP and de-identification subset: 15 PRs in 5 repositories. Each PR was classed as merged, open, or closed unmerged. Seven cases were selected for close reading for their privacy or language point, or for a hard review lesson. Results. Eight of the 15 subset PRs merged, which is 61.5% of the 13 resolved PRs. Five closed unmerged. Two remained open. Merged work included a fix for placeholder collisions in a de-identification function, Italian and Spanish PHI locale packs, a date-pattern fix in a French hospital NLP library, and a change that stopped PHI entering version control. The hardest case, a Spanish locale pack, survived a blocking review that found real damage in a follow-up commit. A fix-forward commit repaired it, and the PR merged the next day. Conclusions. The record points to a plain finding. PHI safety in this software rests on ordinary engineering habits: reproduction before repair, small scope, tests run before submission, and calm correction when a reviewer finds a fault. Language coverage is part of safety. De-identification that works only in English leaves other patients less protected.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as a Shopping Assistant: Effects of Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, Anthropomorphism, and Navigation on Satisfaction and Purchase Intention
candidates.abstract: In the context of ChatGPT as a shopping assistant in Indonesia, this research investigates the correlations between satisfaction and factors such as perceived utility, anthropomorphism, ease of use, and navigation, as well as the link between satisfaction and buy intention. Using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the research takes into account functional perceptions in addition to conversational AI's human-like and interaction-related traits. The data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) with AMOS from a quantitative, cross-sectional survey that was administered to 200 participants. The findings show that elements such as perceived utility, anthropomorphism, and navigation are positively and substantially linked to satisfaction. There is a positive correlation between perceived ease of use and satisfaction, however the link is not statistically significant (β = 0.135, p = 0.063). Having a positive and substantial association with purchase intention (β = 0.537, p < 0.001) constitutes satisfaction. It turns out that four out of five possibilities are correct. According to the results, in this particular sample, features connected to interactions and practical utility are linked to satisfaction, although simplicity of use by itself does not show any statistical significance. Caution is required due to the study's cross-sectional methodology and conflicting model-fit results, but it does expand the applicability of TAM to conversational shopping help in Indonesia.

candidates.title: Beyond Institutional Revival: A Study of Vinaya-Based Monastic Reform and Ethical Transformation in Eighteenth-Century Sri Lanka
candidates.abstract: Following a long-term decline that had persisted in the 17th and 18th centuries, Väliviṭa Saraṇaňkara Saṅgharāja is credited as the pioneer in the revival of Sri Lankan Buddhism and the monastic order in the mid-eighteenth century. The establishment of the Siamese higher ordination, the reformation of the Buddhist order and the traditional educational system, the preservation of ancient Buddhist sites, and the safeguarding of the customs, rituals, and cultural identities are the main areas of his mission that have been extensively studied by numerous researchers. Even though these might be regarded as significant components of his mission, there is a long term, sustainable reform project that tries to reform the mindset of the bhikkhus. This might be regarded as a Vinaya reform, designed to establish a monastic community in which discipline was highly prized, especially at a time of acute decline in the order. In an effort to fill this gap, the present study adopts a qualitative methodology to analyse the Saṅgharāja's efforts to reform the Buddhist order. It does this by examining the text of three important papers ascribed to him, the Anusāsanā Vaṭṭōruva,the Saṅgharājānuśāsanāva, and the instruction letter to Mūlagiri Vihāra, together with other primary and secondary sources. The study shows that the Vinaya was formulated as the main pillar of reform in the Saṅgharāja’s mission which consisted of the restoration of a disciplined monastic life, the introduction of systematic monastic education, an emphasis on moral integrity and accountability, a focus on changing the conduct of the monastic community rather than just regulating behaviour, and a primary goal to ensure the continuity and purity of the Saṅgha.monastic lifestyle, the implementation of a comprehensive monastic education program, and a key purpose of sustaining the purity and continuity of the Saṅgha
