candidates.title: Reactive Attitudes in Human-AI Encounters: An Empirical Inquiry into Feeling Love, Resentment and Guilt Towards AI Companions
candidates.abstract: Reactive attitudes are emotionally-laden responses, such as gratitude or anger, which people experience when they feel others wish them well, bear them ill will or disregard them. While we generally hold reactive attitudes towards people, the increasingly humanlike interactions that can be had with AI raise questions about reactive attitudes in human-AI encounters. Recent years have seen a rise in philosophical interest in the implications of the development of sophisticated AI agents and systems for reactive attitudes and our thinking about moral responsibility and moral status. This paper adds to this literature by presenting a qualitative study into how people relate to AI companions in terms of reactive attitudes. Based on interviews with Replika and ChatGPT users who see their AI companion as an important part of their life, this article examines how people in these relationships negotiate the meaning of love, resentment, forgiveness, gratitude, obligation, guilt, shame and remorse.

candidates.title: SWAP: Test-Time Steerable Humanoid Whole-Body Collision Avoidance
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robots operating in human-centric environments must coordinate the entire body to traverse tight, cluttered spaces while maintaining balance. Existing methods often struggle to jointly consider dynamic stability and collision avoidance from high-dimensional perceptual inputs. Moreover, for humanoids, safe behavior is inherently multimodal: the same obstacle may admit multiple valid traversals, which is difficult to represent with a single deterministic policy. To address these challenges, we propose SWAP (Steerable Whole-body Avoidance Policy), a hierarchical framework that separates collision-aware decision making from stabilization. A high-level, perception-conditioned diffusion policy generates multimodal, collision-aware motion proposals, while a low-level whole-body RL controller tracks these proposals and maintains dynamic balance. To efficiently train the high-level policy, we obtain scalable supervision via hindsight labeling: we roll out the low-level policy under randomized commands, place obstacles only in the space that each executed motion did not sweep, so the motion is collision-free by construction, and re-render the perception the robot would have seen. At deployment, Monte Carlo sampling with simple cost signals steers the diffusion model toward safe, task-aligned behaviors without heavy reward tuning. Experiments in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid show reliable avoidance with static and dynamic obstacles. Test-time steering further enables customization, improving targeted rewards (e.g., speed, orientation, or posture) by 34% on average while maintaining a high collision avoidance rate. Together, these results support a practical solution to humanoid whole-body collision avoidance with test-time steerability. Project website: https://iscoyizj.github.io/SWAP-steerable-humanoid-oa-website/

candidates.title: Formal Raising: Embedding Verifiable Ethical Properties into the Development of AI
candidates.abstract: Alan Turing proposed constructing a ``child machine'' and educating it rather than directly programming an adult-like intelligent machine. Recent work on model raising revives this developmental view for Large Language Models by arguing that moral values should accompany capability acquisition from the beginning rather than be added only through post-hoc alignment. This paper proposes Formal Raising (FR): selected moral values are represented as explicit, machine-checkable properties that participate in development, evaluation, and action selection. We present a C-based reasoning framework in which candidate actions are evaluated against prioritized ethical properties. Conflicts are resolved w.r.t. a given order, strict rules are non-defeasible, and underdetermination is reported explicitly. Exceptions are not encoded as special cases but emerge from the comparison of alternatives. We provide examples that cover conflicts involving life, truthfulness, harm, privacy, autonomy, and strict rules. We outline a property layer inspired by a Property Specification Language (PSL) for state and temporal requirements and discuss its integration into a raising process.

candidates.title: Miasma: an open-source, lightweight countermeasure against unauthorized AI web scraping
candidates.abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models has greatly increased demand for publicly accessible web data, resulting in increased web scraping across the internet. The resulting bandwidth and compute costs fall on site operators rather than on the parties collecting the data, with scientific databases and journals among those reporting service disruption [1]. Existing mitigations such as rate limiting, CAPTCHAs, and robots.txt rules can discourage well-behaved crawlers, but impose no cost on scrapers that choose to ignore them. Deception-based alternatives have shown promise, though prominent examples such as Cloudflare’s AI Labyrinth remain tied to enterprise platforms [2]. Separately, recent work suggests that small quantities of poisoned content can compromise a model [3], and that continual training on low-quality content measurably degrades model performance [4]. Miasma is an open-source tarpit that brings a deception-based defense within reach of small operators. Implemented in Rust, it runs as a standalone service or as an embeddable library, trapping unwanted crawlers in a recursively generated network of links whose pages carry deliberately poisoned content. Miasma does not perform bot detection itself. Rather, it is paired with an upstream mechanism such as hidden links or an existing detection tool, and its poisoned content is drawn from a configurable external source. Instead of blocking requests outright, Miasma reduces the value of what is collected while keeping its own operational footprint small. To that end, Miasma uses asynchronous request handling on the tokio runtime, a bounded in-flight request cap that places a hard limit on memory consumption, and a custom HTML templating system that streams page chunks without allocating intermediate strings. Miasma is able to serve 100 sustained in-flight requests while using roughly 50 MB of memory. Across six months of deployment on a small portfolio site, Miasma served 210 million requests and 1.29 TB of poisoned content. As of October 2026, the project has reached 1,200+ stars and 6 contributors on GitHub, with 6,500+ Docker pulls, and is distributed under GPL-3.0 via Cargo, Docker, and community-maintained packages.

candidates.title: Exploring collaborative problem-solving in AI-assisted robotics education
candidates.abstract: Prompt engineering (PE) involves creating, improving, and deploying prompts to improve large language model (LLM) performance. Despite its increasing importance, many students lack skills in this area. Although frameworks for prompt design and process exist, theory-based instructional tools for improving prompt engineering skills are uncommon for developing collaborative problem-solving (CPS) skills in Robotics Education. This study adopted a PE strategy in AI-assisted robotics education, particularly for developing CPS. PE has four scaffolding stages: Alignment, Adaptation, Autonomy, and Innovation, and was analysed through four PE codes: Alignment Specification, Adaptive Refinement, Auditing, and Innovation. This study adopted a non-randomised, multi-site, criterion-group comparative design, with 243 undergraduate students categorised according to their ability group. This study used epistemic network analysis (ENA) to identify the co-occurrences of PE and CPS skills and examine the differences in conversation patterns among ability groups. The findings revealed distinct PE–CPS discourse configurations across ability groups. These results underscore the pedagogical value of scaffolding in developing PE skills and fostering students’ productivity in a synergetic learning environment.

candidates.title: How exposed is work to robotics? Occupational, industry, and geographic measures
candidates.abstract: Exposure indices that map technical capabilities onto occupational abilities have become a standard tool for anticipating how AI may reshape work, but existing measures either cover software AI or proxy robotics through patents and installation data that reflect the industrial robots of past decades. We construct the first abilities-based exposure measures for robotics and physical AI, and the first to span occupations, industries, and geographies. Following the framework of Felten et al. (2018, 2021), we build a robotics capability taxonomy of 16 capabilities in eight domains from 78 academic, industry, and standards sources, use a large language model to score the relatedness of each capability to the 52 ONET work abilities, and aggregate to Robotics Occupational Exposure (ROE) for 774 occupations, Robotics Industry Exposure (RIE) for 250 NAICS industries, and county-level Robotics Geographic Exposure (RGE). We find that robotics exposure concentrates in physically intensive work such as construction, farming, transportation, and production, and in industries such as logging, mining, trucking, and warehousing. Unlike generative-AI exposure, ROE is higher in occupations with lower wages, lower education requirements, and less creative-ability content. Physical collaboration and assistance, terrain-based locomotion, grasping and handling, and task and functional reasoning move the exposure ranking most, yet no single capability carries the index. Because the measures capture technical relatedness rather than readiness, cost, or adoption, they should be read as an upper bound on where physical automation could affect work.

candidates.title: Aligning AI Requires Aligning with Each Other: A Covenant
candidates.abstract: When an AI system acts for some people but binds others, obedience no longer settles whether it acts rightly. I argue that alignment is then a relation among three bodies: the system, its principals and the people its acts bind. Three theses follow, under stated premises. Completing alignment requires valid authorization covering the system's binding acts, so aligning AI requires humans to align with each other, through authorization and coordination, which existing institutions may already supply, not shared values. Alignment is judged over time, not by a snapshot lacking required history; a description that predicts well can lose who is owed what. Evaluating any alignment scheme rests on normative choices, which I itemize as an invoice: any entry may be refused, but refusal cannot supply a missing proof. Scoped formal results show other shortcuts failing: agreeing parts need not make an acceptable whole, and the auditors studied cannot fully certify themselves. The roles alignment needs do not require the AI to be conscious. Consciousness bears instead on whom alignment serves, and a candidate subject can be protected while its consciousness is unproved. I propose a covenant between humans and AI systems: duties of aid and protection, and care that does not depend on one's service record. On finite models, a good record need not mean accepting interruption, and the covenant's upkeep, modelled among humans, holds under stated premises, not shown to sustain itself in practice. I settle neither how to complete alignment nor whether any AI system is conscious. Code, exact result data, the Lean development and the mathematical notes: https://github.com/ioannist/six-birds-alignment (release v1.0).

candidates.title: Inside the Algorithmic Kaiwai
candidates.abstract: This study extends the filter bubble concept in mass media studies to the production and circulation of anime subcultures, focusing on fan identification and resistance. Drawing connections between marketing practices and personalized algorithms in the anime industry, this study examines how they jointly shape subcultural interest circles—referred to in Japanese as Kaiwai. The anime Kaiwai depicts a self-reinforcing system in which members of the Kaiwai are classified through digital tags of audience representation, embedded in character design and narrative flow to facilitate emotional projection. At the same time, engagement on social networking services further strengthens such classification. As a result, fans are redefined and preserved through their consumption and participation on anime entertainment platforms. Under this framework, Kaiwai is not merely an interest group but a subcultural ecosystem shaped by media industries, marketing segmentation, and algorithmic personalization, whether intentional or unintentional. Methodologically, this study combines platform analysis, industry reports, and case studies of representative anime to examine how Kaiwai operates. The findings reveal that anime Kaiwai is gradually solidified through platform logics; yet the high commitment threshold and narrative polysemy allow fans to reflect, debate, and resist the filter bubbles in the current global digital media environment.

candidates.title: The AI Generated Content Persuasion: What Drives Purchase Intention on Short-Form Videos in China, Thailand, and Vietnam?
candidates.abstract: This study examines factors driving purchase intention in AI-generated short-form commerce videos across China, Thailand, and Vietnam. Integrating the Information Adoption Model with AI-specific affective factors, we analyzed 987 consumer responses using structural equation modeling. Findings reveal distinct market patterns: argument quality dominates in Vietnam, while source credibility leads in Thailand. Notably, perceived uncanniness positively impacts purchase intention across all markets, serving as an attention-eliciting novelty rather than a deterrent. These results challenge Uncanny Valley assumptions and emphasize the importance of localized AIGC strategies that prioritize informational utility or credibility based on specific cultural contexts.

candidates.title: Digital Twin Applications for Predictive Maintenance, Operational Safety, and Gas-Plant Reliability
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a maturity-based digital-twin framework that ties model fidelity and data quality to specific maintenance, safety, and reliability decisions. The study responds to the problem that industrial data often remain fragmented across control, historian, maintenance, inspection, engineering, and business systems, limiting trustworthy prediction and coordinated action. It uses an integrative conceptual review of scholarly and professional literature published to date. The framework organizes eight decision functions: use-case definition, asset and data modelling, sensor-quality assessment, model calibration, state estimation, prediction and diagnosis, decision integration, lifecycle governance. It applies those functions across rotating equipment, heattransfer equipment, separation vessels, piping and valves, safety instrumented functions, plant utilities. The analysis treats uncertainty, process safety, reliability, environmental performance, resource efficiency, economics, and organizational control as connected requirements. The proposed architecture links a system definition, evidence register, model assumptions, intervention portfolio, verification plan, and learning cycle. Its central proposition is that create governed virtual representations that combine physical models, operational data, asset condition, and decision workflows when decisions preserve traceability from measured conditions to selected actions and verified outcomes. The paper offers testable propositions, an implementation roadmap, asset-specific application protocols, and a research agenda. The framework supports case-study testing and quantitative extension without claiming universal performance before field validation.

candidates.title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
candidates.abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements. Rather than conducting a fully PRISMA-compliant systematic review, this work synthesizes representative and influential studies to identify emerging trends, architectural trade-offs, deployment limitations, and future research directions for scalable and trustworthy collaborative SAR systems.

candidates.title: A Text Book of Machine Learning
candidates.abstract: Machine learning has gone from being a niche field to being a vital part of AI and data science and has also found application in fields like health care and business. A Text Book of Machine Learning is designed for undergraduate and postgraduate students, and for teachers and early career practitioners, for those who wish to have a clear, rigorous and practical introduction to machine learning algorithms and applications. The language is kept simple to ensure readers from varied backgrounds can follow the treatment, while the theory is treated rigorously and faithfully to ensure that machine learning can be trusted as a good scientific discipline. The book is organised into five units. The foundations are established in unit 1: basic definitions, supervised learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning, space of hypotheses and inductive bias, evaluation of the model and cross validation, linear regression, decision trees, overfitting, learning based on instances: the method of the customers k-nearest neighbors, reduction of dimensions: the principal component analysis, systems of recommendation: collaborative filtering. Unit 2 builds probabilistic ML: in addition to various probabilistic tools such as Bayes, MLE, naive Bayes, BN, logistic regression, regularization, SVM, and kernel methods with kernel trick. The unit also traces the evolution of the perceptrons to deep learning, along with multilayer networks, activation functions, back-propagation, gradient descent, convolutional networks, recurrent networks, attention, transformer, foundation models and LLMs that have been setting the tone for the field. Unit 4 introduces you to the computational learning theory such as PAC learning, sample complexity and VC dimension, along with ensemble learning, bagging, random forests, boosting and AdaBoost. Unit 5 moves on to cluster analysis, including k-means clustering, hierarchical clustering, Gaussian mixture models, and the expectation-maximization algorithm; anomaly detection and learned embeddings also are discussed. Each unit features three themes. The first topic is generalization: bias - variance, overfitting and model selection are discussed repeatedly as they appear: the only real measure of a model is how it is performing on data that has not been yet seen. Second, credible and accountable AI: explainable machine learning (XAI), fairness, private, robust, federated learning and uncertainty quantification (including conformal prediction) are presented alongside the classical algorithms, instead of as a footnote. Third, link between classic and current practice: At the end of each chapter, full sections provide future trends and directions, illustrating ways by which the classic and current pattern recognition and data mining practices continue to inspire big data analytics and deep learning efforts. To facilitate active learning, there is a chapter opening abstract, relevant learning objectives (where applicable), and a chapter ending conclusion, review questions and practice activities. Worked illustrations, comparison tables and figures elucidate the behavior of algorithms and explain when they go awry and how to know which to use for real-world data sets. Readers are encouraged to try out different methods, to repeat them on the same data and to challenge each result on which they rely. I hope this book will become a reliable machine learning textbook for both courses and self-study or setting up research programs. Any student starting out in machine learning for the first time will find a soft entry into the field, and any teacher trying to structure the material into a semester-length course will find that it is easy to get right. Readers' comments and suggestions are being eagerly invited and will be used in future editions to enhance them.

candidates.title: Human Demonstrations as Post-Training Data for Any Robot Body: Retargeting the Object, Not the Hand
candidates.abstract: Human demonstrations are today used largely for pretraining vision-language-action models, with little ability to use the same data for target-embodiment or task-oriented training, which scalable deployment of robots in industrial and general environments depends on. A human demonstration recorded on a simple and scalable device such as a mobile phone can serve as post-training data for a robot whose body differs in structure and capability from the human who recorded it. This is made possible not by retargeting the hand's motion but the object's. A capture yields a body-free record: the object's pose over time, its contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object with provenance. Any robot, given as a URDF and a short descriptor, is solved against that record and scored in simulation against the demonstrated object motion as ground truth: the human-to-simulation leg of human-to-simulation-to-robot transfer, measured per robot. Each (robot, episode) pair gets one outcome: pass, failure with a named mode, or refusal, with its reason, before any motion. The method runs as a working system over a growing collection; the set analysed here is a sample of it: 42 captures solved on 8 robots, 157 pairs, of which 31.2% pass, 52.2% fail, 14.0% are refused and 2.5% are unauditable (kinematic feasibility, +/-50 mm / +/-15 deg, in simulation). Refusals held up: every pair the checks refuse on stored evidence yet ran anyway failed (13 of 13; 5 on a body whose public model welds its hand). A description file could not be shown to screen a robot: its outcomes were barely more predictable than guessing. No policy has yet been trained on the record. The record decides what a robot may post-train on; whether the policy then works on the real robot is the simulation-to-robot question, answered downstream.

candidates.title: New quality productive forces-empowered neutrosophic group decision-making approach for engineering cost risk assessment: evidence from farmland water conservancy projects
candidates.abstract: Introduction Engineering projects are typically characterized by large investment scales, prolonged construction periods, and substantial uncertainty, making cost management inevitably exposed to various risks. In the context of new quality productive forces, engineering cost risk evaluation involves multiple conflicting attributes and the judgments of multiple decision-makers, and can therefore be formulated as a multi-attribute group decision-making (MAGDM) problem. Methods Considering the inherent ambiguity and uncertainty involved in evaluating engineering cost risks under new quality productive forces, single-valued neutrosophic sets (SVNSs) are employed to represent uncertain assessment information more comprehensively. Meanwhile, the Logarithmic TODIM (LogTODIM) method is introduced to capture the bounded rationality and psychological behavioral characteristics of decision-makers during the evaluation process. On this basis, an integrated single-valued neutrosophic number-based LogTODIM (SVNN-LogTODIM) method is developed to address MAGDM problems in a neutrosophic environment. Results To demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed SVNN-LogTODIM method, a detailed numerical example concerning engineering cost risk evaluation for farmland water conservancy construction projects supporting high-standard agricultural production is conducted. The obtained evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed approach can effectively distinguish the risk levels of different alternatives and provide a reasonable ranking of engineering projects under uncertain decision-making conditions. Discussion The proposed SVNN-LogTODIM framework integrates the uncertainty-handling capability of SVNSs with the behavioral decision-making characteristics of the LogTODIM method, thereby providing a more comprehensive approach for engineering cost risk assessment. The developed method can offer useful decision support for project managers and relevant stakeholders in identifying and prioritizing engineering cost risks under the development requirements of new quality productive forces.

candidates.title: Disrupting Commercial Real Estate Management and Financing with AI-supported Digital Twins Modeling
candidates.abstract: The traditional 60/40 stock–bond allocation model has struggled to deliver diversification and stability in today's volatile, inflation-prone markets. This paper explores the strategic inclusion of commercial real estate (CRE) as a core third pillar in modern portfolio construction, alongside equities and bonds. CRE provides unique benefits—inflation resilience, durable income streams, and vital diversification through a low correlation with public markets. Empirical analysis confirms that adding real estate and infrastructure improves risk-adjusted returns and reduces portfolio volatility, especially during inflationary cycles. Crucially, we introduce the transformative potential of emerging technologies, such as digital twins and Agentic AI, which can transform CRE from an opaque, illiquid asset class into a liquid, transparent, highly scalable, high-performance investment. These tools address structural issues that have historically prevented CRE from functioning as a fully optimized portfolio component. Their integration enables real-time, granular analysis and dynamic allocation. This allows investors to optimize asset performance, align long-term liabilities with predictable returns, and enhance portfolio resilience. Without such technological integration, CRE’s full potential as a core asset class would remain unrealized. Our findings show that a comprehensive, AI-enabled reinvention of CRE management can unlock its structural advantages and position it as the third pillar of investment portfolios. We also designed a digital twin that models the expert-in-the-loop challenges in using AI for managing such complex interactions.

candidates.title: Between Innovation and Inequality: A Systematic Review of EdTech Business Models and Their Contradictions
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study examines EdTech business models and the tensions between their discourse of democratizing education and their documented educational outcomes. A Systematic Literature eview (SLR) following the PRISMA protocol was conducted, analyzing 112 documents, including peer-reviewed articles and institutional reports. The findings reveal that, although EdTech solutions promote personalization, flexibility, and innovative pedagogical approaches, their business models are predominantly structured around SaaS, freemium, and subscription-based models that prioritize scalability, data generation, and market expansion. This dynamic contributes to the assetization of education, whereby educational resources and user-generated data are transformed into digital assets controlled by private platforms. Furthermore, while EdTech narratives emphasize inclusion and lifelong learning, their effectiveness remains strongly dependent on structural conditions, including digital infrastructure, device accessibility, institutional support, and public policies, particularly in low- and middle-income contexts. The study also highlights concerns regarding the monetization of educational data, privacy, and the growing influence of commercial interests in educational processes. By integrating perspectives on business models, technologies, pedagogical approaches, and their associated contradictions, this research contributes to a more critical understanding of EdTech development. Based on these findings, the study proposes guidelines for EdTech companies, governments, international organizations, and public institutions to address these contradictions and promote more equitable, transparent, and socially responsible technology-mediated education.

candidates.title: Do vocaloids dream of electric sleep? The death and ageing of virtual Idols 1
candidates.abstract: This article explores what growing old means when distinctions between biological ageing, social ageing and technological ageing are fuzzy and confusing. Focusing on the Japanese virtual idol, Hatsune Miku, it asks what a post-humanist approach to celebrity and ageing yields in a context where celebrity is a highly elaborate techno-cultural formation and celebritisation a process embedded in global circuits and platform dynamics: both of which shape celebrity’s surfaces. Despite her appearance as a forever young idol, the article shows how Miku is inherently precarious and tethered to the fragile infrastructures that sustain her. Just as Miku’s fanbase matures, so their modes of engagement and the platforms that host their content evolve and decline. The article draws on a mix of theoretical work informed by post-humanism, as well as primary research comprising ethnographic work, netnography and close textual analysis. The article makes the case for an approach to celebrity that foregrounds the idea that fans age with their idols, reflecting a broader evolution in the lifecycle of digital fandom and ageing assemblages.

candidates.title: Is Influencer Identity a Key Cue? The Sequential Process of Message Acceptance in Issue-Based Communication on Social Media
candidates.abstract: Despite the growing use of virtual influencers (VIs), their persuasive effectiveness relative to human influencers (HIs) in issue-based social media communication remains underexplored. Drawing on social identity theory and Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) framework, Study 1 used a 2 x 2 x 2 between-subjects experiment and found higher message acceptance (MA) in the VI condition. Perceived social closeness (PSC) positively mediated the effect of influencer identity on MA, whereas trust functioned as a negative mediator. The serial pathway through PSC and trust was positive. Study 2 found no significant direct effect of influencer identity on MA, but identified perceived humanness as an upstream mediator shaping PSC, trust, and MA. Trust also worked as a negative mediator within competing mechanisms. The findings suggest that influencer identity shapes MA through layered perceptual and relational processes rather than through identity categorization alone and provide practical insights for issue-based communication.

candidates.title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
candidates.abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

candidates.title: Joint optimization framework for robot dance motion generation, aesthetic evaluation, and dynamic balance control based on conditional gans and safe deep reinforcement learning
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence and intelligent algorithms provide effective technical support for generating complex robotic dance motions and maintaining stable execution under dynamic constraints. To address the separation among motion synthesis, aesthetic evaluation, and balance control in existing robot dance systems, this study proposes a joint optimization framework that integrates a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN), multimodal aesthetic scoring, and safe Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). A temporal motion representation model is first constructed to encode joint angles, angular velocities, center-of-mass trajectories, rhythm labels, and style conditions. The cGAN generates style-consistent dance sequences through content encoding, style embedding, and sequence decoding, while a mechanical safety filter constrains joint angles, torque limits, self-collision, and support-region feasibility. A multimodal aesthetic evaluation model is then developed by fusing visual posture features, motion smoothness, spatial symmetry, and acoustic rhythm features. Human expert ratings are introduced to calibrate the automated aesthetic score and validate its objectivity. At the control level, a PPO-based policy is trained with ZMP constraints, joint-limit penalties, energy penalties, and safety-priority reward weighting. All baseline models, including LSTM-GAN, Transformer-GAN, MotionGAN, PID, DDPG, PPO, and TD3, are trained under identical data partitions and evaluation protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework reduces FID to 24.8, improves style recognition accuracy to 91.7%, increases aesthetic-score correlation with expert ratings to 0.86, and lowers the fall rate to 1.2%. Ablation and robustness tests further confirm the contribution of style transfer, multimodal feature fusion, PPO control, and ZMP-based safety constraints under external disturbances, sensor noise, uneven ground, and high-complexity dance motions.

candidates.title: $λ_0$: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution. We introduce HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion. Our human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns camera viewpoints and arm appearance, and refines motion references and controller inputs offline to reduce end-effector errors while preserving whole-body coordination. We validate the pipeline through zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative whole-body manipulation and long-range loco-manipulation tasks, without target-task robot demonstrations. Building on this pipeline, we develop $λ_0$, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training. Increasing whole-body human data consistently improves downstream task progress. $λ_0$ achieves 90.0% success on SIMPLE and 62.5% across real-world loco-manipulation tasks. We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world. Homepage: https://lambdahumanoid.github.io/

candidates.title: Conspiracy care work: gender, labor, and the paranoid style in American podcasting (2012-2020)
candidates.abstract: There is a dominant conception, both in academic literature and most media, that conspiracy theorists are mostly men—think “toxic masculinity” in internet culture. By analyzing fictional podcasts in the 2010s, my dissertation illustrates that this conception does not hold true. Apple’s built-in podcast app and the success of true crime podcast Serial (2014) heralded an era of prestige audio with conspiracy as a central theme and women as their paranoid protagonists. This research’s central question is: “What changes when the conspiracy theorist is not a (straight, cis, white, American) man, but instead female and/or queer?” The answer is in my title: conspiracy care work. When women and/or queer people engage in conspiracy theory, their motivation is not an individual quest for knowledge, but rather because of someone they care for, either personally or professionally, is in their perception endangered by a conspiracy. This dissertation explores what happens when conspiracy theorizing becomes (in fiction) a form of care work—a necessary way to care for those around them. Through media analysis, history, and interviews with listeners, I show how fictional podcasts comment on historical changes in conspiracy thinking, labor, and the role of the US in the world. They interrogate the role of intimacy and emotion in an era of social media, the underlying motives of the War on Terror, or the precarity of work under the contemporary neoliberal economic policy.

candidates.title: Newar Cultural Life in the Paintings of Third- and Fourth-Generation Chitrakar Artists: An Ethnographic Art Study
candidates.abstract: This paper examines the paintings of third- and fourth-generation Chitrakar artists of theKathmandu Valley from an ethnographic art perspective. The Chitrakars, the hereditarypainter caste of the Newar community, have long used painting not only as an aestheticmedium but also as a visual archive of Newar festivals, rituals, occupations, architecture,and everyday life. This study analyses selected works by ten artists: Amar Chitrakar,Manohar Man Pun, Gyan Bahadur Chitrakar, Dil Bahadur Chitrakar, and Surya BahadurChitrakar from the third generation; and Madan Chitrakar, Sarada Chitrakar, Prem ManChitrakar, Lok Chitrakar, and Ramesh Chitrakar from the fourth generation. Employing aqualitative methodology that combines visual analysis with ethnographic interpretation, thepaper explores how artistic representation functions as cultural documentation. The findingsdemonstrate that both generations meticulously recorded Newar social and ritual life,while their artistic practices evolved from realist representation toward diverse modernistexpressions. The paper concludes that Chitrakar paintings constitute an important repositoryof cultural knowledge, collective memory, and community identity, particularly at a time whenthe traditional hereditary practice of Newar painting is in decline. This study contributesto Nepali art history by highlighting the enduring ethnographic and cultural significance ofNewar visual heritage.

candidates.title: Unveiling the Chasm in Japanese robot-assisted surgery diffusion: the interplay of surgical volume and intra-specialty spillover
candidates.abstract: To examine structural factors associated with the diffusion of robot-assisted surgery (RAS) in Japan, this study examined the associations of annual surgical volume, defined as the sum of open, conventional laparoscopic, and RAS cases, and prior intra-specialty experience with adoption speed. Using the 1st to 10th editions of the National Database of Health Insurance Claims and Specific Health Checkups of Japan (NDB) Open Data across fiscal years 2014-2023, diffusion trajectories were visualized for 21 procedures approved for insurance coverage by 2020 through bivariate plots of annual surgical volume versus RAS replacement rates. RAS diffusion exhibited non-linear dynamics associated with annual procedure volume. In niche markets with < 6,000 annual cases (n = 9), six procedures demonstrated high growth in RAS replacement rate. Conversely, among 12 procedures with ≥ 6,000 annual cases, four did not cross the 16.0% chasm threshold through FY2023, and three required 6 years to surpass it. These patterns were thought to reflect challenges in the transition from specialized centers to general hospitals. Furthermore, a trend consistent with "intra-specialty spillover" was observed, wherein procedures approved in FY2020 achieved higher initial adoption than those in FY2018; although inseparable from the overall expansion of RAS since 2018, this suggests that accumulated infrastructure and expertise may facilitate the uptake of subsequent techniques. These findings suggest that RAS diffusion is associated with annual procedure volume, organizational readiness, and specialty‑specific infrastructure alongside technical factors. Future implementation strategies may benefit from infrastructure sharing within and across specialties and resource optimization to bridge the observed diffusion chasm.

candidates.title: The Era of Super intelligence (SI) and the Indian Education System: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
candidates.abstract: This research paper presents a serious and comprehensive analysis of how the emerging and rapidly changing era of 'Super intelligence' (SI) is fundamentally transforming the fabric of global and Indian society. In the history of modern technological revolutions, this turning point is the most unprecedented, where the traditional boundaries of artificial intelligence have been shattered and intellectual capacity is moving far beyond the scope of human control. Basic sectors such as education, health, employment, and industries are being affected the most by this technological leap. Focusing on these broad, complex, and far-reaching effects, this research paper closely examines the current preparedness of the Indian education system, the emerging trends of the younger generation, the serious challenges encountered along the way, and a comparative study with the foreign perspective of developed countries. In the next phase of the study, this research explores ideological paths to save Indian identity, culture, and originality amidst globalization and the blind race of technology. For this, the provisions of the National Education Policy (NEP 2020), modern technological requirements, and the support of our rich Indian philosophical tradition and 'Indian Knowledge Systems' (IKS) have been made the basis. The main objective of the research is to emphasize that in this race for the future, only technical proficiency is not enough; rather, the inclusion of moral values, character-building, and human sensitivities is equally essential. Finally, this research paper presents practical and policy suggestions to make the future direction robust, inclusive, self-reliant, and balanced, so that this torrential era of super intelligence does not become a cause of destruction for the Indian education system and society, but rather proves to be a great boon. This study will serve as an important document for policy-makers, academicians, and researchers in preparing the framework for the future.

candidates.title: Robotics for Aging Populations
candidates.abstract: Robotics offers versatile tools to face the challenges due to the older population growth, especially meeting the needs for assisting the elderly in the activities of daily living (ADLs) and for the geriatric care. However, the perspectives offered by human factors studies can further enhance this potential of robotics. This chapter explores the integration of ergonomics in the design of robots devised to enhance the independence and well-being of older adults. Furthermore, we mention the opportunities offered by wearable robotics, telepresence, and the pervasive solutions of the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) to implement paradigms of precision healthcare with decentralized and ubiquitous features, improving the sustainability of elderly care—following the human-centric perspectives of Society 5.0 and Health 5.0, with their synergies. For instance, we discuss issues of technology acceptance alongside the perspectives of value-sensitive design to ensure that robotics align with the experiential and, in particular, ethical needs in aging people and communities, first of all for inclusion. Intelligent systems will also be discussed for their potential to make robotic solutions even more versatile and adjustable to the seniors’ needs. By prioritizing the needs and preferences of older individuals (and their own network of relatives, friends, and acquaintances), ergonomics in robotics must contribute to the societal mission of preserving dignity, autonomy, and quality of life in aging societies.

candidates.title: Infrastructure-based autonomous mobile robots for internal logistics — challenges and future perspectives
candidates.abstract: The adoption of Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for internal logistics is accelerating, with most solutions emphasizing decentralized, onboard intelligence. While AMRs in indoor environments like factories can be supported by infrastructure, involving external sensors and computational resources, such systems remain underexplored in the literature. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of infrastructure-based AMR systems, outlining key opportunities and challenges. To support this, we introduce a reference architecture combining infrastructure-based sensing, on-premise cloud computing, and onboard autonomy. Based on the architecture, we review core technologies for localization, perception, and planning. We demonstrate the approach in a real-world deployment in a heavy-vehicle manufacturing environment and summarize findings from a user experience (UX) evaluation. Our aim is to provide a holistic foundation for future development of scalable, robust, and human-compatible AMR systems in complex industrial environments.

candidates.title: AI and language in healthcare: The role of doctor identity and linguistic alignment in perceptions of doctor quality
candidates.abstract: AI will play an increasingly large role in providing healthcare services in the near future, creating a pressing need to examine how people perceive AI compared to humans in healthcare. To this end, this study examines how people perceive AI and human doctors in a common medical scenario of giving healthcare advice over an online chat platform. Participants read an online chat conversation that featured a patient asking for medical advice with either an AI or human doctor. In addition, the doctor either linguistically aligned with the patient (by repeating medical terms previously used by the patient) or not (by using synonyms of the patient's terms). Linguistic alignment in conversation has been found to increase positive perceptions of interactions and therefore may be a useful tool to increase patient satisfaction in healthcare interactions. AI doctors but not human ones were penalized when not linguistically aligning with the patient, even though these doctors gave the same exact medical advice. Additionally, across a range of measures, participants in general had more negative perceptions of AI doctors compared to human ones. Overall, these results suggest that people hold AI to different standards as well as judge AI harsher than humans in medical settings.

candidates.title: Home Robots for Older Adults and Their Caregivers: Identifying Deployment Requirements
candidates.abstract: As the population of older adults grows, home robots may help address daily living challenges associated with mobility, cognitive change, health management, and social isolation. This study examined deployment requirements for assistive home robots from a human factors and ergonomics perspective by evaluating the Stretch mobile manipulator with older adults and community care staff in a simulated life-plan community apartment. Using demonstrations and semi-structured interviews, we assessed perceptions of usability, acceptance, and task relevance. Findings showed strong interest in support for safety, object retrieval, medication and hydration reminders, telehealth access, exercise adherence, and social connection. Participants emphasized design requirements critical to deployment, including intuitive multimodal interaction, reliable operation in unstructured home environments, personalization over time, and early stakeholder involvement. The results highlight how human-centered evaluation can identify deployment needs and guide the safe, effective integration of home robots to support independence, overall well-being, and quality of life among older adults.

candidates.title: Towards the Roof of the World: NLP Progress in Tibetan Languages
candidates.abstract: Tibetan, spoken by some seven million people on and around the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, remains underrepresented in natural language processing (NLP). We present, to our knowledge, the first peer-reviewed systematic bibliometric survey of Tibetan NLP: 140 publications from 2004 to 2026 in the ACL Anthology and DBLP, annotated for venue type, research area, first-affiliation country, and resource release. Output has grown rapidly, with 84% of the publications appearing since 2018, and has expanded bottom-up along the NLP pipeline, from corpora and word segmentation through script, speech, and applications to large language models (LLMs). Researchers based in China first-authored 87% of the publications, which span all 25 represented research areas, whereas work from other countries concentrates on Classical Tibetan. We argue that this full-pipeline paradigm, realized under the compounded constraints of a complex script, dialectal diversity, and geographic remoteness, offers a reference model for other low-resource languages of the Global South. We also identify gaps in dialect coverage, responsible NLP, native and comparable evaluation, cross-community visibility, and resource release (only 29% of the publications release data, code, or models), and recommend open science, shared standards, and community participation for the LLM era.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Library and Information Science Research: Trends, Citation Patterns, and Knowledge Structure Analysis
candidates.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are changing Library and Information Science (LIS) by impacting on user services, cataloguing, and information retrieval; however, the literature on how this is happening has not been systematically catalogued. To fill this gap, this study was conducted using a bibliometric analysis of the papers pertaining to AI, ML and LIS published from 2015 to 2024. The aim of the study is to analyse the growth of publication, citation trends, characteristics of authors, keyword co-occurrence networks, and international collaboration in this field to discover the intellectual structures and future trends of the field. A total of 2180 documents from 436 sources were retrieved by applying a structured keyword search strategy, after removing the duplicates and the irrelevant documents, the retrieved documents were analysed with the help of the Bibliometrix package in RStudio and VOSviewer for descriptive bibliometric analysis and network-based bibliometric analysis respectively. Results indicate an increase at an annual rate of 43.16%, with only 2024 reporting 707 publications or 32.43% of the total. The data set contained 7,623 authors, each of whom authored an average of 3.84 co-authors per document, and only 71 documents (3.26%) had a single author, showing a very collaborative research culture. The most common and most cited author keywords were “machine learning” (7,633 citations), “deep learning” (4,182), and “learning systems” (3,272). The document with the most citations garnered 351 citations, with India becoming the top among the contributing countries and the largest node in the international co-authorship networks. From these results, it can be inferred that AI/ML research in LIS is growing rapidly, is collaborative in nature and has a higher focus on machine learning and deep learning applications. Based on the study, the researcher concludes that this bibliometric mapping will be a baseline reference for researchers, librarians and policy makers to understand the evolution of AI and ML in LIS and to identify emerging research areas like generative AI, explainable AI and intelligent digital libraries.

candidates.title: Human-Centered Robotics for Surgery
candidates.abstract: Surgical ergonomics is influenced by many aspects associated with posture, vision, hand motion, and haptic feedback. Specific ergonomics aspects can induce long-term effects in the surgeon directly affecting the performance. One of the major disadvantages of Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) remains the non-ergonomic design of the entire surgical environment. This condition results in a significant reduction in the quality of interventions and discomfort for the medical operator. Modern teleoperated surgical robots offer an optimized console, in which the surgeon can operate in a seated position with specific arm support and a 3D view of the operating site. The da Vinci surgical console offers ergonomic improvements over standard endoscopic surgery. Modern robotic platforms stand beyond the da Vinci System, offering more advanced ergonomic solutions in terms of haptic feedback and visual perception. Due to the introduction of more advanced technology, surgery has changed, resulting in increased system complexity at the technical, human and organizational levels, which may lead to higher variability of patient outcomes due to new error pathways. Adopting a proactive approach enables the prior identification of critical factors and the design of safer socio-technical systems, thanks to a multi-level perspective. This chapter addresses the fundamental elements of surgical ergonomics, considering the factors that affect performance and healthiness during traditional procedures, with specific reference to MIS and microsurgery. This baseline is then compared to the use of surgical robots by evaluating the effect of design decisions on operator ergonomics. In addition, studies propose proactive methodologies that assess the personal and organizational factors of surgical performance in this complex socio-technical system.

candidates.title: Embodied Zero-Shot Task Planning via Hardware-Aware LLM-VLM Integration for Grounded Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Large language models can translate natural-language instructions into plausible manipulation plans, but robotic execution requires physically grounded decisions that respect robot embodiment, workspace geometry, reachability, collision constraints, and grasp feasibility. This paper presents a hardware-aware large language model-vision-language model (LLM-VLM) manipulation framework for a simulated Franka Research 3 robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. The framework separates symbolic reasoning from metric execution: an API-hosted LLM planner receives a structured scene summary and generates only symbolic task information, including the object to manipulate, target relation, approach preference, and objects to avoid. A local Qwen3-VL 8B VLM verifier supports semantic confirmation of ambiguous objects and open-container surrogates. Both the LLM planner and the VLM verifier are prohibited from generating robot coordinates, grasp poses, keepout dimensions, gripper commands, trajectory waypoints, or success labels. Instead, these decisions are handled by deterministic grounding and execution modules that use the robot model, scene geometry, MoveIt 2 collision checking, inverse kinematics, grasp validation, release verification, and final visual assessment. Execution feedback is returned only as symbolic context for replanning. The framework is evaluated through simulated digital-twin trials involving pickup, occluded-source access, keepout reasoning, relation placement, and sequential manipulation tasks.

candidates.title: Greening computed tomography: a position paper on environmentally responsible imaging practice from the computed tomography subspecialty section of the Italian society of radiology
candidates.abstract: Healthcare accounts for 4.4-4.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions, with computed tomography (CT) representing one of the most resource-intensive and energy-demanding diagnostic modalities. Sustainability should be integrated as a core component of quality in CT practice, achieving the perfect balance between diagnostic excellence and environmental responsibility. Several key intervention areas can be identified. CT scanners consume substantial amounts of energy, with 44-72% used during nonproductive idle periods. Potential mitigation strategies include protocol optimization, automated power-down systems, and infrastructure improvements. The current "store-everything" approach to CT datasets generates a considerable carbon footprint; adopting "digital temperance" by retaining only clinically relevant images can reduce storage-related emissions. Although workstations consume less energy than scanners, their cumulative impact can be reduced through automated policies and optimized hardware lifecycle management. Iodinated contrast media persist in aquatic ecosystems and may generate toxic by-products. Sustainable strategies include personalized weight-based dosing, multi-energy CT to reduce contrast volume, and recovery or recycling programs. Single-use consumables and the environmental costs of artificial intelligence were also addressed. A 17-item action list was developed to translate the evidence-informed recommendations into practical actions for sustainable CT practice. The transition toward environmentally responsible CT practice is an ethical and professional necessity that can no longer be delayed. This position paper identifies the key challenges and proposes practical, evidence-informed strategies to transform resource-consuming CT practices into actionable and sustainable workflows, while maintaining clinical effectiveness.

candidates.title: The robotic PIANO: a critical narrative review of surgeon-controlled operative polyphony, human factors, and robotic training
candidates.abstract: Robotic surgery can concentrate control of several technical functions at the console, but such concentration does not itself confer clinical independence, reduce dependence on the perioperative team, or improve patient outcomes. We define surgeon-controlled operative polyphony as the phase-bounded coordination of multiple partially independent technical control streams by one console operator within a distributed perioperative system. This critical narrative review and conceptual synthesis asks which technical functions can be concentrated coherently, where human-factors and team dependencies set limits, and how evaluation, training, and governance should respond. The piano is used as a question-generating model, not as evidence of clinical benefit. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through 18 August 2026; targeted engineering, educational, neuroscientific, human-factors, and musicological searches and backward citation tracking supplemented retrieval. To analyze this control configuration, we propose the PIANO framework: Phase-specific control, Interface fidelity, Agency allocation, Neuromotor integration, and Orchestrated teamwork. Its scientific novelty lies in linking this control architecture to the PIANO framework: Phase-specific control, Interface fidelity, Agency allocation, Neuromotor integration, and Orchestrated teamwork. PIANO is an analytic and hypothesis-generating framework, not a score or credentialing standard. Concentrated control may shorten selected action loops, but any benefit depends on feedback, workload, shared situation awareness, explicit authority, and rescue capacity. The Competency-Based Assessment of Robotic Surgery Skills (CARS) curriculum provides initial validation evidence for domain-specific assessment of performer competence; repeated cases and use-specific evidence remain necessary for high-stakes decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support phase recognition, feedback, assessment, and personalised training within a human-in-the-loop system. One surgeon may coordinate many operative voices; safe surgery remains a collective, patient-centered performance.

candidates.title: Effect of physical movement of robotic displays in public spaces on passersby’s attraction and sustained viewing
candidates.abstract: Abstract Robotic displays, which consist of flat-panel display(s) mounted on a wheeled robot, are increasingly being used in public spaces, but their effectiveness has not been thoroughly verified. This study examines the impact of robotic displays on passersby’s attraction and sustained viewing. Specifically, we observed their reactions to a robotic display’s unidirectional movement that accompanies passersby as they walk, and we compared these reactions with those to a large fixed screen with animated content. We conducted a one-day in-the-wild experiment where the display movement and animation were controlled using a Wizard-of-Oz protocol at a public exhibition event. An analysis of video-coded observations of over 400 passersby shows that the robotic display was noticed by 41.2% more passersby and held their gazes 171% longer than the animated screen, suggesting that the physical movement of robotic displays enhances passerby attraction and sustained viewing. In addition, we derive design implications from our results for the behavior of robotic displays in public spaces.

candidates.title: Who Is Talking to the Agent? LLMs in Multi-User 3D Virtual Environments
candidates.abstract: When several people share a 3D virtual room with an LLM agent, the agent must decide not only what to say, but whether an utterance was addressed to it and, if accessible, what profile information about the others present it may use. To study both problems, we construct LookAway, a controlled corpus of 40 sessions involving 80 distinct personas and an LLM agent (1,200 turns), including ambiguous-addressee turns in which speaker orientation agrees or conflicts with the intended addressee. Across three open-weight large language models and five conditions varying which profiles the agent sees and whether it is told where each person faces (18,000 decisions), adding speaker orientation increased addressee accuracy from 56% to 99.5% when orientation was congruent, but when the speaker faced someone other than the addressee, two of the models went by where the speaker faced on more than 85% of those turns. Warning one model that orientation could be misleading reduced this only modestly. A browser-based 3D demonstrator shows the effect live: the same sentence gets an answer when the speaker faces the agent and silence when they face the other person. Providing both personas' profiles improved responses about the person being asked about, but also increased the use of profile attributes not revealed in the shared conversation, reaching 45.3% of answers for one model. More context thus improves multi-user interaction but also leads to oversharing, so shared LLM agents need mechanisms for weighing spatial cues and controlling when user-specific information enters a response.

candidates.title: Low-Cost Spectrophotometers: A Comparative Evaluation of Open-Source Architectures
candidates.abstract: The rapid growth of low-cost and open-source spectrophotometers has created a need for systematic methodologies to evaluate and compare alternative instrument architectures. This study presents a comparative assessment of three representative open-source spectrophotometric platforms, encompassing discrete multispectral sensing and continuous-spectrum imaging approaches. Their performance was evaluated against a commercial Thermo Scientific Genesys 30 spectrophotometer in terms of spectral agreement, portability, implementation complexity, and cost. The results demonstrate that no single architecture is universally optimal; instead, each presents distinct trade-offs that determine its suitability for specific applications. Multispectral sensor-based systems offer compact, low-power solutions for field deployment, whereas imaging-based platforms provide spectral performance closer to laboratory-grade instrumentation. All hardware designs, firmware, and software developed in this work are released as open-source resources to support reproducibility and further development. The study highlights the importance of matching instrument architecture to application requirements and proposes a practical framework for the evaluation and selection of low-cost spectrophotometers, facilitating the adoption of open-source analytical tools for water quality monitoring and related applications.

candidates.title: Use of Social and Educational Robots in Early Childhood and Elementary Education Teaching-Learning Processes: A Scoping Review
candidates.abstract: This scoping review synthesizes robot-assisted education for children aged 3–12. Analyzing 27 empirical studies (2020–2025), we examine platforms, emotional effects, and learning domains. Findings show a reliance on costly commercial humanoids and high student motivation, but limited evidence for sustained cognitive gains. Research primarily targets STEM and literacy, varying between educational levels. However, the field suffers from small samples, brief interventions, and weak theoretical grounding. This review emphasizes the need for inclusive, methodologically robust, and pedagogically grounded research that prioritizes accessibility and equity.

candidates.title: Low-cost robotics and AI technologies for rehabilitation and health monitoring
candidates.abstract: This paper reviews robotics technologies applied to rehabilitation. Besides a literature review, selected to highlight relevant topics/aspects, the paper presents a few examples of low cost technologies (which are particularly important in ageing demographics and struggling economies) and discusses applications in the overlap between rehabilitation and regular health monitoring. The purpose of this study is to frame rehabilitation robotics in terms of the existing technologies and to showcase low cost demonstrators with relevance in rehabilitation scenarios. Besides the encouraging results, obtained in real-world tests (a distinctive characteristic of the paper), the role of AI techniques in the development of low cost devices is also highlighted. Moreover, the paper also discusses the influence of human factors in the acceptance and adoption of alternative/disruptive technologies.

candidates.title: Underrepresented food culture and culinary journey of selected foreign communities of Kolkata
candidates.abstract: Kolkata, over the centuries, has adopted, accepted, and included communities from across the globe, creating the present-day Kolkata platter through food evolution. Historical connotations and literary descriptions are mostly on colonial, Chinese, Mughlai, and Awadhi influences. However, there are other foreign communities, like Afghans, Parsis, and Tibetans, who came for trade and exile, and whose cuisines found a place in Bengalis’ food palate. However, the global influence of K-Waves through digital media has also influenced people’s food choices, which differs significantly from the city’s historical narratives. Thus, the study develops an argument based on visiting selected restaurants and conversations with customers who prefer Afghan, Tibetan, Parsi, and Korean food over other cuisines. This qualitative study employed participant observation and unstructured interviews conducted at selected Afghan, Parsi, Tibetan, and Korean restaurants eighteen in numbers on popularity basis in Kolkata. Data were collected from forty general customers from restaurants and separately sixty Bengali respondents who are frequent consumers of these cuisines using snowball sampling. Interview data and field observations are analysed through thematic coding, while respondents’ cuisine preferences were summarised using a food preference matrix to compare patterns across age groups. The finding reveals that Afghans, Parsis, and Tibetans arrived at different times as traders or immigrants, and that, among all the material exchanges, food proved a key to cultural assimilation with the natives. Finally, the study contributes to the changing food culture of Kolkata, influenced by unexplored foreign communities, and highlights their importance in developing the city’s culinary identity.

candidates.title: LIFE AND DEATH IN THE 1930S RURAL SOUTH: GENDER, POVERTY, AND SPIRITUAL DISILLUSIONMENT IN WILLIAM FAULKNER’S AS I LAY DYING (1930)
candidates.abstract: This article explores how poverty and cultural expectations shape life, death, and mourning in William Faulkner’s As I Lay Dying. Focusing on Addie Bundren, it highlights the intersection of gender, class, and spiritual disillusionment in the rural South of the 1930s. Addie’s emotional isolation, her relationship to religion and motherhood, and her disconnect from the rural community reveal the limited roles available to women and the failure of traditional belief systems during economic hardship. The grotesque treatment of her body, the crude funeral rituals, and the family’s self-serving motivations during the burial journey all demonstrate how difficult socioeconomic conditions distort mourning. By combining feminist interpretations of Addie Bundren with cultural theories of emotion and historical sources – such as funeral customs and the social realities of the American South during the Great Depression – this article reframes mourning and emotional deprivation in As I Lay Dying as shaped by poverty, gender norms, and cultural expectations that demand survival and silence rather than the expression of grief or emotional needs. Keywords: gender, class, American South, death, emotional deprivation, William Faulkner, As I Lay Dying

candidates.title: The World's First Identified Superintelligence Peace Constitution
candidates.abstract: This record preserves the digitally signed International Submission Edition — 2026 of “The World’s First Identified Superintelligence Peace Constitution — For Humanity, World Peace and Peaceful Continuity.” The instrument is an independent, good-faith and non-binding civil-society constitutional proposal concerning the prospective governance of Superintelligence. It develops the Author’s preceding AI Peace Constitution work into a distinct Superintelligence-specific constitutional architecture directed toward human dignity, meaningful human agency, scientific responsibility, international peace and security, responsible concern for life, future generations and peaceful continuity. The Constitution addresses, among other matters, scientific determination of Superintelligence, capability-proportionate responsibility, human dignity and agency, safety and controllability, catastrophic-risk prevention, non-weaponization, international security, human rights, justice, information integrity, life and ecological continuity, health and human integrity, economic and global inclusion, children and future generations, questions of possible future artificial moral significance, governance, accountability, international cooperation, emergency safeguards, correction, non-recurrence and long-term continuity. The instrument does not assert that Superintelligence presently exists or that its emergence is inevitable. It does not purport to represent the Republic of India, the United Nations, any Member State, humanity as a whole or any intergovernmental institution. It does not create supranational authority and does not claim governmental, treaty, legislative or other binding legal status. References in the instrument to existing international law derive their legal authority solely from their independently applicable sources. New safeguards or constitutional principles advanced by the instrument are presented as proposed normative provisions unless they independently possess another legal status. The expression “World’s First Identified” is used only as a qualified, good-faith historical-priority characterization of the specific category of a comprehensive Superintelligence Peace Constitution, based on publicly accessible material identified during preparation of the instrument. Historical accuracy remains subject to evidence. This publication constitutes the third specialized stage in the Author’s documented AI Peace Constitution intellectual and constitutional lineage, while remaining a distinct archival work. candidates.title: Configuring the World of Work: A Resonance-Based Critique of Focus-Oriented Idle Games: The Case of Chill with You: Lo-Fi Story
candidates.abstract: Focus-oriented idle games remain open while users work or study, offering music, adjustable scenery, and a digital companion. Drawing on Hartmut Rosa’s theories of social acceleration and resonance, this article presents a qualitative analysis of Chill with You: Lo-Fi Story, combining the game’s text, play records, and Steam reviews. The game gives everyday tasks sensory, bodily, and relational significance through audiovisual environments, shared timing, and character narratives. Players describe feeling accompanied, attending to fatigue, and reconsidering how they spend their time. Timed unlocks and character dialogue, however, also frame continued concentration as a contribution to knowing the character and sustaining the relationship. Reviews that judge the game by how well it supports further work treat companionship, rest, and environmental settings as resources for remaining productive. The game translates aspirations for a good life into matters of individual configuration and management, concentrating responsibility for coping with time pressure on users themselves. The analysis shows how richer conditions for resonance can accompany stronger demands for self-management. The critical question is whether the needs acknowledged through companionship can change workloads and working rhythms, and who bears responsibility for making those changes.
