candidates.title: Sweet Pepper Harvesting Robots: Advances in Perception, Decision-Making, Manipulation and Mobile Systems
candidates.abstract: Sweet pepper is a high-value crop in protected horticulture whose robotic harvesting is complicated by canopy occlusion, asynchronous ripening, the need for precise peduncle cutting, and stringent damage limits. This review presents a systematic search and narrative synthesis guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, with the revised evidence base comprising 262 eligible reports/publications. Reports describing the same robot platform, trial series, or overlapping evaluation dataset were linked as companion reports within a common study/evaluation family to avoid double counting in system-level comparisons. It examines crop constraints, perception, decision-making and system integration, manipulators and end-effectors, and mobile platforms across the complete harvesting cycle. Beyond a module-based synthesis, we propose a five-stage chain—visibility, assessability, reachability, operability, and sustained operation—supported by a unified failure taxonomy, a stage-wise funnel, and a scenario–technology matching matrix. This framework explains why strong module-level results do not necessarily yield effective whole-system harvesting. Representative system-level evaluations within the direct sweet-pepper/Capsicum evidence base report harvesting success rates of approximately 18–83% and source-reported cycle times of approximately 10–69 s per fruit under differing task boundaries, although direct ranking is inappropriate because environments, crop modifications, occlusion levels, sample sizes, task boundaries, denominators, and success criteria differ. As fruit detection and basic grasping improve, losses increasingly arise from incomplete action-ready information on maturity, pose, and peduncles; narrow approach and cutting tolerances; and weak recovery, unloading, and repositioning loops. Near-term development should investigate robot-friendly greenhouses, repeatable docking, local closed-loop control, and human-supervised or collaborative operation, while directly validating productivity, safety, workload, and economic effects. Medium-term priorities are active multimodal perception, fault-tolerant grasping and cutting, and coordinated mobile manipulation. Longer-term progress will depend on agronomy–equipment co-design and long-duration validation of reliability and economic viability.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a process of socio-technical co-evolution: a structured review of the transition from content generation to operational intelligence
candidates.abstract: In the era of the digital economy, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become a transformative force, and its impact extends far beyond the scope of content creation. GenAI has rapidly evolved from generating text, images, and code to assuming operational roles across industries, science, healthcare, and governance. Tracing this evolution requires more than a catalog of technical milestones. A dedicated analytical framework is therefore needed. This study constructs a comprehensive analytical framework organized around three intertwined axes: technology generation, operational intelligence, and socio-technical co-evolution. The framework is applied comparatively across five domains: industry, healthcare, education, finance, and public governance. Three cross-cutting principles emerge from this cross-domain analysis. These are situation-sensitive anchoring, dynamic trust calibration, and responsibility-aware delegation. Risk tolerance, cultural background, and the depth of domain-specific knowledge are identified as key moderators that shape the transition from generative tools to operational intelligence. By synthesizing evidence across these dimensions, this review identifies future directions for research, design, and governance of GenAI systems.

candidates.title: Responsible AI guidelines fall short at work? How responsible AI governance can benefit from the world of work perspectives
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming part of everyday work and people management, with potentially far-reaching consequences for employees, organizations, and labour markets. Yet the regulation of workplace AI is still evolving, leaving organizations and policymakers uncertain about what “Responsible AI” (RAI) means in practice. Governments, professional bodies, and organizations have produced a growing number of RAI guidelines. But do these guidelines help equip organizations and policymakers to govern AI in the workplace? This paper examines 183 organizational RAI guidelines to understand how they address work and employment issues. Our analysis identifies the main themes emphasized across the guidelines and reveals that work- and labour-related concerns rarely occupy a central position. It also suggests that, despite their proliferation, RAI guidelines remain centred on largely stable and abstract principles, with limited evolution in their normative focus. When workplace issues are mentioned, they are usually framed indirectly, most often through concerns about discrimination and employee safety. RAI frameworks therefore rarely confront the workplace directly, even though employment is one of AI’s most immediate and consequential arenas. We argue that anchoring RAI governance in established governance mechanisms – including international labour standards and fundamental principles and rights at work – can help organizations and policymakers ensure that workplace AI addresses ethical concerns in the world of work and promotes decent work.

candidates.title: LiteEMG-FM: An Efficient and Deployable Foundation Model for Robust EMG Sensing
candidates.abstract: Electromyography (EMG) signals vary substantially across individuals, body regions, recording sessions, and sensing hardware, limiting the generalization of models for assistive devices and human-computer interaction. Existing time-series foundation models are also computationally expensive for real-time wearable deployment and often fail to capture EMG-specific time-frequency characteristics. We present LiteEMG-FM, an efficient hybrid CNN-Transformer foundation model for practical EMG sensing. Pretrained on 16 diverse upper- and lower-limb EMG datasets, LiteEMG-FM learns representations that generalize across users and datasets. For resource-constrained deployment, we implement a hierarchical wake-up architecture in which a lightweight, always-on 1D-CNN filters rest and non-target activity and activates LiteEMG-FM only for valid gestures. We evaluate full inference offloading, split inference, and full on-device processing, characterizing their trade-offs in latency, power consumption, and memory footprint. Across diverse evaluation settings, LiteEMG-FM outperforms state-of-the-art time-series foundation models and supervised baselines, particularly under zero-calibration cross-participant and data-scarce conditions. These results demonstrate that LiteEMG-FM is an effective, efficient, and deployable foundation model for EMG applications.

candidates.title: ChunkVLA-AM: Parallel Action Chunking for Vision-Language-Action Robot Control in Additive Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models unify visual perception, language understanding, and action generation, offering new opportunities for automation in additive manufacturing (AM). However, deployment in AM remains challenging because adapting these models to unseen robot embodiments is costly, and performance can degrade under environment changes. In this work, we present a framework for deploying OpenVLA-OFT on a FAIRINO FR3 robot in a fixed AM workcell. A data pipeline converts monocular real-world demonstrations into OpenVLA-compatible TFDS/RLDS datasets to support adaptation to the FR3 embodiment. At runtime, each inference request predicts an eight-step chunk of 7-D actions. The FR3 executes each chunk open loop before capturing a new observation, providing closed-loop feedback between chunks. The system uses a cloud-edge architecture in which the FR3 client streams observations to a remote inference server through a FastAPI interface. In 42 physical A-to-B object-transfer trials, evenly split between red and blue targets, the system succeeded in 39 (92.9%). All three failures occurred during final placement, when insufficient release-height control caused the object to topple. An illumination sweep identified a low-error luminance range of 85-125 on a 0-255 scale, with the lowest mean spatial error at 95.

candidates.title: From Homunculus to Cybernetics: Artificial Life and the Evolution of the Artificial Human in Performing Arts
candidates.abstract: The study traces the aesthetic development of the image of the artificial human from the medieval homunculus through modern forms of artificial beings and science fiction films to the contemporary robot or cyborg as a phenomenon that influences not only science but also art.The artificial human is understood here not as a technological device, but as the latest historical embodiment of a long continuity of attempts to create artificial human and nonhuman being, reaching back to ancient automata.The central question guiding the study is how the figure of the artificial human, reactivated across radically different historical and technological contexts, continues to renegotiate the boundary between the living and the artificial, and what this recurrence reveals about the changing aesthetic and cultural functions of that boundary.To address this, the study outlines how the aesthetics of the artificial human have changed in cultural and artistic narratives, and how these transformations have influenced theatrical and performative approaches in the 20 th and 21 st centuries.

candidates.title: Analysis of Social Media Subscriber Bases and Viewership Patterns across Tamil Television Channels
candidates.abstract: This paper examines audience demography, cross-platform syndication dynamics and digital subscriber bases in the regional Tamil television broadcasting sector. The Tamil language market has more than 75 licensed satellite channels across General Entertainment (GEC), 24x7 News, Feature Cinema, Music and specialized niche broadcasting. This research adopts a triangulated methodology grounded in Chadwick’s hybrid media systems framework, Jenkins’ participatory culture paradigm, and theories of vernacular digital diaspora. It utilizes cross-platform API harvesting (YouTube Data API v3 and Meta Content Library), an empirical stratified survey of television-owning households across urban and rural clusters (N = 1,240, fieldwork conducted across Q3 2026), and qualitative thematic key informant interviews (n = 36). The quantitative results show that GEC programming is the king of digital video engagement, accounting for 58.4% of total consumption, followed by News & Current Affairs (19.8%), Cinema/Music (14.2%) and Devotional/Niche channels (7.6%). When broken down by platform, demographic differences are starkly inverted. Linear TV is the domain of older women (67.6% of linear viewing, peaking at 78.0% for prime-time soap operas), whereas social media syndication is dominated by male-leaning (55.6%) and youth (64.2% aged 18–34) demographics. High-frequency syndication velocity (50–120 posts/day) is a strong predictor of subscriber acquisition for news broadcasters (beta = 0.82, p < 0.001), whereas GEC channels drive subscription through short-form viral engagement density (beta = 0.89, p < 0.001). This study elucidates how vernacular networks generate hybrid multi-screen broadcasting ecosystems and provides practical suggestions for modular production, algorithmic metadata optimization and cross-platform monetization.

candidates.title: DexWrist: A Robotic Wrist for Constrained and Dynamic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Development of dexterous manipulation hardware has primarily focused on hands and grippers. However, these end-effectors are often paired with bulky and highly stiff wrists that limit performance in human environments. More recent designs have adopted backdrivable actuation, but are still difficult to model and control due to coupled kinematics or high mechanical inertia from heavy links. We present DexWrist, a compact robotic wrist combining quasi-direct-drive actuation with a decoupled parallel kinematic mechanism to advance manipulation in highly constrained environments and enable dynamic, contact-rich tasks. It delivers 3.75$\pm$0.05 Nm rated torque, 0.33$\pm$0.06 Nm backdrive torque, 10.15$\pm$1.34 Hz torque bandwidth, $\pm 40^\circ$ ROM in both DOFs, and a diagonal velocity-constraint Jacobian (one-to-one motor-to-DOF mapping) in a 0.97 kg package. In practice, these properties increase workspace in clutter and stabilize contact without finely tuned admittance control. We evaluate DexWrist as a drop-in upgrade in simulation and on three robot arms across constrained and contact-rich tasks. In learned policy evaluations on the AgileX PiPER and UR3e, DexWrist achieved 50-76% relative improvements in success rate and reduced autonomous task completion times by 3-5x; on a torque-controlled Franka FR3, where a strong joint-impedance baseline already succeeds, it still completed the task 1.4x faster. Project page and videos: https://martinpeticco.com/dexwrist

candidates.title: Developing and validating the attitudes toward large language models scale
candidates.abstract: With large language models (LLMs) now embedded in a wide range of everyday technologies, there is increasing interest in accurately measuring public attitudes toward these systems. General AI attitude instruments may not fully capture attitudes specific to LLMs. To address this gap, we adapted the 5-item Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence (ATAI) scale, a dual-component scale measuring AI Fear and AI Acceptance, and developed two new measures: the Attitudes Toward General LLMs (AT-GLLM) and Attitudes Toward Primary LLM (AT-PLLM) scales, assessing general attitudes and attitudes toward the LLM each respondent uses most. Both instruments were designed specifically for the LLM context and validated in a UK sample of 526 adults (ages 18-45). Psychometric analyses supported a two-factor structure, strong measurement invariance across gender, and acceptable internal consistency across the four subscales (Cronbach’s α = 0.742–0.786; McDonald’s ω = 0.747–0.793). Both scales demonstrated convergent and discriminant validity. These measures offer more precise tools for assessing attitudes toward LLMs than general AI attitude scales and can be used in research and applied settings, enhancing evaluations of user experience and supporting the monitoring of public engagement with this evolving technology.

candidates.title: To Ban or Not to Ban? How Open Source Projects Govern GenAI Contributions
candidates.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is playing an increasingly important role in open source software (OSS). Beyond completing code and documentation, GenAI is increasingly involved in issues, pull requests, code reviews, and security reports. Yet, cheaper generation does not mean cheaper review — and the resulting maintenance burden has pushed OSS projects to experiment with GenAI-specific rules in contribution guidelines, security policies, and repository instructions, even including a total ban on AI-assisted contributions. However, governing GenAI in OSS is far more than a ban-or-not question. The responses remain scattered, with neither a shared governance framework in practice nor a systematic understanding in research. Therefore, in this paper, we conduct a multi-stage analysis on various qualitative materials related to GenAI governance retrieved from 67 highly visible OSS projects. Our analysis identifies recurring concerns across contribution workflows, derives three governance orientations, and maps out 12 governance strategies and their policy instruments. We show that governing GenAI in OSS extends well beyond banning — it requires coordinated responses across accountability, verification, review capacity, code provenance, and platform infrastructure. Overall, our work distills dispersed community practices into a structured overview, providing a conceptual baseline for researchers and a practical reference for maintainers and platform designers.

candidates.title: Search-Based Testing of Vision Language Models for In-Car Scene Understanding
candidates.abstract: The automotive industry is increasingly exploring vision-language models (VLMs) for in-car scene understanding (ISU), extracting semantic information from camera-recorded scenes to detect safety-critical events such as driver distraction. However, VLMs may generate incomplete, erroneous, or misleading scene descriptions, highlighting the need for systematic testing. Collecting real in-vehicle data is costly, difficult to scale, and often infeasible, particularly in early design stages. In this paper, we present ISU-Test, an automated testing approach that combines rendering-based scene generation with search-based testing to evaluate ISU systems. By framing testing as an optimization problem and systematically modifying scene parameters, our method generates diverse in-car scenarios and explores a wide range of configurations. We evaluate ISU-Test on both an industrial prototype and open-source VLMs across two case studies: question answering and captioning, comparing against randomized scenario generation. Results show that ISU-Test significantly outperforms the baseline, achieving up to 10× higher failure rates and up to 3.6× higher coverage.

candidates.title: Crypto airdrops as post-speculative finance: A digital methods study of platform-mediated value in digital cultures
candidates.abstract: Abstract Crypto-finance permeates digital culture through platforms like YouTube and Telegram, transforming how financial value is produced, circulated, and legitimised. This article examines crypto airdrops – token distributions that reward users for blockchain transactions, Web3 gameplay, and online engagement – as a key site where finance becomes embedded in digital culture. What might initially appear as a niche crypto practice generates substantial platform-mediated financial participation. Across the seven airdrop campaigns documented on YouTube and Telegram, we identify a transnational and multilingual community that consistently produces, circulates and engages with airdrop-related content. Drawing on quali-quantitative digital methods, we map the communicative, visual, and algorithmic labour through which users perform eligibility for token rewards, and trace how cultures of participation sustain token value. Our findings reveal a structural shift from speculative hype cycles to labour-intensive participation, underpinned by new forms of governance, legitimacy and financial subjectivation. We argue that airdrops exemplify a post-speculative modality of finance: a structural reorganisation of speculation around prescribed labour, platform-mediated coordination, and the distributed cultural work of users. The article contributes to debates on the social logics of finance, platform governance, and the transformation of financial subjectivity.

candidates.title: Large testing of AI-based camera traps on a forest defoliating pest in Europe
candidates.abstract: Background Recent advances in AI-based surveillance technologies have shifted agricultural pest monitoring from reactive to proactive, yet their application to forest pests remains limited despite the need for efficient monitoring across large, remote and difficult-to-access forest landscapes. The pine processionary moth, Thaumetopoea pityocampa, is one of the most damaging forest pests in the Mediterranean region and a species undergoing climate-driven distributional and phenological shifts. Methods We evaluated the performance of the AI-based camera system for monitoring the insect under field conditions. Automated traps were compared with conventional traps across four European countries (France, Italy, Portugal, and Slovenia), encompassing contrasting habitats and population densities. We assessed trapping efficiency, automated image recognition accuracy, probability of early detection, relationships between adult trap catch and local nest density, environmental drivers of flight activity, and non-target captures. Results Automated traps consistently outperformed conventional traps by catching significantly more moths in France, Italy and Portugal, while demonstrating the same positive trend under the low-density conditions found in Slovenia. The smart trap also detected adult activity earlier and significantly increased the probability of detection during the first weeks of the flight season. Manual validation confirmed excellent performance of the AI recognition algorithm, with near-perfect precision, recall, F1-score, and overall accuracy throughout the flight season. For both trap types, adult trap catches showed positive and statistically significant relationships with subsequent nest density, indicating that higher catches were associated with greater larval infestation. The meteorological data provided synchronously by automated traps showed that temperature generally promoted moth flight activity, whereas high relative humidity hindered it. In addition, automated traps significantly reduced non-target catch compared to conventional traps. Conclusions Overall, this study provides the first large-scale evaluation of an AI-based camera trap for monitoring the pine processionary moth and demonstrates its considerable potential to improve forest pest surveillance.

candidates.title: Robots and Women in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Automation transforms the combination of tasks performed by machines and humans and reshapes labor markets by replacing and reinstating jobs. This article studies whether industrial robots affect the share of women in manufacturing employment and whether this mechanism depends on levels of female labor force participation. It constructs an industry-level panel dataset of eleven manufacturing industries across fourteen countries during 1993–2015. The article uses dynamic panel data models that control for the autocorrelation in female shares and endogenize robotization and female labor force participation. Robotization is associated with an increase in female shares in manufacturing employment. However, this positive association decreases as female labor force participation increases. The article also finds a similar conditional effect of robots in women's employment levels, but not for men's employment. Partitions of the sample suggest that the link between robotization and women in manufacturing varies according to preexisting industry-level labor productivity and income levels in the country.

candidates.title: The WoKaS-Iso database: workflow for a global compilation of oxygen-18 and deuterium records in karst springs and cave drip water for enhanced understanding of karst systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract. For analysing karst hydrogeological systems, observations of karst springs and cave drips are considered indispensable. In addition to hydrometric observations, knowing the oxygen and hydrogen stable isotope ratios has improved the understanding of vadose zone and aquifer dynamics, likewise supporting system characterisation and modelling. However, limited accessibility and high costs of the analysis of stable isotopes in karst aquifers have hindered progress in karst research and impeded the accurate understanding of karst processes especially when it comes to comparative or large-scale studies. In this study, we present our workflow to compile the WoKaS-Iso database, the first extensive collection of time series data for Oxygen-18 and Deuterium isotopes in karst springs and cave drip water from diverse sources, encompassing publications, theses, reports, online archives, and collaborative initiatives worldwide. The database incorporates data sourced from 236 springs and 74 caves, comprising in total 997 time series (379 time series for the springs and 618 time series for the cave drip water). These datasets provide coverage across significant karst regions globally, spanning China, the USA, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia. Within datasets, 79% for springs and 68% for cave drip water exhibit resolutions finer than monthly intervals. In addition, by integrating isotopic records with ancillary environmental variables including spring discharge, cave drip rate, precipitation, and rainwater isotopes, the database offers a more comprehensive perspective on hydrological behaviours in karst aquifers, hence advancing hydrogeological characterisation and modelling. The WoKaS-Iso database not only deepens the understanding of the complex systems but also promotes sustainable water resource management as well as the potential to foster collaborative research. The database can be accessed at: https://doi.org/10.25532/OPARA-909.

candidates.title: Sanitizing the stain: a critical integrative review of sportswashing discourse
candidates.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a critical integrative review of 45 peer-reviewed articles, identified through systematic searches of major academic databases. After two-stage screening, the corpus was analyzed qualitatively from an interpretive stance, using thematic synthesis followed by abductive theorization. Findings This study first maps the sportswashing ecosystem − stains, actors, motivations, mechanisms, phases and outcomes − revealing complexity and tensions pervading the literature. Building on this synthesis, it identifies five cleansing logics through which sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process: separation, dilution, displacement, containment and sanctification. Each logic illuminates how sportswashing operates as a contest over cultural classification through association without explicit claims. Research limitations/implications This synthesis advances a research agenda for interpretive marketing and consumer research, highlighting what qualitative inquiry could reveal about sportswashing across consumer resistance, platformization of consumer culture, CSR-washing, macromarketing, branding and reputation, marketing communications, market systems and critical and postcolonial marketing. Originality/value This paper theorizes sportswashing as a symbolic purification process, extending the CSR-washing literature from deception to associative classificatory work. Its five cleansing logics connect marketing scholarship on sponsorship, reputation, meaning transfer and brand activism; show how fan meaning-making and consumer resistance become embroiled in cultural-political reputation management; and reframe sportswashing as a contest over cultural classification, resolving persistent conceptual tensions.

OpenJaws: An Open Hardware UMI Framework with Stereo Localization for Generalist Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Handheld data-collection interfaces such as the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) allow manipulation demonstrations to be gathered in the wild without a robot in the loop, but the quality of the resulting action labels is bounded by the accuracy of vision-based localization. Existing systems recover end-effector pose from monocular visual-inertial odometry, which is subject to scale ambiguity and drift, or delegate tracking to closed-source modules and external infrastructure that reintroduce cost and setup burden. We present OpenJaws, a fully open hardware and software framework for sensorized UMI that improves localization and simplifies deployment across robot platforms. OpenJaws pairs a modular, 3D-printed gripper exposing a standardized ISO adapter with a low-cost stereo camera to recover metric camera trajectories. We further introduce UMI-Loc-Bench-v1, a benchmark quantifying real-world localization accuracy for handheld data-collection devices, and show that stereo localization substantially outperforms monocular alternatives. Finally, we demonstrate that policies trained on data collected with OpenJaws can be deployed on a real robot across multiple tasks. Hardware, software, and data are released under a commercially permissive license. Code, data, and videos are available at https://open-jaws.github.io/

candidates.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
candidates.abstract: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.

vibe‐qc : An Open‐Source, General‐Purpose Electronic‐Structure Code for Molecules and Solids Developed With Generative AI
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT We present vibe‐qc , a general‐purpose open‐source electronic‐structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely with agentic AI under expert human direction. The code is released under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPLv2). The implementation comprises a C++17 numerical core and Python calculation drivers. Molecular methods include Hartree–Fock, Kohn–Sham DFT, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster, active‐space methods, and excited states. Dispersion corrections, continuum solvation, and effective core potentials are also available. Periodic calculations use Gaussian‐basis HF and DFT with Brillouin‐zone sampling. Molecular and periodic method coverage differs; the feature matrices specify analytic and numerical derivatives and distinguish validated and experimental implementations. The validation set is a key contribution of this work. It combines independent program comparisons, published benchmarks, and internal consistency tests. Molecular mean‐field energies agree at the nanohartree scale, and conventional CCSD(T) energies agree within for the tested systems. Local‐correlation and periodic limitations are reported with the comparisons. Numerical results, calculation metadata, and analysis scripts are supplied as machine‐readable . The independently maintained vibe‐view viewer, vibe‐queue scheduler, and qvf toolkit support visualization and job management; trexio provides wavefunction interchange.

candidates.title: Off‐The‐Shelf Large Language Models Are Unreliable Judges
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT I conduct large‐scale empirical experiments to test the reliability of large language models (LLMs) as legal interpreters. Combining computational methods with the results of a new survey, I find that LLM judgments are highly sensitive to prompt phrasing, output processing methods, and choice of model. I also find that frontier LLMs do not accurately assess linguistic ordinary meaning, and I provide original evidence that tuning base models into assistant models shifts ordinary‐meaning judgments unpredictably and can worsen their alignment with human judgments. These findings undermine LLMs' credibility as legal interpreters and cast doubt on claims that LLMs elucidate ordinary meaning.

candidates.title: Allocating cognitive work across people, language models and deterministic tools: A task-analytic method
Liability for rogue behaviors of agentic AI
candidates.abstract: This article addresses liability for harm caused by rogue behaviors in agentic AI systems (AAI), such as specification gaming and deliberate deception. These harms stem from inherent AI vices - intrinsic, inevitable, and unpredictable rogue behaviors of AAI which cannot be fully eliminated with the current state of technological development. Current regulatory frameworks mainly focus on risk prevention but fail to address how liability should be allocated when harms do occur. In response, we conducted a game-theoretic analysis to study the optimal design of legal liability for unpredictable AAI harm caused by rogue behaviors under imperfect information. Our analysis shows that the optimal liability regime dynamically hinges on the explainability of the AAI system in question. Under this regime, courts can leverage industry-led explainability benchmarks to differentiate damages based on whether the developer can satisfactorily prove that the harm in question was caused by inherent vices. Under this arrangement, developers are incentivized to invest in explainability techniques to reduce both the risk of their AAI and their own liability exposure. Through this analysis, we demonstrate how a liability framework grounded in explainability can create economic incentives for developers to prioritize transparency and accountability of commercially available AAI.

candidates.title: Robust design of air chamber to enhance impact connection strength of magnetic connectors on modular truss robots
candidates.abstract: The connection mechanisms between neighboring modules are crucial subsystems in modular reconfigurable robot (MRR) systems. Magnetic connectors have been widely used for docking and undocking because of their mechanical simplicity and ease of use. However, they suffer from lower maximum tensile strength compared with mechanical docking mechanisms. This limitation is critical when modular truss robots are subjected to impact forces during locomotion, reconfiguration, docking, and undocking. To address this challenge, this paper presents a comprehensive parametric study and establishes design guidelines to maximize the impact resistance of magnetic connectors. As a core component of this approach, we investigate a mode-switching silicone air chamber designed to enhance impact absorption while mitigating the degradation of undocking capabilities. To evaluate the performance of the air chamber, we introduce an experimental evaluation method inspired by the Charpy impact test. Because the transient response of the soft structure is highly complex, the Taguchi and full factorial design method were employed to optimize the design parameters and derive the design guidelines. In the case of parameters, four factors were selected that could be judged to have an impact on the pneumatic stiffness, structural flexibility, and fluid damping of the air chamber. Also, each design parameter was divided into three levels, and five replicate experiments were conducted for each combination using an \(L_9(3^4)\) orthogonal array. The performance metrics consist of the sum of weighted values of \(M_1\) , which indicates the air chamber’s resistance to impact, and \(M_2\) , which reflects the indicator of mode switching between opening and closing the air chamber’s bottom hole. To explore the vicinity of the optimal value identified in the first experiment, a second experiment was conducted to pinpoint the final optimal parameter configuration, achieving a metric improvement of 0.051969 over the worst-case scenario. Finally, the practical feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed design guidelines were demonstrated through a hardware model using a prototype connector within a configured MRR system, demonstrating connection retention under selected impact conditions.

candidates.title: Fast and Robust Actuation of Continuum Robots via Antagonistic Tendons
candidates.abstract: Tendon driven continuum robots (TDCRs) exhibit extraordinary dexterity and navigability in highly constrained workspaces, for example, in minimally invasive surgery or industrial inspection and repair tasks. The curvilinear nature of these robots, with their extreme diameter-to-length ratios, enables them to dexterously navigate around obstacles in their environment to reach their goals. However, the dynamic properties of these highly deformable mechanisms make them challenging to operate autonomously at high speeds, and the presence of external loads can significantly impact the accuracy of kinematic models. In this work, we present a compact, low-cost, modular tendon robot actuation platform with fast and stable open-loop dynamics. We explore how pretensioned antagonistic pairs can enable repeatable actuation at high bandwidths using our low-cost hardware setup. Secondly, we show how intrinsic sensing using only motor currents and displacement can be used to improve the shape estimate of the robot when manipulating unknown objects at its tip, without any additional sensors. In this work, we show how high-performance continuum robots can be achieved with relatively low-cost components through the mechanical design of the actuation structure and by leveraging existing information available from the actuators in the computational modeling of these systems.

candidates.title: Design and Construction of a Low-Cost, Open-Source Syringe-Based Pipetting Robot Using 3D Printing and Common Hardware Parts
candidates.abstract: Abstract Automation in chemical laboratories improves the reproducibility, precision, and efficiency in liquid handling. A three-dimensional (3D)-printed, stepper-actuated pipetting robot was developed and tested via silver nitrate (AgNO3) experiments. The system employs a rigid 3D-printed frame to secure syringes and tubing, stepper motors for plunger actuation, and microcontroller-based software to automate the pipetting sequences. The robot was evaluated for volume accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanical reliability using 5 mL syringes. The results indicate consistent volume delivery and stable mechanical performance over multiple cycles. Detailed mechanical, electrical, and software specifications are provided to enable replication and customization in other laboratories.

candidates.title: An open-source, 3D-printable droplet microfluidics platform with strobe-enhanced microscopy
candidates.abstract: Droplet microfluidics underpins many single-cell, precision biomedical, and nanomaterial techniques. However, implementing these methods reproducibly remains challenging outside specialised laboratories due to high equipment costs, operational inflexibility, mechanical impracticality at the microscope stage, as well as open-source pumping solutions that are inadequately validated for low-flow stability. We present an accessible, research-grade, open-source droplet microfluidics platform integrating a compact, microfluidics-optimised microscopy stage with networked syringe-pump control. Designed for local digital fabrication, primarily 3D printing, and widely available components, the platform supports reproducible builds across diverse settings. This setup enables stable droplet generation, observation of rapid droplet dynamics, and automation-ready networked workflows. The microscopy module uses a Raspberry Pi camera and microsecond stroboscopic illumination to capture sharp images of fast-moving droplets without the need for a high-speed camera. A modular hardware interface and extensible, web-accessible software stack provide a path to integrate additional modules and laboratory automation beyond the configuration evaluated here. For infusion, we introduce an open-source syringe pump optimised for low reliable flow rather than maximum rates, combining gearbox-assisted stepper mechanics with workflow-centric control that enables manual intervention (keypad control) and remote operation (web interface and automation hooks). We benchmark droplet regimes, size tuning, and time-stability under low-flow conditions (between 25 and 2500 µL/h) relevant to advanced assays and demonstrate biomedical readiness through the encapsulation and incubation of cells, beads, and bacteria in monodisperse droplets. The platform has been replicated across laboratories in Latin America and globally, including independent builds, supporting reproducibility. All design files, firmware/software, analysis notebooks, and benchmark datasets are openly released.

candidates.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
candidates.abstract: Many robot manipulation videos do not indicate whether the task was successfully completed. RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that takes a task instruction, 10 frames of a manipulation attempt, and (if available) final frames from auxiliary cameras and predicts whether the robot accomplished the task. RoboJev-27B is a variant of JEV-27B-VL, trained with a rank-32 LoRA adapter on the language model only (keeping the vision encoder frozen) using 52,598 episode records. It also uses a source-specific KL penalty that applies only to research data, anchoring predictions closer to the original model on those sources. It uses a calibrated two-token readout that outputs success/failure probabilities in a single forward pass. On 268 held-out episodes of the same robot model (SO-101), RoboJev-27B attains 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC. It also generalises to episodes collected by unseen labs/robots (AUROC = 0.890 over 459 episodes) as well as to clearly labelled community-collected episodes (accuracy = 93.3% over 135 episodes), where the base model attains an AUROC = 0.900 on the unseen-lab/robot subset with the same inputs. It takes 0.26 seconds per episode (median, serial) to infer on a single H100, which is about \$0.19 per 1,000 success predictions at \$2.69 per GPU-hour (not including media processing and serving costs). RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection. We also compare against strong API-based frontier VLMs, which take in fewer input frames (4 images from the primary camera only); note that this comparison is not strictly like-for-like because RoboJev-27B is given more frames at inference.

candidates.title: Collision Avoidance Path Planning for Mobile Robots Using an Improved Bi-RRT Algorithm*
candidates.abstract: Abstract To address the high path redundancy, poor smoothness, and low planning efficiency exhibited by the Bi-directional Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (Bi-RRT) algorithm in complex dynamic environments, an improved Bi-RRT* algorithm for collision avoidance path planning in mobile robots is proposed. The method employs a Social LSTM network to predict the trajectories of dynamic obstacles. The predicted positions over a 3-second horizon are utilized to guide real-time obstacle avoidance decisions. A bidirectional target-biased sampling strategy and an adaptive step-size mechanism are adopted to enhance search efficiency and adaptability in dynamic environments. Additionally, a via-node optimization is introduced to eliminate redundant nodes in the initial path. Finally, the generated path is smoothed using a cubic Cardinal spline. Experimental results demonstrate that in mixed obstacle scenarios, the average planning time is reduced by 52.1%, the path length is shortened by 12.5%, the success rate reaches 96.7%, and the average curvature is decreased by 62.2% compared with the BD‑RRT algorithm. These findings validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in terms of real‑time performance, smoothness, and kinematic feasibility.

candidates.title: Visuomotor coordination on the road: Low-dimensional representations reveal adaptive, context-dependent reductions in the dimensionality of natural driving behavior
candidates.abstract: The brain's ability to transform complex, high-dimensional sensory and motor inputs into coordinated, goal-directed behavior remains a central challenge in neuroscience research. Current research suggests that behavior is generated through patterns within a low-dimensional structure. What visuomotor patterns underlie complex, unconstrained behaviors such as driving, and how stereotypical they are, remain poorly understood. Driving involves complex perception-action interactions, which we hypothesize are specific to the driver's role and adapt to task demands. Here, we unfold these dynamics using an immersive virtual drive that recreates ten hazardous on-road events. We collected eye, head, and vehicle movements from participants assigned to either a manual or an automated driving condition. From the behavioral movements of 284 drivers, we constructed a common time-resolved behavioral state space based on collective variance, computed via principal component analysis across participants. The obtained low-dimensional representation thus captures generalized visuomotor coordination strategies. We then characterized the evolving low-dimensional structure with cosine similarity and various measures of effective dimensionality. We tested whether leading components contained condition-specific information using discriminant analysis. Throughout the entire drive, few components accounted for most of the variance in behavior, and effective dimensionality decreased reliably around critical events, indicating tighter coordination between perceptual and motor variables. During periods of low effective dimensionality, the contributions of eye, head, steering, and vehicle heading reorganized toward leading dimensions in a task-dependent manner. Across events, between-subject similarity was partially stable and stronger among manual drivers. This reorganization also made behaviors more distinct across driving conditions, enabling better classification of driving modes using only the first two components. These results show that naturalistic driving is supported by shared low-dimensional visuomotor coordination strategies that are flexibly reshaped by contextual demands, and provide a principled behavioral framework for linking neural manifolds, human driver models, and the design of adaptive automated vehicles.

candidates.title: Proceedings of NORA's Annual Meeting 2026
candidates.abstract: NORA - The Norwegian Artificial Intelligence Research Consortium - works to strengthen Norwegian research, education and innovation within the fields of AI, machine learning and robotics. NORA is a collaboration between 9 universities, 4 university colleges and 4 research institutes. The current article provides a summary of NORA’s annual conference 2026.

candidates.title: Offensive–Defensive Codesign
candidates.abstract: This chapter addresses the insufficiency of isolated offensive and defensive AI strategies in modern cybersecurity by proposing codesign through joint protocols and shared testbeds. Central to the framework is red/blue co-training, wherein adversarial and defensive agents evolve simultaneously through iterative cycles that mirror the continuous adaptation in real-world cyber conflict. Curriculum learning structures this coevolution by escalating scenario complexity—from basic credential theft and anomaly detection to multi-stage advanced persistent threats—preventing premature convergence and ensuring diverse skill formation. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) formalizes competitive and cooperative dynamics under partial observability, with balanced reward structures that sustain adversarial pressure. Human-in-the-loop augmentation introduces expert oversight to correct unsafe behaviors, refine policy alignment, and enforce operational risk tolerances. Adversarial playgrounds—including simulated network environments, scenario-driven testing mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, dynamically adaptive topologies, and hybrid testbeds incorporating real hardware—provide controlled infrastructure for evaluating agent coevolution with high fidelity. Benchmark-governance charters, dataset provenance records, ablation requirements, and signed reproducibility packages enforce scientific rigor across co-training evaluations. A cross-national laboratory case study demonstrates how governed benchmarks, mandatory partner-lab replication, and transparent failure reporting produce credible, peer-reviewed findings, including traceable retractions. Incremental shadow-mode deployment and phased security information and event management (SIEM) integration complete the transition from laboratory codesign to operationally resilient practice.

candidates.title: From Static Classrooms to Living Systems
candidates.abstract: This chapter explores how Digital twins (DTs) are changing in their roles across the educational spectrum. DTs play both theoretical and practical roles, facilitating immersive, feedback-intensive and personal experiences beyond traditional simulations. DTs in life sciences and agricultural engineering enable safe, repeatable and data-rich learning environments where learners can practice realistic simulations of poultry farm management, disease control and performance analytics without endangering living animals in the laboratory. DTs have been applied to reinvent introductory programming education in computing education. DTs have been identified as potential solutions for schools in developing countries such as Mozambique and Rwanda that lack physical laboratory facilities. In chemical engineering education, virtual reality twins of extraction columns enable interactive manipulation of flow parameters and AI-based image analysis to optimize droplet size, introducing students to the fusion of process control and data analytics in an accessible, hardware-light format.

candidates.title: Replication Package for the Paper "Evolving Agentic Configuration Artifacts in the Open-Source: An Empirical Study"
candidates.abstract: Replication package of the paper "Evolving Agentic Configuration Artifacts in the Open-Source: An Empirical Study" (anonymous submission). The study mines the agentic configuration files of 45,333 GitHub repositories, with their git history: agent skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, Copilot instructions, Claude Code subagents and commands, rules, settings, hooks and MCP configurations. An LLM labels the files and their contents. The analyses measure:- what skills contain and where they are used (RQ1);- how they are maintained after their introduction (RQ2);- which files change together with them (RQ3);- the activity of repositories after they adopt agentic files. The package holds the mined dataset, the data derived from it, the final codebooks, every result as data, the scripts that produced them (comments removed), the prompts sent to the model, and the study design (methodology.pdf). README.md describes every folder. Files- One zip per folder: codebooks, prompts, data_collection, extra_counts, qualitative_analysis, quantitative_analysis, results_catalog.- The two largest folders as multi-volume RAR archives: Data (Data.part01.rar to Data.part09.rar) and work (work.part01.rar to work.part41.rar).- Not archived: README.md, methodology.pdf, requirements.txt, the licenses and the checksums. Rebuilding the packageDownload all files into one folder. Extract there every zip and the first volume of each RAR archive (Data.part01.rar, work.part01.rar); WinRAR, 7-Zip or unrar read the other volumes. The result is the folder described in README.md, about 50 GB. The scripts need Python 3.12 and Node.js 24 (requirements.txt and the package.json files). Checksums (SHA-256)- CHECKSUMS.sha256: every file of the package- zips.sha256: the zips- parts.sha256: the Data volumes- work_parts.sha256: the work volumes LicensesData under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt), code under MIT (LICENSE-CODE.txt). Mined contents keep the license of their repository.

candidates.title: The ‘good mobile’: a mobile launcher for children to facilitate human interactions
candidates.abstract: Children today grow up in a hybrid physical and digital environment, engaging with mobile devices from an early age, which poses a risk of negatively impacting their development. This usage often replaces social interactions and physical activities, potentially deteriorating relationships, socio-cognitive skills, and mental health. Banning device use is unrealistic, but the way children use mobiles can be altered through responsible technology. In the present study we (1) explored parental expectations regarding children's mobile applications, (2) directlyincorporated these expectations into the design of a specific application (Alphie), and (3) examined its reception through UX testing. Alphie is a child-focused application (launcher) that promotes social interaction, real-world activities, and reduces solitary screen time. Its design is informed by parental expectations and scientific data, emphasizing educational, age-appropriate, and moderately stimulating content, with parental control features. A user study with parent-child dyads showed positive experiences. Notably, the games requiring active parental involvement were also well-received, suggesting that they are effective tools for facilitating joint activities within the family. This research highlights how responsible technology can support the mental and physical health of the new generation. By linking parental expectations, application design, and user experience within a single framework, the present studyprovides a more integrative perspective on the development and evaluation of child-focused digital applications.

candidates.title: Digital Mediation, Selfhood, and Hybrid Agency: A Minimal Three-Dimensional Framework
Discovering supernovae in the Virgo Cluster during the LSST era
candidates.abstract: In the era of unprecedentedly wide, deep and high-cadence sky surveys the chance for discovering new explosive transients in nearby, rich galaxy clusters within hours after explosion is expected to increase dramatically. In this paper we focus on the Virgo cluster ($D \simeq 16.5$ Mpc), and estimate the expected numbers of new, very young supernovae in different sub-structures and galaxy types of the cluster during the proposed lifetime (~10 years) of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) by the Vera Rubin Observatory. These predictions will be tested observationally during the ongoing Shadow-LSST discovery and follow-up program led by University of Arizona in the upcoming years.

candidates.title: UMaPP: Universal Maize Phenotyping Platform - A low-cost, open-source robotic manipulator-based imaging system for three-dimensional maize reconstruction and trait measurement
candidates.abstract: This repository provides the CAD design files, control software, and experimental output data associated with the Universal Maize Phenotyping Platform (UMaPP), a low-cost, open-source robotic imaging system developed for non-destructive 3D maize phenotyping. UMaPP uses a modified robotic manipulator, a single RGB camera, and controlled illumination to acquire multi-view images for photogrammetric 3D reconstruction. The repository includes hardware designs, software for automated image acquisition and robotic control, and experimental results used to evaluate plant architectural traits, including plant height and leaf length. These resources are shared to support reproducibility, system replication, and further development of open-source plant phenotyping technologies.

candidates.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
candidates.abstract: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.

candidates.title: Benefits and Harms of Adult Videos: A Sex Difference Social Representations Analysis Among Young Adults in Japan
candidates.abstract: Pornhub Insights (2025) reported that Japan ranked 11th worldwide in total traffic, indicating widespread use of adult videos (AV). Existing research has primarily focused on AV-related harms from expert and Western perspectives. Few studies examine how Japanese young adults perceive these effects, particularly the benefits that sustain use, and sex differences remain underexplored. This study investigated the core social representations of AV benefits and harms and how they differ by sex. Data were collected from 251 Japanese participants, of whom 137 (54.6%) were male, with a mean age of 20.71 years. Most participants (81.3%) reported using AV, and most identified as heterosexual students. Data were analyzed using prototypical analysis to identify elements with high consensus. Five key observations emerged: (1) Both genders see "satisfaction," "pleasure," and "crime prevention" as key benefits of AV. (2) Sex differences appeared in describing benefits, with men mentioning "sex education" and women mentioning "stress relief." (3) Both genders identified "incorrect knowledge" as a primary representation of AV-related harms. (4) Male respondents cited "addiction" as a harm, whereas female respondents were more likely to reference "encouraging sexual crime." (5) More words or phrases were used to describe AV benefits than harms. These findings may inform targeted interventions and policy discussions.

candidates.title: Social chatbots and character: Mind-modelling, mimetics, and postdigital misperception
candidates.abstract: This article examines how users cognitively process social chatbot output as a novel form of participatory, generative “character,” co-produced through human–AI interaction. Reporting on the results of empirical research on user responses to the social chatbot platform character.ai, it shows how cognitive stylistic and narratological approaches to character can be utilised but also must be developed to analyse and theorise users’ experience of and interaction with generative AI agents. It makes specific contributions to cognitive stylistics, rhetorical narratology, character studies, and research on gen AI chatbots by: (1) illustrating how the concept of mind-modelling can used to analyse the ways in which users linguistically anthropomorphise social chatbots; (2) developing two new audience response types – transmimetic and hypermimetic – to respectively capture ways in which users assess chatbots against prior knowledge of characters across media and cases where chatbots appear so convincingly human that users question their ontological status; (3) proposing the concept of ‘postdigital misperception’ to reflect the way that users of AI can misattribute the ontological origin of an LLM’s output. The article demonstrates how social chatbots are reshaping how users understand character, agency, and reality in interactive, participatory and generative digital contexts and argues that social chatbots epitomise postdigital experience in blurring the distinction between the digital and non-digital as well as fictional and real.

candidates.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives
candidates.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.

candidates.title: AI-Based Elderly Health Monitoring and Emergency Assistance Robot
candidates.abstract: The increasing demand for elderly healthcare has encouraged the development of smart assistive technologies that support independent living and improve patient safety. This review paper examines existing research on intelligent healthcare solutions, focusing on vital sign monitoring, fall detection, medication management, and robotic assistance. It evaluates the techniques used in these systems, highlighting their major benefits, technical limitations, and areas requiring further investigation. The review identifies the need for a unified solution capable of combining multiple healthcare functions rather than relying on separate devices or applications. To address this gap, an AI-based elderly health monitoring and emergency assistance robot is proposed, integrating health sensors, intelligent event detection, and IoT-enabled communication. The proposed approach aims to facilitate timely emergency notifications, improve caregiver accessibility, and provide a more reliable support system for elderly individuals.

candidates.title: InstMeter: An Instruction-Level Method to Predict Energy and Latency of DL Model Inference on MCUs
candidates.abstract: Deep learning (DL) models can now run on microcontrollers (MCUs). Through neural architecture search (NAS), we can search DL models that meet the constraints of MCUs. Among various constraints, energy and latency costs of the model inference are critical metrics. To predict them, existing research relies on coarse proxies such as multiply-accumulations (MACs) and model's input parameters, often resulting in inaccurate predictions or requiring extensive data collection. In this paper, we propose InstMeter, a predictor leveraging MCUs' clock cycles to accurately estimate the energy and latency of DL models. Clock cycles are fundamental metrics reflecting MCU operations, directly determining energy and latency costs. Furthermore, a unique property of our predictor is its strong linearity, allowing it to be simple and accurate. We thoroughly evaluate InstMeter under different scenarios, MCUs, and software settings. Compared with state-of-the-art studies, InstMeter can reduce the energy and latency prediction errors by 3× and 6.5×, respectively, while requiring 100× and 10× less training data. In the NAS scenario, InstMeter can fully exploit the energy budget, identifying optimal DL models with higher inference accuracy. We also evaluate InstMeter's generalization performance through various experiments on three ARM MCUs (Cortex-M4, M7, M33) and one RISC-V-based MCU (ESP32-C3), different compilation options (-Os, -O2), GCC versions (v7.3, v10.3), application scenarios (keyword spotting, image recognition), dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, temperatures (21°C, 43°C), and software settings (TFLMv2.4, TFLMvCI). Our source codes and the MCU-specific benchmark datasets are available here: https://github.com/haoliu001/InstMeter.

candidates.title: Experimental reasoning in large language models
candidates.abstract: Abstract Scientific reasoning requires interaction with the physical world: designing experiments, interpreting outcomes, and deciding what experiment should come next. Here we show that general-purpose large language models (LLMs) already possess substantial capabilities for experimental reasoning. We connected LLMs to a liquid-handling robot and camera through PEARL, which provides perception, action, and persistent state. Given objectives rather than prescribed workflows, the system designed and successfully executed experiments, interpreted observations, and revised its approach as evidence accumulated. When information was insufficient, PEARL autonomously designed and performed intermediate experiments to acquire it. In quantitative enzyme characterization, it judged whether measurements were sufficient, new data were required, or conditions needed to change. Across eight scenarios, these behaviors were reliable with limited agent scaffolding and no supplied scenario-specific recovery recipes. More broadly, general-purpose LLMs may provide a reasoning layer between scientific objectives and physical experimentation, shifting laboratory automation from executing predefined procedures toward AI systems that participate directly in the experimental process.

candidates.title: The Life of a Showgirl as a Cultural Artifact: What's Hidden by the Lipstick and Lace?
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a collage-based framework to holistically assess Taylor Swift’s highly anticipated first release after the Eras Tour concluded. The Life of a Showgirl, with sparkling promotional materials leading up to its October 2025 drop and polarizing critical reception following it, represents an entertainer’s lifestyle while still concealing what was alluded to behind the Eras Tour curtain. Rather than engage in a direct response to Showgirl, I critically evaluate positive and negative commentary from listeners regarding the album, and I thematically analyze lyrical concepts throughout Swift’s discography to contextualize Showgirl within the arc of her work. I find that discussion of The Life of a Showgirl is rooted in four primary topics that I refer to as Muse, Lyricism, Artistic Integrity, and Political Implications, and I place notable significance on listener-driven aspects of the Showgirl era. I further argue that such discourse constitutes important pedagogical processes and reinforces pop culture as not only entertainment or commercialization, but as a broad infrastructure for learning outside of formal settings. Listeners of The Life of a Showgirl and consumers of related media negotiate complex ideas about authenticity, authority, and creative labor.

candidates.title: Interpretation of National Values in Uzbek Theater: Historical Evolution and Modern Processes
candidates.abstract: This article analyzes the organic connection between national values and Uzbek theater from historical, theoretical, and practical perspectives. It provides a scholarly examination of the ways in which national values, traditions, and spiritual-enlightenment ideas have been interpreted on stage throughout the various stages of the formation and development of Uzbek national theater—encompassing the era of Jadidism, the Soviet period, and the era of independence.

candidates.title: Flexible Language-Guided Representation Editing for Adaptive Robot Behavior
candidates.abstract: Trajectory demonstrations show robots how to behave but not why, leaving them to guess which features of the task actually matter. Incorrect guesses produce misaligned internal representations and lead to incorrect robot behaviors. Because task features are often semantically defined, we argue that natural language is better suited for specifying features rather than relying on demonstrations. Although existing representation editing methods have proposed using language to specify new features, only allowing additive edits produces feature sets that are often over-specified or too narrowly scoped, especially in sequential editing tasks. We propose the Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline (FLEX), which uses language models to iteratively refine a robot's internal representation of task features from natural language corrections via three complementary operations: Add missing features, Generalize existing specific features, and Mask irrelevant features. We evaluate FLEX on 2D navigation scenarios, 7DoF Franka tabletop manipulation tasks, and a real-world study using naturalistic human language corrections and real-robot demonstrations. Comparisons against single-operation and unscaffolded baselines show that all three operations are necessary in interactive scenarios, and that FLEX achieves consistently higher normalized reward compared to other feature editing approaches while maintaining compact, transferable representations. Project available at https://mit-clear-lab.github.io/FLEX/

candidates.title: From “how” to learn to “what” to learn in multiagent systems and robotics
candidates.abstract: Abstract There remains much more to Artificial Intelligence than understanding how to learn with neural networks. Inspired in part by how babies, and humans in general, tend to choose for themselves what (and when ) to learn in addition to how to learn, this article discusses similar opportunities, in the areas of multiagent systems and robotics. Grounded in past research on the topic, it categorizes opportunities for choosing what to learn as coming from task decomposition or simplification for difficult problems and/or large environments; unsupervised pre‐training of representations and priors; multiagent learning; and learning from human interaction. The article is based closely on a keynote talk with the same title, delivered at the AAAI‐2026 conference in Singapore on January 22nd, 2026.
