candidates.title: CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection
candidates.abstract: We present CAST-ASD (Causal Attention over Speakers and Time), a causal joint model for active speaker detection (ASD). Recent ASD models improve performance by jointly processing all faces in a scene, but operate offline, with the full clip available before any frame is labelled. Low-latency causal detectors instead process each face independently. CAST-ASD combines joint face reasoning with fully causal inference. It applies scene-level attention across faces within the current frame and causal temporal attention over each face's history, enabling information sharing across speakers with zero lookahead. Its parameter count does not grow with the number of faces. On MSDWild, where most negative face-frames contain a visible competing speaker, CAST-ASD reduces competing-speaker false alarms by 32% relative to the causal per-face detector it extends, with larger gains as scene occupancy increases. It outperforms all causal baselines on both validation splits while using only one-tenth the inter-speaker parameters of a three-block fixed-roster convolution. Code and models are available at https://github.com/prathamg007/CAST-ASD.

candidates.title: Design for Machinability: Topology Optimization for Subtractive Machining Using Trimmed Neural Fields
candidates.abstract: Topology optimization has found significant utility in additive manufacturing, but the resulting geometries are often difficult to realize using subtractive methods. The complex, curved surfaces of optimized designs typically require time-consuming point milling operations. In contrast, geometries composed of developable surfaces are well suited to flank milling, enabling substantial improvements in machining efficiency and surface quality. However, globally minimizing Gaussian curvature leads to overly simplistic designs. We address this challenge with a novel method that represents geometry using three implicit neural fields, optimized to produce machinable components. The resulting designs consist of regions of developable surfaces separated by seamlines where curvature is concentrated. Seamlines are efficiently computed as intersections of the implicit fields, while the geometry emerges through their product. By constraining surfaces to align with the cutter’s normal or tangential direction, our approach further accommodates practical constraints of 3-axis machining. We demonstrate concurrent optimization of topology and Gaussian curvature, enabling control over seamline feature scale. Compared to methods that enforce subtractive machinability without considering milling efficiency, our approach consistently reduces machining time while maintaining competitive structural performance.

candidates.title: A deep hybrid feature extraction model based on MobileNet and vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia prediction
candidates.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from peripheral blood smear images can support microscopic screening, but reliable evaluation requires both discriminative feature learning and transparent reporting of the experimental protocol. This study presents MoViTHAFX-Net, a hybrid MobileNet–Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) and Grad-CAM++ visualization for binary classification of ALL blasts and healthy hematogones (HEM) using the 10,661 labelled cell images in the training component of the C-NMC 2019 dataset. MobileNet extracts local morphological information, whereas ViT models long-range contextual relationships. HAF first refines the two branches and then adaptively combines three learnable morphology-guided feature projections before binary classification. The reported experiment uses an image-level stratified partition containing 7462 training images, 1600 validation images, and 1599 held-out test images; augmentation is restricted to the training partition. On the held-out test partition, the model correctly classified 1583 of 1599 images, corresponding to 99.00% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 0.990 and an AUC of 0.99. Ablation results within the same experimental setting indicate an incremental advantage of HAF over direct CNN–ViT concatenation. Grad-CAM++ is used as a qualitative post hoc visualization of image regions contributing to predictions. Because the reported custom split is image-level rather than subject-disjoint and evaluation is limited to a single benchmark dataset, the results should be interpreted as internal benchmark performance rather than evidence of patient-independent or multicentre clinical generalization.

candidates.title: The 2026 World Cup, Anime Edition: Production, Engagement, and Circulation of Generative Memetic Sports Content
candidates.abstract: Generative AI gives audiences new ways to portray real sporting figures through familiar fictional worlds. Expanded opportunities to create, however, need not broaden cultural representation or distribute attention evenly. We examine this tension through the supply, demand, and circulation of anime style football videos on Instagram. Using 2,021 posts and associated video and account data, we combine caption entity extraction, human-reviewed visual identity clustering, engagement analysis, and content-reuse networks. Representation is uneven across athletes, while Blue Lock, Naruto, and One Piece account for 60.1% of explicit franchise mentions. Among posts referencing generative tools, rankings by total engagement differ from rankings by average engagement per video, distinguishing aggregate visibility from response to individual posts. Reuse is extensive: 772 of 1,548 evaluated videos belong to 124 detected groups, including 71 spanning multiple known accounts. Shared material connects a large account component alongside smaller groups, and later observed uploads receive lower median normalized engagement than first observed appearances. These findings characterize generative cultural crossover as a practice organized around concentrated cultural resources, uneven attention, and extensive recirculation. More broadly, they distinguish opportunities for visual authorship from the processes through which particular representations become widely visible.

candidates.title: Future of Anticipatory Robotics in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Collaborative robots, designed to work alongside humans in shared environments, are transforming manufacturing production lines, enabling partial automation and boosting productivity. But their potential extends beyond these benefits. By implementing anticipatory strategies to prevent workers’ risky behaviours and reduce excessive workloads, collaborative robots can proactively enhance working conditions. For example, they can take on repetitive or strenuous tasks to reduce physical effort or adjust the pace of operations to help alleviate stress levels. Indeed, Musculoskeletal Disorders (MSDs) and Common Mental Disorders (CMDs), which arise from uncontrolled physical and cognitive loads, are major work-related health problems in developed countries, with incommensurate social and economic costs. Collaborative robots can curb the effect of such disorders and help in preserving workers’ health. This Chapter addresses how Human Factors and Ergonomics (HFE) can be monitored to provide robots with relevant inputs about the human state, and how robots can be employed to improve HFE. Novel strategies are proposed to adapt online robot behaviour to the workers’ psycho-physical state and enhance their well-being and productivity.

candidates.title: Design and development of IoT based solar power agriculture robot
candidates.abstract: Agriculture in developing economies such as Pakistan remains heavily dependent on manual labor and single-purpose, grid or fuel-powered machinery that is often unaffordable for smallholder farmers. This paper presents the design, fabrication, and experimental evaluation of a multifunctional, solar-powered, Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled agricultural robot capable of performing soil cultivation, seed placement, irrigation, and crop cutting within a single integrated platform. The system architecture is built around an ESP32 microcontroller that interfaces with a DHT11 temperature/humidity sensor, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic obstacle sensor, an ESP32-CAM module for visual field monitoring, an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver, and relay-controlled actuators, with energy supplied by a 20 W photovoltaic panel, a 12 V/7.2 Ah battery, and a battery management system (BMS). Mechanical subsystems comprising a tooth-type cultivator, a soil-leveling roller, a servo-actuated seed dispenser, a DC pump-based irrigation unit, and a blade-type cutter were designed in CAD, fabricated, and integrated onto a four-wheel-drive chassis. Engineering calculations were used to size the power budget, battery backup, drive-motor torque, structural factor of safety, seeding rate, and irrigation flow. Field trials show a typical operating power demand of 24.4 W against an average usable solar output of 11–12 W, a battery backup of approximately 3.5 h, The experimental results demonstrated satisfactory performance of the proposed agricultural robot, achieving an average seed-placement accuracy of 74.45% over 11 experimental trials. The developed system also successfully performed soil digging, irrigation, crop cutting, obstacle detection, and real-time IoT-based remote monitoring, demonstrating its suitability for sustainable precision agriculture.

candidates.title: Defective, Amplified, Contested: Folk Conceptualizations of AI Slop
candidates.abstract: AI slop has flooded social media feeds with overprocessed and derivative content--Jesus fusing with a shrimp, a humanoid orange chubby cat shoplifting, and a "hero" dog rescuing a human child after a plane crash. This might be no laughing matter, as waves of media coverage have taken a distinctly negative bent, emphasizing its low quality, ethical concerns, and threats to human creativity. Despite extensive attention from politicians and technologists, the perspectives of everyday users--the very audience most exposed to this phenomenon--remain largely unexplored. This descriptive work explored how Reddit users experience, conceptualize and contest AI slop. Inductive thematic analysis of posts and comments across six slop-related subreddits identified four themes covering constitutional defects, algorithmic overreach, user resistance, and entertainment outcomes--ranging from anxieties about eroding agency, moral norms, creativity, and existential questions to defensive distinctions between quality AI content and slop. We derive a user-driven definition: AI slop is audience-contested AI-generated content characterized by constitutional defects and enabled by platform logics. We operationalize slop through a facet-theoretical framework to inform future research into this fuzzy category.

candidates.title: SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
candidates.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) predict a robot's actions together with the observations those actions will produce. However, the strongest models rely on video diffusion transformers that are far too computationally expensive for resource-constrained edge devices. We present SmolWAM, a latent WAM that we derive from the 2B-parameter Cosmos Policy by keeping its pretrained trunk and rebuilding its inference interface: single-frame visual latents, cached text features that preserve the trunk's attention sinks, 12 of 28 transformer blocks, and 1,008 tokens from which actions and future visual latents are read out in one rectified-flow step. Trained in 3.6 GPU-hours, SmolWAM succeeds in 95.5% of 400 LIBERO episodes at 57 ms and 2.3 TFLOP per 16-action chunk with 2.4 GiB of GPU memory, 11x faster than its teacher with 18.5x fewer FLOPs and 3.2x less memory, and its world head still forecasts scene motion.

candidates.title: NÁYU UNIVERSAL LANGUAGE RESEARCH CONCEPT
candidates.abstract: NÁYU — Global Validation Challenge: A 10-Page Open Research Protocol NÁYU is an early-stage universal scratch language concept exploring whether a deliberately designed language can support simple human communication and predictable processing by AI systems, software, edge devices, IoT systems, and robotics interfaces. This document introduces the proposed sound inventory, core syllable combinations, prototype grammar, and a global research challenge inviting independent evaluation. It outlines experimental methods for assessing human learnability, multilingual accessibility, AI model interpretation, deterministic parsing, computational resource usage, edge-device performance, and robotics safety. It also proposes benchmark metrics, comparison methods, visualization ideas, reproducibility requirements, and a staged validation roadmap. Research status: Conceptual proposal requiring further specification, implementation, testing, and independent validation. The document does not claim that NÁYU is a proven universal language or that its performance advantages have been experimentally established. The objective is to encourage transparent, reproducible research and collaboration among AI researchers, universities, linguists, software engineers, embedded-systems developers, and robotics teams. Central research question: Can we design a language humans can learn, software can validate, AI can reason over, and future devices can process efficiently? Author: Chigateri RajeshaVersion: 1.0Date: October 2026

candidates.title: Field Notes from a Low-Cost Robot Learning Lab: Hardware Churn, Software Whiplash, and What Actually Went Wrong
candidates.abstract: This is the informal companion to two more rigorous papers from the same project. Over roughly seven weeks we trained imitation-learning policies on a self-built SO-101 robot arm, and along the way we moved the work between machines more often than planned, rebuilt the camera setup, fought a fast-moving open-source framework, and lost an embarrassing amount of time to causes that turned out to be a loose power cable, a swapped port, or a missing audio package. The quantified findings are reported elsewhere. Here we tell the rest: what the hardware and software path actually looked like, which incidents cost us the most time and why, what we would warn a newcomer about, and which threads we deliberately left unfinished. We write for people building something similar on a hobbyist budget, not for reviewers, and we try to be as candid about our mistakes as about our results.

candidates.title: Occupational Wearable Robotics
candidates.abstract: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

candidates.title: Blockchain Security: An Empirical Evaluation of High‐Impact Exploits and Detection Tools
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Blockchain introduced secure, peer‐to‐peer transactions in decentralized environments without reliance on central authorities. However, attackers continue to exploit blockchain projects. Over the past decade, reported blockchain exploit losses have exceeded $24 billion. Although existing research analyzes blockchain vulnerabilities and real‐world incidents, many studies focus on specific vulnerability classes or smart contract issues only. Therefore, we present an empirical study of major blockchain exploits from 2020 to 2025. Based on detailed analysis of these exploits, we introduce a practitioner‐oriented taxonomy that organizes the dominant root causes observed in the analyzed exploits across four domains: Human Risks, Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities, Private Key Compromises, and Smart Contract Vulnerabilities. Across these categories, we present case studies, code illustrations where applicable, and mitigation strategies. Moreover, we evaluate five vulnerability‐detection tools spanning four paradigms, namely static analysis ( Slither , 4naly3er ), symbolic execution ( Mythril ), bounded/formal verification ( SMTChecker ), and LLM‐assisted analysis ( GPTScan ), on a curated test suite of vulnerable and secure contracts. Our results show detection gaps under the evaluated setting: Slither, Mythril, and 4naly3er all scored recall below 40%. SMTChecker and GPTScan were evaluated separately because of their narrower target scopes. SMTChecker detected only arithmetic issues, while GPTScan produced no benchmark‐relevant detections. The study highlights the high average loss associated with smart contract access‐control failures, the need for post‐deployment monitoring beyond one‐time audits, and risks related to Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities. By analyzing exploits and offering mitigations, we provide a structured reference for identifying, prioritizing, and mitigating major blockchain security risks.

candidates.title: Between Journalism and Justice: Disciplinary Humility in Open-Source Investigations
candidates.abstract: Open-source investigations (OSI) have become an increasingly influential method for reporting on conflict, documenting human rights violations, and supporting justice and accountability efforts. As the field has matured, OSI practitioners have increasingly operated across journalistic, legal, human rights, and technical domains, creating innovation and collaboration opportunities, but also disciplinary tensions. Despite growing scholarship on the institutionalization of OSI, less attention has been paid to how practitioners navigate overlapping disciplinary mandates. Drawing on interviews with 35 practitioners involved in OSI across journalism, human rights, law enforcement and specialized investigative organizations, this article examines how disciplinary boundaries are experienced and responded to within justice and accountability contexts. The findings show that practitioners respond to tensions between journalistic and legal norms through forms of boundary recalibration, including recognizing disciplinary limitations and restructuring investigative work. To explain these dynamics, this article introduces disciplinary humility, defined as the recognition of the limits of one’s disciplinary expertise and mandate when operating across overlapping professional jurisdictions. The article contributes to digital journalism scholarship by showing that the OSI institutionalization is shaped not only by hybridity and boundary crossing, but also by boundary recalibration through which practitioners re-examine expertise and mandates across journalistic and legal contexts.

candidates.title: USE OF DATABASE NARRATIVE IN MULTIMIDIA IPs AND VISUAL NOVELS
candidates.abstract: This article aims to present the theoretical concepts and practical effects of the process of creating multimedia Intellectual Property (IP), as a franchise solidified in the market, through the use of database narrative in the creation of a game genre called visual novel. Through an exploratory study on concepts such as otaku subculture, database narrative, visual novel, and multimedia IPs, using the narrative review method, two case studies were structured. The results demonstrated that the capacity of visual novels to generate new successful multimedia IPs requires relatively small investments compared to other media in this cultural field, both in specific niches and throughout the otaku subculture in general, and even surpassing this subculture, with successful Western visual novels already circulating in the market, feeding back into this highly engaged subculture. This confirmed the hypothesis that the use of visual novels in the construction of a multimedia IP is a strategy successfully adopted since the 1990s, allowing cultural product companies to ensure, with little investment, a constant generation of original or adapted content, just as the creation of content by fan communities after the release of a title. Therefore, it can be concluded that this strategy is ideal for experimenting with narrative elements and for launching products on the market with low cost and high reach among the public.
authors: Vitor Pedro da Silva Castelo Tavares

candidates.title: QSLA Application to Agentic AI-Mediated Robots and Robotic Design
candidates.abstract: Robots directed by agentic artificial intelligence can translate natural-language objectives into sequences of perception, planning, tool use and physical action. Their engineering challenge extends beyond generating a feasible plan: a particular action must have valid authority, adequate evidence, an acceptable transition envelope and enforceable execution conditions. This paper proposes a robotics application of Quantum-Safe Ledger Architecture (QSLA), integrating those obligations through a non-compensatory admission rule. The architecture separates an agent that proposes tasks, an independent governance plane that admits bounded skills, a local controller that maintains immediate physical safety, and an evidence service that records decisions and observed consequences. Heuristic Admissibility and Lineage Logic (HALL) evaluates material claims; the Stochastic Control Barrier Function (SCBF) evaluates uncertain transitions; a theta intervention mechanism selects operational responses; capability security binds permissions to specific robot configurations; and resource reservations coordinate concurrent robots. A hybrid model connects discrete task admission to continuous plant dynamics, with explicit inter-sample obligations and a conditional finite-horizon risk bound. Four worked cases cover warehouse navigation, collaborative manipulation, hospital logistics and AI-assisted robotic design. Proposed information models, failure responses, standards-support mappings and an independent evaluation programme make the architecture inspectable. No robot

candidates.title: Traceable World State: A Provenance-Aware State Representation and Deterministic Replay Framework for Robotic Systems
candidates.abstract: Robotic systems operating over extended tasks must maintain a world state assembled from observations arriving at different times, with varying confidence and potential revisions. Conventional representations emphasize latest estimates, hindering fact provenance, decision reproduction, or execution auditing. We present Traceable World State (TWS), a middleware-neutral semantic representation and reference runtime for provenance-aware robot world state. A TWS snapshot captures entities, relations, observations, confidence, and revision metadata. Validated update operations transform snapshots immutably, ordered updates support deterministic replay, and a canonical SHA-256 hash chain ensures tamper-evident logs. We evaluate TWS through schema conformance, complete state lifecycles, deterministic replay, and fault injection. Passing 38 tests across Python 3.10-3.14, the framework detects record corruptions, broken hash links, sequence discontinuities, and world mismatches. Across ten public BEHAVIOR-1K task definitions, TWS imported 153 entities and 146 relations with successful validation. On 103 NVIDIA Unitree G1 simulated trajectories containing 78,369 frames, TWS achieved exact terminal-state replay in all episodes and detected 412/412 injected corruptions with a 1.72% storage overhead over Plain JSONL.

candidates.title: AI Companions and Loneliness: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing Synthetic Mindfulness and Exploring Its Role in Alleviating Loneliness
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The rise of AI companions has sparked interest in their potential to alleviate the growing social problem of loneliness, yet evidence of their effectiveness remains unsettled. Drawing on social surrogacy theory with a theories‐in‐use approach, this research introduces synthetic mindfulness, defined as consumers' judgment of an AI companion's capacity to maintain an attentive presence, engage in a non‐judgmental way, and respond with sensitive attunement to their needs. We argue that these judgments shape whether consumers experience AI companions as capable of reducing their loneliness. Across one qualitative and four quantitative studies, we develop and validate a three‐dimensional measure of synthetic mindfulness. Our final study demonstrates that higher judgments of synthetic mindfulness reduce loneliness via consumers' strengthened sense of belonging and self‐esteem. This research advances understanding of how AI companions can effectively address loneliness and provides a conceptual foundation for examining synthetic mindfulness in human–AI relationships.

candidates.title: AutoIndexer: Flexible-Order Decoding by Training Causal Models on Chains of Edits
candidates.abstract: Autoregressive decoding is less suited to non-causally ordered data, e.g., cross-references or future dependencies, since their outputs cannot be revised post hoc, unlike iterative human reasoning. Diffusion LLMs partially mitigate this limitation but still cannot flexibly insert or remove arbitrary numbers of tokens from a pre-generated context. We design AutoIndexer as a generative model with a novel training and decoding mechanism that simulates a Chain of Edits, allowing the model to flexibly modify its prior outputs in hindsight via token insertions, substitutions, and deletions. The model learns to predict marker tokens for opening and closing edits, simultaneously moving a cursor to positions in the existing token sequence, analogous to a text editor. Training sequences are obtained by perturbing ground-truth labels with inverse chained edit operations, and the model learns to edit by undoing those inverses. The perturbation training allows AutoIndexer to be robust to erroneous context and adaptable to editing tasks such as code correction. We demonstrate that our method exhibits post-generation context-editing capabilities that most autoregressive and diffusion models lack without compromising performance on standard LLM benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/AutodeskAILab/autoindexer.

candidates.title: Rethinking Diagnostic Assessment Through Culturally Embedded AI for Meaningful Learning
candidates.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence have accelerated the transformation of educational assessment, but most innovations remain focused on automating scoring rather than generating meaningful evidence of learning. This study aims to develop and validate the Meaningful Diagnostic Assessment Framework (MDAF), which integrates culturally contextualised diagnostic tasks, AI-based analysis, and pedagogical interpretation to generate meaningful evidence of learning in mathematics education. The study employed a controlled quasi-experimental design involving 178 junior high school students in Indonesia. Data were analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), mediation analysis, and tests of agreement between AI-generated diagnoses and expert assessments. The results indicate positive associations between the MDAF and symbolic mathematical performance and student engagement. Cultural Embeddedness Perception partially mediated these relationships, while AI-generated diagnoses showed high agreement with expert assessments. These findings suggest that AI's primary value in assessment lies not in automatically generating scores, but in transforming student responses into meaningful evidence of learning that supports pedagogical decision-making. This study offers a new paradigm for diagnostic assessment by shifting the focus from “assessment as measurement” to “assessment as the generation of meaningful learning evidence,” thereby providing a conceptual foundation for developing digital assessments that are more adaptive, transparent, and oriented toward the learning process.

candidates.title: Spa-Bench: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Spatial Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) offer a promising route toward general-purpose robotics by transferring semantic knowledge from large-scale vision-language pretraining into language-conditioned control. However, most VLA evaluations emphasize aggregate manipulation success under changes in objects, instructions, or environments, leaving unclear how reliably these policies ground spatial descriptions in the physical scenes where they act. We therefore ask a sharper question: how reliably can current VLAs translate spatial descriptions into appropriate real-robot behavior? To investigate this, we introduce Spa-Bench, a real-robot benchmark that evaluates spatial grounding across six tabletop tasks covering Object State, Relative Size, Referential Description, Relational Placement, Ordinal Position, and Counting. Our primary evaluation compares in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) spatial configurations while retaining training support for the relevant objects, concepts, and actions, reducing object and motor unfamiliarity as alternative explanations for failure. Four diagnostic conditions further probe physical execution, sensitivity to wording, object-task associations, and recognition that no action is required. We release 4,092 episodes collected on the SO-101 robot arm: 1,200 human-teleoperated demonstrations and 2,892 real-robot evaluation rollouts from five state-of-the-art VLA policies. Across the three fully evaluated policies, success falls from 67.5-73.3% on ID spatial configurations to 40.7-52.0% on OOD spatial configurations, while matched direct instructions improve success by 28.3-40.0 percentage points. These results show that the evaluated VLAs can often execute the required manipulations but lack robust spatial grounding. Project materials, including videos, code, and benchmark data, are available at https://justintiensmith.github.io/Spa-Bench/.

candidates.title: Ritual Paraphernalia Toward a Modular Approach to Coptic Magic
candidates.abstract: This article explores the redactional strategies through which ritual experts in late antique and early medieval Egypt articulated their textual products. It adopts what is here heuristically termed a ‘modular approach’, which treats magical texts as assemblages of discrete textual segments that could be extracted, recombined, and adapted to different redactional agendas. Drawing on selected case studies from Coptic ritual manuscripts, the article offers a new model for understanding scribal practice and the transmission of ritual knowledge.

candidates.title: Characterizing the Landscape of Open-Source Satellite Software
candidates.abstract: Satellites have become fundamental components of modern technological systems, supporting critical infrastructure in communication, navigation, Earth observation, and scientific research. As space exploration advances and demand for satellite-enabled services grows, reliance on complex, heterogeneous satellite software continues to increase. A systematic understanding of the satellite software landscape is therefore increasingly important, yet existing studies still lack a comprehensive empirical examination. To address this gap, we present the first characterization study of open-source satellite software, examining its ecosystem and development practices. We mine and analyze 22,286 satellite-related GitHub projects through three research questions on popularity trends (RQ1), software goals (RQ2), and development practices (RQ3). First, we characterize the temporal evolution of projects and active developers, revealing increasing popularity. Second, through manual inspection of 646 projects, we construct a taxonomy of 43 software-goal categories spanning conceptual design, datasets, system implementation, simulation, testing, and tools. Third, we conduct an in-depth analysis of projects with source code, revealing a highly heterogeneous and task-specialized ecosystem with 66 programming languages and diverse implementation strategies. Finally, we summarize key findings and derive actionable implications for satellite developers and researchers.

candidates.title: Smartphone Communities
candidates.abstract: Smartphone Communities places the smartphone - our most personal and ubiquitous medium - at the centre of an in-depth exploration of contemporary community formation. The book ground-breaking contribution lies in theorizing the smartphone not merely as a device, but as a dynamic social infrastructure through which communities are continuously assembled, negotiated, and contested. Conceptualizing the smartphone user as a mobile, permanently networked subject, the book advances a multi-directional media-theoretical framework that bridges participation theory, fan studies, and visual culture. Focusing primarily on Western, platform-capitalist contexts from the 2010s to the mid-2020s, Anne Ganzert analyzes topical and widely recognizable case studies, including TikTok, Pokémon Go, Tinder, and Habitica. These platforms serve as lenses through which social, economic, and political power relations become visible, from algorithmic governance and data extraction to practices of play, intimacy, self-optimization, and resistance. Readers will gain a comprehensive understanding of smartphone-based communities through a blend of media theory and empirical analysis. Addressed to undergraduates, postgraduates, scholars of media and cultural studies, as well as non-specialist readers such as librarians and booksellers, the book offers an accessible yet theoretically ambitious account of smartphone-based communities.

candidates.title: HuMBLE: Human Motion-Driven Behavior Learning for Embodied Locomotion
candidates.abstract: Despite recent advances in humanoid locomotion, controllers optimized for command tracking and robustness tend to produce mechanical gaits, whereas controllers tied to human motion data often fail to generalize to commands outside the data distribution. This work introduces a learning framework that balances these competing objectives to synthesize real-time steerable, robust, and biomimetic locomotion policies from human data. Using an in-house curated locomotion dataset covering diverse speeds and directions, we first learn a natural locomotion prior policy through a teacher-student distillation process. Specifically, we train a full-body reference-conditioned policy with Reinforcement Learning (RL), then distill it into a lightweight prior policy conditioned solely on proprioception and a planar torso-velocity steering command. Next, we fine-tune the prior policy with multi-task RL to expand command coverage and robustness beyond the data distribution, pairing a goal-conditioned task that tracks arbitrary commands with a reference-guided task that tracks the human data as an explicit style regularizer. We validate our framework on three humanoid robots: the Boston Dynamics Atlas R1, Atlas D1, and Unitree G1. Experimental results demonstrate robust performance across real-world scenarios, including direct user-controlled locomotion in indoor and outdoor environments, and integration as the locomotion layer within hierarchical control stacks. Benchmarks against Tabula Rasa RL policies trained without human data and ablation studies confirm that our framework yields a lightweight, deployable policy that reconstructs coordinated whole-body behavior from a steering command, retaining the human gait characteristics while remaining robust and fully steerable.

candidates.title: Intelligent Mechatronics: intelligence in the design process, not only the machine
candidates.abstract: Designing a physical machine requires mechanical, electronic, control, and software decisions to be settled together, each constraining the others, under the standards governing the environment it will work in. This reasoning is held by experienced engineers and rarely written down. That, I argue, is why artificial intelligence has reached the design of software but not of the machines that software runs on. Physical design is, in part, genuinely harder, and its errors are costly and irreversible, but that is not the whole explanation. Software’s design reasoning was written down alongside the public code that an AI could learn from; the knowledge that conceives and sizes a physical system was not. As the design bottleneck shifts to physical systems, intelligence must be applied to the design process itself, not only to the product. Taking mechatronics as the case, I find that where its defining sources invoke intelligence at all, it is for the product or the discipline that builds it, never for the process that designs it. The capture of tacit, cross-domain design knowledge in a form that AI can use is a binding constraint on AI-assisted physical design, and the most neglected as well. A three-layer model locates it: Layer 1, this design knowledge is the missing foundation; the AI reasoning and agent layers above advance rapidly but cannot design physical systems without it. The physical machine and its intelligent twin are developed together from this foundation. A worked design-rationale analysis of an offshore-crane actuation decision grounds what Layer 1 must hold: the rationale residue that existing formats do not capture. In this article, I set out a research agenda, from capturing this knowledge to generalizing beyond mechatronics, and state the conditions under which its central claim would fail.

candidates.title: Skill-SLM: Agent Skill-driven Small Language Models for Reliable Robot Operation
candidates.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) have been increasingly adopted for onboard robot operation because they enable intelligent decision-making. However, existing approaches are mainly distillation-oriented and rely on enumerating representative task-solution pairs. This makes dataset construction difficult and limits generalization to diverse robot tasks whose possible forms grow rapidly. This paper proposes Skill-SLM, a framework that reformulates SLM-driven robot operation as a task-decomposition and skill-composition problem. Given a natural language task instruction, Skill-SLM decomposes the task into subtasks, selects appropriate skills from the skill library, and orchestrates the selected skills into executable robot operations. First, to support the skill-driven workflow, we propose a novel robot operational skill aware context-free grammar (CFG) to extract the skills required to accomplish tasks and build the skill library accordingly. Then, we configure LLM teachers to induce and synthesize training datasets for the SLMs, enabling SLMs to decompose tasks and orchestrate skills reliably. Additionally, we employ a progressive skill orchestration strategy to improve the reliability of skill implementation and overall robot operation. Experiments on UAV operation tasks indicate that Skill-SLM substantially outperforms distillation-oriented baselines, especially on unseen tasks that require generalization of capabilities. Additional experiments on ground vehicle tasks further demonstrate that Skill-SLM can be applied to different robot platforms.

candidates.title: Cross-Validation of Open-Source Quantum Network Simulators
candidates.abstract: We present a comparative analysis of two open-source quantum network simulators, QuISP and SeQUeNCe, focusing on cross-validation of basic networking tasks to ensure consistency and accuracy in simulation outputs. Although both simulators are designed to study quantum network management policies and their dynamics under complex noise models, their differing underlying assumptions can lead to variations in simulation results. We highlight the discrepancies in how the two simulators handle connections, internal network node processing time, and classical communication, resulting in significant quantitative and qualitative differences in the time required to perform basic network tasks such as entanglement generation, purification, and swapping. We simulate common scenarios between the simulators to compare both the latency of resource distribution and the fidelity of the distributed resources. Our findings indicate that while the simulators differ in the time required to complete network tasks---a constant factor difference attributable to their respective connection models---they agree on the fidelity of the distributed resources under identical error parameters. This work demonstrates a crucial first step towards enhancing the reliability and reproducibility of quantum network simulations, as well as leading to full protocol development. Furthermore, our benchmarking methodology establishes a foundational set of tasks for the cross-validation of simulators to study future quantum networks.

candidates.title: Quantitative ethnobotanical study of medicinal plants used by Mullu Kuruma community of Wayanad, the Southern Western Ghats, India
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: The traditional ethnomedicinal knowledge of the Mullu Kurama tribes, one of the oldest tribal communities in Wayanad, India, holds considerable significance. Indigenous communities in the Western Ghats have developed extensive ethnomedicinal knowledge through sustained interactions with local biodiversity. However, socioeconomic changes, reduced intergenerational knowledge transmission, and conservation challenges increasingly threaten their traditional knowledge (TK) of medicinal plants. This study aims to validate the ethnomedicinal plants used by these communities and assess their medicinal applications through quantitative analysis. METHODS: Ethnobotanical data were collected through field visits, direct observation, semi-structured interviews, group discussions, and a standardized questionnaire administered to traditional healers and community members. RESULTS: A total of 130 medicinal plant species, representing 121 genera and 55 families, were identified. Fabaceae was the most represented family, followed by Asteraceae and Lamiaceae. Herbs constituted the predominant growth form, and leaves were the most frequently used plant parts. Centella asiatica exhibited the highest use value (UV) of 1.84 and a relative frequency of citation (RFC) of 0.085, followed by Asparagus racemosus, Mangifera indica, and Plectranthus amboinicus. Informant consensus factor (ICF) values ranged from 0.72 to 0.94, with the highest consensus observed for hair care and dermatological disorders. Sixty-seven species demonstrated a 100% fidelity level (FL), indicating strong therapeutic specificity. Family importance value (FIV) ranged from 0.046 to 10.64, with Asteraceae attaining the highest value. Cross-cultural analysis revealed low Jaccard similarity index (JSI) values, ranging from 7.89% to 17.83%, in comparison with other Wayanad tribes. CONCLUSION: The findings highlight the richness, specificity, and cultural distinctiveness of Mullu Kuruma ethnomedicinal knowledge. Medicinal plants identified as culturally significant through quantitative indices are promising candidates for future phytochemical and pharmacological investigations. Responsible harvesting, conservation, and intergenerational transmission of indigenous knowledge are essential to maintain medicinal plant diversity and traditional health care practices.

candidates.title: We Query, Therefore We Compute: On Oracle Computation beyond the Machine, with an Application to Agents
candidates.abstract: Agentic systems use large language models (LLMs) to carry out concrete tasks. Prior work often borrows abstractions such as scheduling, caching or isolation piecemeal from operating systems, so the mechanisms it builds share little common ground, and the shared view of the two forms of agentic system, Workflows and Agents, is limited. We construct an abstract machine that provides both. We treat the LLM as an Oracle and extend a two-stack pushdown automaton with one instruction, which hands the Oracle a whole stack as its query and appends the answer to that same stack. The machine thus performs two computations, the Oracle's and a Turing-complete one that we call the Priestess. A stack that the program only appends to grows autoregressively, as an agent's context does. Two symmetry breakings, S in storage and T in transitions, make a Priestess program the operating system of the programs the Oracle runs, and produce the Agent and the Workflow as the two placements of a task's program. For internally autoregressive Oracles, the two computations synchronize at the end of every answer under certain conditions, and through that synchronization we model caching and analyse scheduling. No guarantee that holds for every Oracle can fix which content crosses between the two computations, but such a guarantee does fix the boundary itself. The construction V fits the machine to a von Neumann computer. To show that it is realizable, we propose ArchNights, an extended RISC-V ISA and a Linux-style operating system implementing the machine by design. ArchNights-SE runs on gem5 as a computer system, becomes an agentic system when it runs an LLM as the Oracle, and will be open source. Agentic systems can then be designed as computer systems are. With a foundation built and a unified view, future work can share invariants and bounds, each with its conditions.

candidates.title: Beyond LLMs: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Commonsense Reasoning in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Domestic robots often receive instructions that are underspecified regarding everyday actions. Large language models can interpret varied language and draw on everyday knowledge, but their reasoning is not explicitly inspectable. Symbolic systems provide transparent knowledge representation and inference, but depend on potentially incomplete rules. This thesis investigates whether combining these approaches can preserve or improve LLM performance on embodied commonsense tasks while making decisions more interpretable. Two complementary neuro-symbolic pipelines are evaluated on RoboCSKBench, a benchmark covering five embodied commonsense tasks. Pipeline 1 investigates the partially automated construction of Answer Set Programming rules for the Tidy Up and Tool Usage tasks, combining commonsense graphs, SOMA-inspired annotations, LLM-generated rule proposals, and Clingo verification. Pipeline 2 covers all five tasks: an LLM extracts controlled facts at runtime, while SWI-Prolog performs reasoning using knowledge-base evidence or hand-crafted rules. Pure-LLM and pure-logic ablations are evaluated using three Mistral model sizes, and Pipeline 2 is transferred without modification to five out-of-distribution datasets. Results show that symbolic reasoning is beneficial only under specific conditions. It is most effective when symbolic components can retrieve relevant affordance or capability knowledge and apply constraints aligned with the task’s answer format. In such cases, explicit grounding can reduce the performance gap between larger and smaller language models. Conversely, for open-ended generation or tasks whose expected decision structure is not supported by the symbolic selector, the architecture may become redundant or harmful. Overall, the findings support a conditional view of neuro-symbolic reasoning: it can improve decision traceability without necessarily sacrificing performance, provided that representation, knowledge, and inference are properly aligned.

candidates.title: Proactive Robot Assistance via Event-Driven Reasoning over State Changes
candidates.abstract: Assistance in collaborative manipulation is often initiated by user instructions, making high-level reasoning request-driven. In fluent human teamwork, however, partners often infer the next helpful step from the observed outcome of an action rather than waiting for instructions. Motivated by this, we investigate an event-driven formulation of proactive assistance, where human--object interaction outcomes initiate assistive reasoning without user-provided task specifications at inference time. To this end, we propose an event-driven framework that monitors workspace state changes with an event monitor and, upon event completion, extracts stabilized pre/post snapshots that characterize the resulting state transition. A frozen pretrained Vision-Language Model (VLM) then uses its semantic priors to infer the task context, decide whether assistance is appropriate, and, when needed, generate a sequence of assistive actions from the observed transition. To make outputs executable and verifiable, we restrict actions to a set of action primitives and reference objects via integer IDs. We evaluate the same framework across three distinct real world tabletop collaboration tasks without task-specific training or fine-tuning. The event-driven framework achieves performance comparable to variants given user instructions.

candidates.title: Rethinking Service Recovery and Customer Experience in the Age of AI: A Multi-Perspective Review
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is gradually integrating into service systems and beginning to play an important role in service recovery following service failures. As AI systems take over tasks originally performed by frontline employees, the design and evaluation methods of AI-enabled service recovery, as well as its positioning in the overall service scenario, have become urgent issues to explore. This chapter provides a comprehensive and structured review of existing research on AI-led service recovery, clarifies its theoretical foundations, and integrates scattered research findings from various disciplines. Based on an analytical framework, the chapter organizes prior studies from three complementary perspectives: technology, customer perception, and service context. The technical perspective highlights how AI appearance, expressive styles, and functional boundaries shape recovery interactions; the customer perception perspective summarizes attributional, perceptual–affective, and relational mechanisms through which customers evaluate AI-led recovery; the service perspective analyzes how service processes, contextual contingencies, and relationship norms condition the effectiveness and legitimacy of AI-enabled recovery. By mapping dominant research streams and key constructs, this chapter advances a holistic understanding of AI-driven service recovery and identifies directions for future research. This chapter defines AI service recovery as a dynamic service model jointly influenced by technical design, customer cognitive interpretation, and service system characteristics, enriching relevant research in the service field.

candidates.title: OntoPlan: An Ontology-Grounded Scene Representation and Agentic Framework for Scalable Robot Task Planning
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based robot task planning is promising for open-ended instruction following, but degrades on long-horizon tasks in large environments. When spatial information is conveyed to the LLM through text, the model can fail to capture spatial context, and token cost grows with environment size. Generating action sequences directly with an LLM also makes it difficult to satisfy the current world state and action preconditions. We address this with an ontology-grounded scene representation that aligns objects, spaces, relations, and states in a shared symbolic vocabulary for spatial reasoning and task planning, and with OntoPlan, an agentic framework that interprets instructions, selectively retrieves task-relevant information, formalizes goals and constraints, and produces executable plans. Across 150 general tasks spanning five indoor environments and three scene scales, OntoPlan achieves 0.89 average task success, compared with 0.27 for the strongest baseline, while using 18.1k total tokens per task on average, about 5.6$\times$ fewer than the most efficient baseline. These advantages persist as scene scale increases, whereas prior methods degrade more sharply in success and remain far more costly in tokens. OntoPlan also responds appropriately to ambiguous or infeasible instructions by asking follow-up questions or reporting insufficient information rather than committing to invalid plans. Code available at https://github.com/namhyeongwoo/OntoPlan.

candidates.title: Beyond boundaries: a transdisciplinary review of ethical, philosophical and social dimensions of biohybrid robotics
candidates.abstract: The domain of biohybrid robotics attracts significant attention from the scientific community due to its novel approach to combining living and non-living materials and technical capabilities. Notably, the field intrigues not only natural scientists but also social scientists, ethicists, and philosophers, given its distinctive nature and the socio-technical questions it poses, which transcend disciplinary boundaries. This paper reviews the social, ethical, and philosophical dimensions of biohybrid robotics, focusing on recent literature that extends beyond scientific and technical aspects, and presents illustrative cases where the research integrates societal perspectives into its design. The review reveals that, while there are papers addressing ethical debates and various philosophical approaches to understanding living material-integrated robots, there is limited social scientific literature on biohybrid robotics. Importantly, empirical social studies on biohybrid robotics and their communities are lacking. The paper also aims to introduce Science and Technology Studies (STS) insights to better situate biohybrid robotics’ potential to shape, and be shaped by, society and its values. By working together and integrating societal values, the biohybrid robotics domain can develop a distinctive path that enriches its foundational growth, enhancing self-understanding through diverse social science perspectives and fostering internal growth.

candidates.title: TECHNIQUES IN REAL-TIME BIG DATA ANALYTICS: AN APPRAISAL OF ADVANTAGES, LIMITATIONS, AND APPLICATIONS
candidates.abstract: The rapid growth of connected devices, social media, and digital services has produced unprecedented data volumes, driving a shift from batch processing to real-time analytics (RTA). RTA emphasizes velocity, enabling data to be ingested, processed, and analyzed as it arrives to deliver immediate insights and business value. This article reviews major RTA techniques, including stream processing (SP), complex event processing (CEP), query- and rule-based analytics, programmatic platforms, anytime algorithms, and hybrid edge–cloud architectures. The paper assesses stream processing frameworks such as Apache Flink, Kafka, and Storm for scalability, fault tolerance, and latency, with Flink consistently achieving sub-100-millisecond performance for complex tasks. CEP is highlighted for detecting event patterns and correlations, supporting applications in fraud detection, predictive maintenance, and smart environments. Anytime algorithms are examined for their ability to provide progressively refined results, enabling rapid decision-making in time-sensitive contexts. The integration of machine learning into streaming pipelines, edge deployment strategies guided by the latency–bandwidth–compute triangle, and emerging hybrid architectures are also discussed. Three developmental trends are identified: evolution from batch to stream-native systems, convergence of batch and stream paradigms, and fusion of machine learning with RTA. Findings underscore the need to balance latency, cost, and complexity when selecting techniques for specific use cases.

candidates.title: Towards Efficient Robotic Manipulation Models with Self-Recursive Pruning
candidates.abstract: Network pruning can reduce parameter redundancy in robotic policies. However, generic pruning criteria are tailored for image recognition tasks and commonly designed to preserve weight magnitude, local reconstruction, or language-model likelihood rather than closed-loop action behavior. Directly applying these pruning algorithms to robotic tasks yields unsatisfactory performance. In this paper, we propose Loss-Conditioned Activation-Moment (LCAM) pruning, a training-free method for unstructured pruning of pre-trained robotic manipulation policies. Specifically, we first rank connections using row-normalized weight contribution, activation moments measured on calibration demonstrations, and the sensitivity of output directions to the action-prediction loss. We further design a self-recursive coarse-to-fine procedure: importance is recalibrated after each nested coarse pruning stage, while held-out offline action distortion guides fine-grained budget allocation after a sparsity knee. Our algorithm is free from costly recovery training and simulator rollouts after pruning. Experiments on three LIBERO suites with competitive robotic policies, together with evaluations on OpenVLA, show that LCAM attains competitive performance across a broad range of pruning ratios. Notably, on LIBERO-Object with OpenVLA, our LCAM achieves 84.0% success at 50% unstructured pruning, retaining over 90% of the dense policy's success rate. Promising results on real-world robotic ping pong further demonstrate the effectiveness of our pruning algorithm.

candidates.title: Toward Mechanical Intelligence in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Conventional robotic systems concentrate sensing, control, and actuation in electronic hardware, creating constraints in harsh environments, energy efficiency, and miniaturization. The physical body of a robot is more than a passive executor of control commands; it is an active substrate that transforms inputs into functional operations through its intrinsic mechanical dynamics. This perspective describes this capability as mechanical intelligence and identifies three core operations: filtering, routing, and switching. These operations address three fundamental questions in physically mediated transformation: what inputs are selectively admitted, where signals propagate, and when the system transitions between states. Together, they enable selective responsiveness, spatial coordination, and state‐dependent behavior without dedicated electronic hardware. Design variables and quantitative metrics are proposed for each operation, and the framework is illustrated in locomotion and manipulation, providing guidance for designing mechanically intelligent robots. Responsive materials extend this framework by transducing environmental stimuli into mechanical signals while also harvesting ambient energy for actuation. Rather than replacing digital computation, mechanical intelligence complements it by embedding part of sensing, processing, and actuation into the physical body, pointing toward hybrid systems in which mechanical and digital intelligence work together.

candidates.title: Magnet-Aware Control of Legged Robots
candidates.abstract: Autonomous robots can increase uptime and reduce human exposure in Big Science facilities, but strong magnetic fields needed for their operation corrupt sensors and induce pose-dependent mechanical wrenches that destabilize robots and challenge conventional reactive controllers. This paper presents a control framework for modeling, estimating, and dynamically compensating for spatially varying magnetic wrenches acting on legged robots to improve robustness in these fields. We introduce a custom physics plugin for the MuJoCo simulator to model magnetic forces on rigid-body elements, alongside an inverse field-estimation framework to infer the latent magnetic field directly from quadruped dynamic responses and any number of sensor readings. Furthermore, we develop a Magnet-Aware Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Whole-Body Control (WBC) architecture that predicts and counteracts magnetic perturbations during locomotion to increase the range of magnetic fields in which the robot can operate. The effectiveness of the framework is validated through both simulation and physical hardware experiments. We show our method increases the the maximum rejectable disturbances from magnetic field in the force space by a factor of 2.5 and and between 1.6-2 times in torque space compared to a non-compensated system. Within the proposed magnetic field, this constitutes an increase in the area in which the robot can operate by 29,34% of which 10,84% would have previously caused an immediate collapse to non-compensated controllers.

candidates.title: Cross-Layer Network Security in the Post-Quantum Era:From Integrated Quantum Sources to Datacenter-Scale Cryptography
candidates.abstract: The security of digital communication rests on mathematical problems that are easy to pose but, for classical computers, practically impossible to solve. The prospect of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) undermines this foundation: once such a machine exists, the public-key cryptography that protects nearly all modern infrastructure can be broken. Although the precise arrival of "Q-Day" is uncertain, the threat is already operational through "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) attacks, in which adversaries store encrypted traffic today to decrypt it once the hardware matures. Mitigating this threat is not a single algorithm-selection problem but a tiered, heterogeneous re-engineering of communication systems. This shift is driven by fundamental trade-offs between security guarantees, deployment complexity, and performance: computationally secure post-quantum cryptography (PQC) scales to protect high-volume datacenter traffic but relies on mathematical assumptions, whereas quantum key distribution (QKD) offers information-theoretic, physics-based security at the cost of specialized optical hardware and dedicated infrastructure. A comprehensive defence must therefore integrate both paradigms. The central premise of this dissertation is that scaling quantum-resilient communication is an integration challenge governed by boundaries among the device, protocol, and infrastructure layers. A cryptographic primitive that is secure in isolation may still be impractical if it cannot meet the latency, throughput, determinism, power, or observability constraints of the network in which it runs; likewise, a quantum primitive becomes operational infrastructure only when its photonic devices, post-processing pipeline, and classical integration points are engineered together. The work was carried out within the Quantum Resistant Communications: Advance Learning in Applied PQC Training (QUARC) doctoral network as an industrial doctorate embedded with NVIDIA's networking organization. The dissertation comprises peer-reviewed publications, manuscripts under review, and patent applications grouped into three parts. Part I treats QKD as a deployable network capability: it presents the design and characterization of integrated photonic entanglement sources for wavelength-division-multiplexed QKD, and the offload of QKD post-processing onto data processing units (DPUs). Part II investigates how PQC algorithms can be executed efficiently on heterogeneous CPU--GPU--DPU platforms and applied to secure end-to-end real-time pipelines. Part III examines datacenter-scale security, addressing the ordering- and timing-related risks of RDMA over high-throughput optical fabrics and cross-layer observability and intrusion detection for confidential artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Taken together, these contributions show that device-level, protocol-level, and infrastructure-level design choices are tightly coupled: decisions made at one layer constrain or enable the others. The synthesis argues that quantum-resilient communication is achievable with today's and near-future technology, but only by actively engineering the integration points where cryptography, photonics, and programmable network hardware meet, rather than treating them as independent disciplines.

candidates.title: Transmedia Storytelling
candidates.abstract: Transmedia Storytelling examines how successful stories move between platforms, from traditional media to digital formats, and diagnoses how platform capitalism has transformed transmedia storytelling from a democratic expansion of storyworlds into a machinery of extraction. Drawing on the author’s dual expertise as both producer and academic, this book analyses how storytellers create worlds that work successfully across multiple formats through an abundance of case studies. These case studies span from Marvel and Stranger Things to diverse global storytelling ecologies, including Japanese manga serialisation, Korean platform co-productions, and Nollywood video-film networks. Readers will discover practical tools for developing cross-platform stories, methods for creating effective story bibles and world-building, techniques for adapting characters across different media, and approaches to inclusive storytelling that acknowledge coherence as labour. The book also confronts emerging challenges, including algorithmic personalisation that fragments audiences into parallel monocultures, IP financialisation that transforms franchises into liquid assets, and generative AI that automates the appearance of coherence while degrading narrative causality. This book provides essential reading for undergraduate and postgraduate students undertaking digital storytelling, narrative theory, and film and media production, as well as media studies classes. It also functions as a hands-on toolkit for industry professionals already working within film, gaming, and content creation.

candidates.title: Systemization of Knowledge (SoK): Human-Centered AI Safety for Youth
candidates.abstract: While HCI increasingly examines AI-safety for youth, the literature lacks a comprehensive view of what risks have been identified, how they are addressed, and whether proposed protections work in-practice. We systematically reviewed 100 empirical HCI studies involving children and youth interacting with or exposed to AI across schools, homes, care settings, and public services. Using the YAIR taxonomy for risks and the MIT Mitigation Taxonomy for countermeasures, we map which risks have been identified, whether each risk is addressed by countermeasure(s), and whether each countermeasure for that risk is implemented and even evaluated. The risk-countermeasure mapping shows that most risks are matched only with proposed/ideated countermeasures; few countermeasures have been implemented, and fewer still evaluated; and existing evaluations often measure technical performance rather than protection from harm. We identify where coverage is absent, where safeguards remain untested, and propose concrete directions for HCI research to strengthen youth AI-safety.

candidates.title: Exploring dimensions and metrics of cyber-to-physical impact: A systematic review
candidates.abstract: Modern Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks capable of causing potentially catastrophic cyber-to-physical (C2P) impacts. However, the absence of unified guidance on impact characterization and measurement forces analysts to rely on ad-hoc analytical choices or inefficient post-simulation observations. To address this gap, this work presents a systematic analysis of 53 model-based studies, integrating grounded theory and systematic literature review (SLR) methodologies. We propose the PERSEOS model, which defines seven interconnected C2P impact dimensions: Physical, Economic, Reputational, Safety, Environmental, Operational, and Societal. Additionally, we establish an extensive categorization of impact metrics based on four salient themes: generalizability, scope, tooling requirements, and measured attributes, delineating their specific characteristics, utility, and trade-offs. Validated against historical incidents and demonstrated via two water and wastewater case studies, this framework enables the preemptive selection of analysis objectives and informs key decision points during analysis. Overall, our work provides a clear and shared vocabulary and the theoretical foundations required to transition from ad-hoc monitoring to more structured, objective, and informed C2P impact analyses.

candidates.title: How Could AI Eliminate Humanity? A Failure-Mode Analysis of Civilizational Risk
candidates.abstract: This article develops a failure-mode framework for analyzing how advanced artificial intelligence could contribute to human extinction, irreversible civilizational collapse, or permanent human disempowerment. The central thesis is that catastrophic AI risk does not require consciousness, hostility, or an explicit intention to harm humanity. Instead, risk may arise through several distinct but interacting pathways, including autonomous misalignment, harmful human use, organizational failure, and competitive deployment. The severity of these pathways depends on factors such as capability, autonomy, external access, persistence, institutional safeguards, and the preservation of recovery capacity. The analysis is deliberately non-operational: it identifies causal conditions, empirically tractable intermediate quantities, and defensive research questions rather than procedures for causing harm.

candidates.title: Aye robot! When should(n’t) service providers say yes to humanoid robot frontline employees?
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robot technology is transforming the servicescape. We investigate when it is (versus is not) prudent for service providers to employ humanoid robot frontline employees and offer strategic guidelines for marketers. Across two studies, we find that humanoid robot (versus human) frontline employees elicit lower (higher) levels of perceived warmth (creepiness) amongst customers, ultimately resulting in diminished customer comfort, lower service expectations and subsequent negative behavioral intentions. Additionally, we identify embarrassment associated with the service context as an important boundary condition. Further, we find that perceived creepiness of human (but not humanoid robot) frontline employees is contingent on service context.

candidates.title: From visual detection to traceable progress evidence: A schedule-driven ontology framework for construction monitoring
candidates.abstract: Construction progress monitoring is increasingly combining Computer Vision (CV) and semantic technologies, yet schedules, site photographs, and monitoring outputs often remain disconnected. This limits the interpretability, traceability and reuse of progress-verification results in construction reporting. This research proposes a schedule-driven pipeline that links project planning data and construction-site visual evidence through open-vocabulary object detection, RDF-based Knowledge Graphs, SPARQL queries and controlled LLM-based verbalisation. The project schedule is used to derive and optimise the labels queried by GroundingDINO, while the resulting detections, photographic metadata and schedule information are integrated into a Knowledge Graph to assign progress-related semantic statuses. The LLaMA 3.1 8B model then reformulates the structured SPARQL output into concise technical statements without altering the rule-based classification. The pipeline is tested on the installation of a 100-metre free-standing tower crane at a hotel construction site in Milan. The results show that schedule-driven CV, semantic modelling, and controlled natural-language generation can support transparent, traceable, and semi-automatic documentation of construction progress. The workflow also contributes to SDG 9, SDG 11, and SDG 12 by supporting digital innovation, sustainable construction management, and traceable, resource-aware decision-making.
