candidates.title: LocAttMamba: A Low-Complexity Mamba Framework with Attention-Based Multi-AP Fusion for Indoor Localization
candidates.abstract: Accurate and low-complexity indoor localization is important for location-based services in fifth generation (5G) and sixth generation (6G) networks, where positioning devices operate under limited computational budgets and non conditions. Indoor localization has been studied widely using traditional signal-level localization approaches. However, these techniques often show degraded performance in on-line-of-sight (NLoS) scenarios. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-based techniques, including transformers, have been applied to address these challenges. While transformer-based architectures can capture the dependencies within the measurements collected from distributed access points (APs), their high computational complexity results in a large number of multiply-accumulate operations and long inference time. In contrast, lightweight recurrent and convolutional models trade this cost for degraded accuracy. In this paper, we propose LocAttMamba, a low-complexity localization framework in which the channel impulse response (CIR) and time-based features of each AP are processed by a separate Mamba encoder with near-linear complexity, and the resulting per-AP embeddings are fused through a multi-head attention layer that weights each AP according to its importance at every time step. The framework jointly predicts the user location and its per-axis uncertainty, which is refined through a post-hoc calibration step. We evaluate the proposed framework using two real-world 5G and ultra-wideband (UWB) measurement datasets. Our numerical results reveal that LocAttMamba obtains a mean two-dimensional (2-D) positioning error of 1.004 m and 0.599 m, respectively, on 5G and UWB datasets, outperforming the second-best benchmark by 9.79% and 5.82%, while requiring the fewest multiply-accumulate operations among all evaluated models and being 4.4-16 times faster than the transformer-based benchmarks.

candidates.title: The future of surgery
candidates.abstract: Abstract Surgery is entering a period of accelerated transformation driven by artificial intelligence, robotics, and emerging postmodern medical technologies. Unlike prior technological shifts, innovation cycles are compressing into years, challenging established models of evidence generation, regulation, training, and professional identity. This Perspective examines plausible trajectories for digital surgery, emphasizing ethical, educational, and institutional adaptation under conditions of continuous technological acceleration rather than offering definitive predictions.

candidates.title: Organizing Intangible Cultural Heritage: How a Community-Based Organization Sustains Paper-Cutting Transmission in an Urban Community
Migration as Method, Death as Border: Necropolitics and Speculative Cosmopolitanism in Mohsin Hamid’s Exit West
candidates.abstract: This article’s distinct intervention is to theorize Mohsin Hamid’s Exit West as practicing speculative cosmopolitanism: a narrative method that couples the “autonomy of migration” with informal, care-based affiliations beyond the nation-state. Through a triangulated reading that brings together border-as-method, necropolitical governance, and urban informality with cosmopolitan ethics, the essay argues that the novel’s magical doors do not merely elide sovereignty; they operationalize migration as a world-making practice, reframing space as contingent and mobile. At the same time, Exit West reveals how racialized migrants are rendered hypervisible and disposable within securitized urban zones, particularly London’s fractured architectures of control, producing subjects through death, delay, and managed precarity. Turning from diagnosis to possibility, the article reads squatter communities and improvised collectives as speculative laboratories of postnational affiliation, where heterogeneous, precarious forms of cohabitation model relational ethics under scarcity. In this account, Exit West is not only a narrative of displacement but an experiment in world-making, an imaginative refusal of the carceral state and a fragile blueprint for shared futurity.

candidates.title: Covert Systems – On the Intelligence of Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: In light of recent developments in Artificial Intelligence, particularly the development of Large Language Models (LLMs), the question if machines can be said to think is examined. The problem was already addressed by Alan Turing in the 1950s, laying the groundwork for our argumentation. Our text refutes four common objections. Firstly, it challenges Ada Lovelace’s claim that computers are incapable of creating truly original content, demonstrating that neural networks, such as Transformer models, independently generate novel structures. Secondly, the assertion that LLMs merely statistically predict the next word is discussed. They are shown to be capable of constructing compressed internal representations from their input data through nonlinear operations, distinguishing them from statistical models. A third argument concerns AI’s lack of sensory access to the world. However, as Turing has demonstrated, the development of mental capabilities requires only communication between a teacher and a student, and sensory experience can be technically replicated at any time. The Chinese Room thought experiment, which suggests that algorithms merely simulate intelligence through formal symbol manipulation, is already anticipated by the Turing Test, which posits that any machine successfully feigning mental functions should be deemed to possess them. The text explores how LLMs generate a perfect compression of their input data, resulting in an accurate model of the world, a convincing simulation of human intelligence, and mastery of language. It discusses the phenomenon of “emergence”, the appearance of higher-order cognitive capabilities with increasing amounts of training data. Although the successes in implementing intelligence are notable, the neural network methodology employed results in the enigmaticity of the underlying basis, failing to illuminate the true nature of the mind as originally hoped. This obscurity was already evident in the foundational works of Kurt Gödel and Alan Turing, highlighting the complexities inherent in understanding human and machine intelligence alike.

candidates.title: Social Navigation for Tour-guide Robot
candidates.abstract: We propose a force-based model for social navigation of a tour-guide robot. Social forces due to various factors like obstacles, user position and heading, have been accounted for in the model. We claim that each one of these forces makes the robot more sociable to the user and we design an experimental setup for evaluation. In the experiment, the user follows an autonomous robot to a destination in a known map, while undertaking a few simple sub-tasks in the middle, which serve as distractions. For each participant, we run several rounds of the experiment, each with different forces and a shortest path, A*-search baseline model. Using per-round subjective indicators, we propose to study the effect of our force model on constructs such as: follow-ability, perceived safety, and perceived intelligence.

candidates.title: Mobile Robot Retrofit for the ROS2 Framework
candidates.abstract: This article presents the retrofit of a TurtleBot2i mobile robotic platform to support the ROS2 framework. The motivation for this migration lies on the discontinuation of ROS1 and the growing need for educational and research platforms to align with current technologies. The retrofit process encompassed both hardware and software adaptations: the robot was upgraded with a new power system and additional sensors, including a Velodyne LiDAR and an Intel RealSense camera, while its software environment was updated to Ubuntu 22.04 and ROS2 Humble, with the robot model and drivers adapted to ensure full integration. The results confirm the platform’s compatibility with the ROS2 ecosystem, enabling advanced perception and SLAM algorithms. These improvements enhance the applicability of the TurtleBot2i in educational and research contexts, ensuring its continued relevance in mobile robotics development.

candidates.title: Priced Guidance: Can Language Models Generate Future Research Ideas?
candidates.abstract: We evaluate language models' capability to generate novel research ideas through the lens of compression. We aim to lower-bound the potentially tiny probability that a language model generates the essence of a future research idea without any hints. Rather than estimate this probability through expensive repeated sampling, our Priced Guidance framework measures the compression cost: how many additional bits of information are needed to guide the model to recover the target idea. We prove that if the model can recover the target idea with at most K bits of guidance in expectation, then it can generate the idea without any guidance with probability at least $2^{-K}$. In our framework, the language model, called the generator, can pose a sequence of multiple-choice questions and specify a probability distribution over possible answers. A guide, which is a language model with access to the target idea, selects answers. If a selected answer has prior probability p, the generator pays $-\log_2 p$ bits. The generator aims to produce an idea that matches the essence of the target idea with minimal cumulative cost. This cumulative cost equals, up to an additive constant, the number of bits of information sent by the guide. Using this methodology, we evaluate five generator LLMs (Opus 5, Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, and GLM 5.3) on the core ideas in 87 recent high-quality deep learning papers and we use LLM as judge to determine whether the generated idea matches the target in terms of the central research object and defining mechanism. Fable 5.1 achieves the lowest median compression cost at 69.9 bits, substantially lower than gzip's median of 5,712 bits for losslessly compressing the summary of the target idea. A uniform ensemble of Fable 5.1, Opus 5, and Astra further reduces the median compression cost to 55.8 bits and improves the generation probability lower bound by 18,000 times.

candidates.title: Perioperative management and challenges of robotic-assisted surgery: a narrative review
candidates.abstract: Over the past two decades, robotic surgical technology has become increasingly widespread worldwide. RAS (robotic-assisted surgery) has attracted surgeons across various specialties with its advantages of high precision, a shorter learning curve, and reduced postoperative pain, while also imposing new requirements on the entire surgical team, including anesthesiologists. The physiological changes and unique complications associated with RAS have brought major challenges for anesthesiologists, who should respond rapidly to patient responses throughout the entire procedure.This review focuses on the potential issues encountered in the perioperative management of RAS, as well as the application of RAS across several specialties and the specific intraoperative management challenges involved.

candidates.title: Lightweight and Resource-Efficient Perception for Robotic Guide Dogs
candidates.abstract: Robotic guide dogs should understand their surroundings, objects, and potential risks. Prior research has focused on raw sensor data from cameras and 2D or 3D LiDAR, which precisely measure distance points rather than provide a semantic understanding of the scene. While these physical measurements are effective for robot-centric collision avoidance and robot safety, they are not suitable for human-centric guidance. The system should recognize the type and relevance of obstacles and explain them, clearly and actionably, in terms of their spatial relation to the user. We present complete on-device perception modules that fuse a 360 camera and a 2D LiDAR for reliable collision avoidance, with moving-object detection and tracking for human-centric guidance. Finally, in walking-impossible situations, a vision--language model delivers pathway explanations as a safety mechanism to reduce user anxiety. In experiments, verification of fused 360 camera--LiDAR depth shows reliable near-range perception but inherent mid-range bias, while the system as a whole sustained real-time performance under 55 W. On the real-world egocentric GuideDogQA benchmark, our system achieved 83.8\% accuracy, compared with 67.1\% for GPT-4o. These results demonstrate that practical human-centric guidance with real-time on-device inference is feasible even on quadrupeds.

candidates.title: 16-bit Precision of Convolutional Neural Networks on Microcontroller Units for 8-bit Costs
candidates.abstract: To deploy deep neural networks on edge hardware, highly efficient inference schemes are necessary that retain high accuracy. This work presents W16A16, a high precision (16-bit), fast speed, low energy quantization method. On a widely applied microcontroller architecture Armv7E-M, our proposed approach achieves faster speed and lower energy consumption on layer- and model-level compared to alternative quantization schemes. We analyze the architecture of Armv7E-M, explain the underlying principles behind the performance advantages of 16-bit approaches, and evaluate the empiric quantization errors for regression and classification tasks, as well as empiric time- and energy consumption in MCU deployment. We observe ca.\ 10 times lower quantization errors compared to 8-bit quantization schemes while achieving similar or better inference times and energy consumption.

candidates.title: Standardized benthic imaging with small, modular ROVs: an open-source framework developed in temperate kelp forests
candidates.abstract: Abstract Kelp forests support ecologically, commercially, and culturally important species, yet their benthic communities remain difficult to monitor consistently across space and time. Scientific SCUBA surveys provide valuable observations but can be constrained by safety, bottom time, depth, and the spatial extent that divers can efficiently cover, motivating complementary approaches for collecting standardized benthic imagery. We developed and field-tested a standardized, open-source framework for benthic visual-imaging surveys using a small, modular remotely operated vehicle (ROV). Across four costscalable hardware configurations, we integrated navigation sensors, custom BlueOS Extensions, and our surftrak contribution to ArduSub, which enables fixed-altitude flight above the seafloor, and developed two open-source desktop applications that streamline field operations (rov flight ops) and imagery processing (rov imagery processing). We also evaluated power supplies, benthic lighting, camera settings, field protocols, and telemetryprocessing workflows over 303 transects conducted on 64 survey days from 2022 to 2026. The ROV operated across soft-sediment and rocky habitats, currents of 0–3 kt, and underwater visibility of 0–10 m. surftrak held the ROV within ± 0.2 m of its target altitude for 96% of 21 h of survey transects, producing an approximately 1 m 2 standardized image footprint. Sufficient illumination and optimized camera settings yielded high-resolution imagery in visibility below 2 m, while topside power increased endurance and operational flexibility. Combining Doppler velocity log and underwater acoustic positioning data through the vehicle’s extended Kalman filter improved navigation and post hoc transect reconstruction. During 2026 surveys, rov flight ops and rov imagery processing automated flight logging, log retrieval, fault diagnosis, and the sorting, development, and telemetry annotation of survey imagery. Dense kelp canopies nevertheless constrained vehicle operation, and downward-facing imagery provided limited observations of cryptic or obscured organisms. We provide configuration-specific bills of materials, hardware and wiring documentation, software and firmware inventories, camera settings, open-source field and imagery-processing software, step-by-step field protocols, and pre- and post-dive checklists to support replication and adaptation of the framework. Together, these resources provide a field-tested starting point for expanding standardized benthic imaging while complementing diver surveys across kelp forests and other shallow coastal ecosystems.

candidates.title: A Modular Open-Source Augmented Reality Drone Environment for Human–Drone Interaction Research
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a modular open-source augmented reality (AR) environment for safe, repeatable, and extensible Human-Drone Interaction research. Developed in Unity for the Meta Quest 3, the system renders a virtual drone in the user’s physical surroundings using passthrough AR. It supports configurable three-dimensional approach trajectories, randomized trial sequences, spatial audio, experimenter-controlled stopping, safety constraints, and automatic logging of stopping distances. Experimental parameters can be adjusted through the Unity Inspector, enabling researchers to change key experimental parameters, such as drone model and trajectories, without restructuring the system. Furthermore, researchers may choose to adopt any subset of components from the system, e.g. only the drone model or audio. By reducing the risks, variability, and development effort associated with physical-drone experiments, the environment provides a reusable foundation for controlled studies in human-drone research.

candidates.title: Collaboration dynamics for space technology: the case of Satellite Networked Open Ground Station
candidates.abstract: Introduction This paper explores the dynamics of open-source software collaboration for networked satellite ground stations. Building on open-source collaboration literature, it examines how these dynamics unfold in a distributed technological space infrastructure that combines software, hardware, and operational activity. It does so through the case of SatNOGS, a globally distributed crowd-sourced satellite ground-station network operated by the Libre Space Foundation. Methods To examine this empirically, we employ an exploratory mixed-methods research design that combines a quantitative strand, a Contribution Matrix (CM) mapping 148 contributors across 39 system elements, with a qualitative strand of eleven semi-directed interviews analyzed through the Framework Method. Results Findings indicate that SatNOGS software is organized around a modular collaboration structure, combining a large periphery dominated by single-element contributors (68.2%), with a small core of contributors responsible for much of the integration work. Interviews further reveal a distinctive group of paid and unpaid contributors, structured around specialist and generalist roles. Discussion Overall, SatNOGS is sustained through two coexisting modes of a dynamic collaboration: extreme modularity, which enables broad peripheral participation, and intertwined collaboration, which maintains system-wide coherence. This dynamic structure sustains the common project despite other governance-related challenges, i.e., contribution barriers or the lack of a shared roadmap.

candidates.title: The Spatial Morphology of Future History
candidates.abstract: Big History characterizes cosmic evolution as a sequence of thresholds where ordered systems—from stars to civilizations—harvest energy to maintain rising complexity. However, standard historical narratives typically terminate at the present, treating the future as a domain of pure uncertainty. This study proposes that while specific events are unpredictable, the morphological structure of civilization follows a trajectory shaped by the time-invariant constraints of its generalized environment. We introduce Computational Future Historiography (CFH) to map these structural tendencies. Integrating Non-equilibrium Thermodynamics, Network Science, and classical settlement theories, we argue that the Planetary Trap—driven by the rising maintenance costs of complexity—creates structural pressure for a phase transition toward spatial expansion. To model this trajectory, we apply a recursive Civilizational Expansion Cycle (Node-Edge-Hub-Network), which manifests distinct morphologies across cosmological scales due to a shifting Triarchy of Constraints: the depth of gravity wells (Energy), the limits of hardware durability (Matter), and the finite speed of light (Information). At the Solar System scale, the Energy constraint dictates a highly centralized, monocentric structure (Fortress Sol), organizing a dependent industrial periphery around a kinematically calculated Dynamic Heartland in the Mars-Asteroid corridor. As expansion reaches the Local Stellar Neighborhood (R < 50 ly), the Matter constraint (hardware and biological attrition) triggers Logistical Symmetry Breaking, dissolving the monocentric hierarchy into a Polycentric Federation sustained by interstellar percolation via M-dwarf stepping stones. Finally, at the Galactic scale, the Information constraint (light-speed latency) imposes extreme temporal isolation, acting as an evolutionary filter that drives biological speciation and cognitive divergence. The expanding civilization transcends a unitary polity to become a diverse Galactic Neural Network, bound not by synchronous political control, but by the asynchronous exchange of invariant knowledge. This research posits that the future is not a random accumulation of events, but a constrained morphological adaptation to the unforgiving geometry of our cosmic environment.

candidates.title: Abel: Integrating Large Language Models into the Cognitive Architecture of a Hyper-Realistic Humanoid for Natural Social Interaction
OpenRUA: Robot-Use Agents Are Zero-Shot Visuomotor Policies
candidates.abstract: Coding agents are extending their reach into the physical world by writing and executing robot control programs. One might expect the agents to use the existing mature software stack that engineers have developed over decades to access sensors and control motion. Yet prior work primarily engineers complex custom harnesses to orchestrate agents for robot use, particularly by prescribing specialized workflows and providing bespoke interfaces. This raises the question: "Is such additional harness engineering necessary?" We introduce OpenRUA, a zero-abstraction harness that bypasses bespoke abstraction layers by providing off-the-shelf coding agents with only terminal access to the robot's native software interface ROS 2. OpenRUA employs a minimalist workspace-as-harness design, only offering ROS 2 documentation and basic tools while leaving the coding agent to organize its own work without orchestrating any agentic workflow. Within this workspace, OpenRUA recasts perception as file I/O and manipulation as coding. With Claude Code powered by Claude Opus 5, OpenRUA achieves success rates of 99.0% on CaP-Bench and 87.0% on LIBERO-PRO, demonstrating that an off-the-shelf coding agent can serve as a zero-shot visuomotor policy through the robot's native interface, without bespoke primitives or task-specific training. Under this minimalist design, further analysis reveals striking emergent behaviors of coding agents: (1) For perception, the agent spontaneously writes programs that process raw sensory inputs and derive metric measurements in 96.80% of episodes. (2) For manipulation, the agent spontaneously builds motion-control clients (e.g., gripper control) in 95.87% of episodes and closed-loop control programs (e.g., adjusting motion based on sensor feedback) in 50.13% of episodes. Our code is available at https://github.com/terminalworld/OpenRUA.

candidates.title: V-DART: VR-Based Dual-Arm Robot Teleoperation with Mobile Base Control and Data Recording
candidates.abstract: We present V-DART (VR-based Dual-Arm Robot Teleoperation), an extended virtual reality framework for the teleoperation of mobile dual-arm robotic systems, building upon our previous work on stationary manipulator control. The enhanced system leverages Unreal Engine 5.6.1 (UE5) for real-time visualization and interaction, introducing critical advancements for complex environments: the control of the robot's base movement via both joystick input and direct mapping of the user's physical position and orientation within the tracked space. This allows users to navigate the robot intuitively by simply moving their body, while maintaining precise control over both arms using VR (Virtual Reality) controllers. Furthermore, we introduce a robust data logging layer that records expert movements during teleoperation tasks. By capturing timestamped streams of user pose, controller inputs, and robot states that can be synchronized downstream, this module facilitates the creation of high-quality datasets from expert demonstrations. These datasets can be leveraged for machine learning applications, such as behavior cloning, reducing the need for extensive manual annotation. The system maintains bidirectional communication between the VR interface and the physical robot, ensuring responsive control and real-time feedback. We describe the architectural enhancements, user interaction design, and performance evaluation, demonstrating the viability of this unified approach for both teleoperation and data-driven robotics development.

candidates.title: APTree: Extended behavior trees for adaptive and scalable automated robotic task planning in construction
candidates.abstract: Task planning for robots in off-site construction prefabrication is primarily manual, leading to planning inefficiencies and reluctance to adopt robotic solutions. Existing approaches provide limited support for scalable, modular automated task planning and localized runtime replanning. This paper proposes APTree, a model-driven framework that integrates automated task planning with modular task execution using behavior trees as the execution model. APTree repeatedly applies and coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners to automatically generate and compose modular task plans at runtime. To support this approach, we develop a domain-specific language for the formal specification and validation of task plans, together with a compatible execution engine. We evaluate APTree on the real-world livMatS Biomimetic Shell pavilion, where it models the construction robotic fabrication domain, detects injected specification and planning errors at design time and runtime, and automatically generates large-scale task plans by coordinating three symbolic planners across numerous planning modules. A machine-checked formal analysis further shows that composed execution and local replanning are safe under explicitly stated assumptions, including planner soundness and non-interference of generated plans, providing practitioners with explicit conditions for dependable plan composition. APTree thus enables construction practitioners to leverage automated task planning without requiring detailed knowledge of symbolic planning techniques or APTree’s internal implementation.

candidates.title: Supporting adolescent mothers using Video Interaction Guidance (VIG)
candidates.abstract: Children of adolescent mothers may be more likely to have negative developmental outcomes, which may be mediated by socio-demographic factors and lower levels of maternal sensitivity. In order to support adolescent mothers and the outcomes of their children, there is some evidence to suggest that video feedback interventions may be effective in enhancing maternal sensitivity. However, Video Interaction Guidance (VIG) has not yet been used with an adolescent sample within the UK. This research used a mixed method design to explore whether VIG enhanced attuned interactions and maternal sensitivity in adolescent mothers. The adolescent mothers’ experiences of VIG as an intervention were also explored using semi-structured interviews. Three adolescent mothers aged 17-18 and their children aged five to 18 months old, were recruited from an organisation that supports adolescent mothers to stay in education. All participants completed three cycles of the VIG intervention and a post-intervention interview. The total number of attuned interactions for all three adolescent mothers increased, however the increase was not statistically significant. Differences in maternal sensitivity after Cycle three were also not statistically significant however one participant’s score increased from medium to high sensitivity. The two other participants’ scores indicated a decrease in sensitivity but remained within the high sensitivity range. Qualitative findings suggest that VIG was a positive and feasible experience for adolescent mothers as it provided an opportunity to learn about their relationship with their child and may have empowered and increased their confidence as adolescent mothers. Implications for Educational Psychology practice and future recommendations for research are discussed.

candidates.title: Multi Robot Coordination For Swarm Robotics
candidates.abstract: Swarm robotics leverages the collective behavior of decentralized, self-organized systems to perform tasks that are too complex or time-consuming for a single autonomous agent. This project presents a framework for multi-robot coordination utilizing a robust master-slave architecture to ensure synchronized movement and task execution. At the core of each robotic unit is a PIC microcontroller, selected for its efficient processing capabilities, real-time control, and seamless integration with peripheral hardware. To achieve dynamic collaboration, the system relies on Radio Frequency (RF) communication to establish a reliable, low-latency network between the master controller and the slave robots. The master robot is responsible for processing high-level objectives and broadcasting precise navigational commands via RF modules. The slave robots receive these signals and drive their DC motors accordingly to maintain formation and execute localized movements. The embedded control logic and communication protocols are developed using C programming within the MPLAB environment, ensuring highly optimized, hardware-level execution. This coordinated approach demonstrates a scalable and fault-tolerant method for robotic collaboration, offering significant potential for real-world applications such as automated environmental exploration, search and rescue operations in hazardous environments, and decentralized industrial automation.

candidates.title: Testing ChatGPT in Music Promotion: Assessing AI Efficiency Compared to Industry Standards
candidates.abstract: Abstract ChatGPT is now an everyday topic, attracting the interest of the general public, researchers and specialists interested in exploring its capabilities. In the music industry, although artificial intelligence (AI) already has known uses, there is a lack of analysis of how chatbots can help promotional efforts. This research performs a comparative content analysis on AI-generated texts, using several music promotion prompts, to evaluate the success and efficiency with which ChatGPT offers advice on promoting artists. It examines promotion tools, more specifically artist websites, social media and video content, through the lens of efficiency criteria from specialised literature. This study asks whether ChatGPT can generate music-promotion strategies for artist websites, social media and video content that meet literature-derived efficiency criteria and how consistent these outputs are across repeated runs. The results suggest that ChatGPT does not consistently meet every efficiency criterion imposed by the industry, but it can serve as a useful starting point. Inconsistent results raise questions regarding the reliability and practical implications of AI for artists navigating an increasingly competitive industry. One of the solutions this paper suggests for generating efficient and comprehensive information is for the user to enter several detailed prompts and refine them progressively. Moreover, the present results encourage users to pass the AI outputs through the filter of industry professionals or specialised resources. These results show how important it is to understand how ChatGPT processes and delivers information and music promotion strategies, offering a fertile ground for further research through the obtained data, the prompt efficiency suggestions and the novel tools it provides.

candidates.title: A scoping review of disability representation in engineering design education
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Design engineering coursework often includes projects that address marginalized communities, such as the disability community, and the design experience and associated curricula can impact engineering students' perspectives on user‐engaged design practices. Purpose To understand the representation of the disability community in design engineering courses, this review asks: (1) How is disability presented and discussed in course‐based engineering design projects? and (2) How is the disability community represented and involved in these projects? Scope/Method This scoping review identified conference papers and journal articles in engineering education venues that analyzed the outcomes from course‐based engineering design projects. Articles involved designing for disability and included at least one engineering design phase. Results Of the 521 articles screened, 72 articles met the review criteria. Designing for the disability community was described most as service‐based learning (30.6%) and was conducted with undergraduate students in 98% of studies. Disabled individuals had no specified involvement in the design process in 52.8% of studies. Additionally, over half (52.8%) of studies did not report actionable steps for the final product of the course‐based project. Only four of the 72 studies reported that course curricula included education on disability rights or disability studies. Conclusions Students and faculty are pursuing course‐based engineering design projects that attempt to support the disability community but have varying success in directly involving disabled individuals and translating the final product for the community's benefit.

candidates.title: Environmental and economic assessment of an embedded photonic sensor system for composite manufacturing monitoring
candidates.abstract: The increasing use of embedded sensing technologies in composite manufacturing requires assessment of their economic and environmental implications alongside their functional performance. This study presents an integrated environmental and economic assessment of a photonic-based embedded sensor system developed for real-time monitoring of composite manufacturing processes. The sensor enables in situ monitoring of key process parameters during sensor manufacturing. A combined life cycle costing (LCC) and life cycle assessment (LCA) framework was developed to evaluate the sensor system during prototype fabrication and industrial scale-up. The economic assessment employed a hybrid bottom-up and activity-based costing approach, while the environmental assessment was conducted using GaBi software in accordance with ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 standards. The results identified labour-intensive assembly and post-processing stages as the dominant cost contributors, while PIC fabrication and post-processing showed the highest environmental impact and energy demand. The study further demonstrates that production cost and commercial viability are strongly influenced by learning curve behaviour, labour rates, and automation strategies. Opportunities for reducing environmental impact through process optimisation and scalable production are also identified. Overall, the work provides a framework for assessing the scalability, economic feasibility, and environmental performance of emerging photonic sensing technologies for composite manufacturing applications.

candidates.title: Open-Source Multi-Wire SPI Readout for Wearable Ultrasound Probes
candidates.abstract: Wearable ultrasound probes must transfer increasingly large acquisition payloads while maintaining compact, low-power electronics. In TinyProbe, the current bottleneck in data transfer occurs between the acquisition FPGA and the wireless system controller. This work presents an open-source, multi-wire SPI readout interface that uses serial command and address phases followed by a build-time-selectable dual- or quad-lane payload phase that is intended to address this bottleneck by increasing the potential bandwidth over the wifi limit while retaining compatibility with the Microcontroller-centric wearable US architecture. The interface emulates a serial flash memory, enabling compatibility with a broad range of microcontroller families and their existing peripheral interfaces. On the FPGA, the data path connects the existing acquisition FIFOs to the SPI interface through clock-domain crossing, sample reshaping, and packing into 32-bit words. Dual-SPI readout is integrated into the existing IGLOO2/SiWG917 TinyProbe architecture and verified at an SCLK frequency of 5 MHz. A separate Kria K26 testbed is used to characterize the FPGA SPI interface independently of the acquisition and wireless subsystems, demonstrating error-free transfers at SCLK frequencies up to 66 MHz. These measurements identify the SiWG917 multi-lane SPI implementation as the next bandwidth-limiting component and motivate a future upgrade of the system controller. The HDL and MCU implementations are released under a permissive open-source license.

candidates.title: Navigating Open Source Software Development in the Generative AI Era: Challenges and Opportunities for Project Communities
candidates.abstract: It is difficult to overstate the impact of generative AI on software engineering. In the report Navigating Open Source Software Development in the Generative AI Era, LF Research, Red Hat, Futurewei, OpenSSF, and LF AI & Data investigate how AI tools are impacting open source development workflows, and how maintainers and developers are experiencing this shift. The findings reveal that 1 in 4 incoming pull requests are low-quality "AI slop," driving maintainer burnout to the #1 concern for large projects. Additionally, only 1 in 3 projects have formal AI contribution policies. However, developers harvest 19%–52% time savings using AI across tasks. Maintainers and contributors must transition from reactive management to clear AI governance and verification systems.

candidates.title: Widening the Authorial Bottleneck: Towards an Open-Source Model of Theatre
candidates.abstract: This article defines the concentration of attribution, authority, and ownership in the figure of the director as an authorial bottleneck.Twentieth-century collaborative practices began to widen this bottleneck, while the emergence of the network society created new possibilities for distributing theatrical resources across institutions and communities.Drawing on performance theory and commons-based peer production, the article develops an open-source model in which a production is understood as one attributable version within a continuing history of adaptation.The model distinguishes three interdependent layers: dramaturgical resources, institutional infrastructure, and ethical governance.
